NOVO LIFE MES PAS-X
ADMINISTRATOR GUIDE
NL-MES-AG-001  |  Version 0.1  |  12 Aug 2026

This document converts the issued lifecycle design into a controlled administrator training/reference structure. It deliberately omits executable production details. Site-specific runbooks, role permissions, parameters, commands, secrets, locators and screenshots require approved baseline verification before activation.

The Administrator Guide defines the evidence-led control model for privileged support of the fictional Novo Life MES PAS-X solution. It distinguishes human privileged access, non-human identities, configuration/change, service/job/interface administration, monitoring/logs, backup/recovery, security and incident support. It complements NL-MES-UG-001 and NL-MES-OMSOP-001.

Identifiers and labels are DUMMY/conceptual. 'Approved' means approved through the separately controlled lifecycle process; it never means approval inferred from this guide. Each task requires EVID-AG evidence. STOP means preserve state, do not repeat or improvise, and route through the controlled escalation path.

Development, validation/test, training and production-like contexts must remain distinguishable and separately authorised. Data, roles, secrets, packages, job schedules, interfaces and evidence cannot be copied across environments without an approved change and data/security assessment. This guide defines no live environment identifiers.

The accountable System Owner remains ultimately responsible even where administrative activities are delegated. Delegations, supplier/provider splits and designated approvers must be documented. Criticality and residual-risk acceptance cannot be delegated. Administrators implement only authorised tasks and cannot convert technical success into release, risk acceptance or regulated resume.

An administrator must have role-specific curriculum, practical assessment, approved unique personal privileged access, applicable technical competence, current runbooks and acknowledged evidence/incident/change responsibilities before work. The future NL-MES-TRN-001 must link training result to role/access. Completion of this DUMMY guide grants no access.

Every privileged task follows: authorise -> identify -> assess/segregate -> capture before-state -> execute approved action -> capture result -> independently verify/reconcile -> decide rollback/escalation -> close session/access -> package evidence and hand over actions. A missing link blocks closure.

Use personal privileged accounts for privileged work and personal non-privileged accounts for ordinary work. Routine built-in/default/shared accounts are prohibited. Access is role-based, least privilege, environment-specific, training-linked, independently authorised/implemented, preferably time-limited, logged and reviewed.

Each non-human account must be distinguishable, linked to an approved technical purpose, have an accountable owner and credential custodian, be least privilege/non-interactive unless justified, and have rotation/review/retirement controls. Secrets are never stored in this guide, tickets, logs or scripts.

Security controls are risk-based, documented, securely implemented, monitored/tested and maintained. Administrators support implementation; they do not accept residual risk. Use approved secret-management and privileged-identity controls, protect admin workstations/sessions and report suspected compromise.

Administrator actions affecting roles, configuration, records, interfaces, services, jobs, reports, security or recovery must be time-aligned, attributable and protected. Logs relied on for review must be outside the administrator's alteration/deletion control. Signature configuration or evidence cannot be detached from its record, meaning, signer and time.

Configuration management covers planning, CI identification, approved baselines, change control, status accounting and configuration audit. Scope is risk-scaled but must allow exact component/version/environment/relationship understanding and recovery reproducibility.

Normal, standard and emergency changes follow the approved O&M/change process. The change defines impact/risk, approvals, package, target, prerequisites, verification, rollback and release/resume decision. 'Standard' does not mean uncontrolled; 'emergency' does not mean undocumented.
section: 9 Controlled change, promotion, rollback and maintenance

content: Starting, stopping, restarting or maintaining services requires an approved runbook and assessment of active batches, jobs, transactions, dependencies and evidence. Technical health alone is not regulated readiness.

Before enable/disable/rerun/replay/disposition, capture stable identifiers, last/current state, attempt/acknowledgement, downstream/source state and duplicate risk. One approved deterministic action is permitted; ad-hoc payload edit, status force, clearing history and blind repeat are prohibited.

Review approved signals for application, database, integration queues, scheduled jobs, storage, backup, security and capacity. Each signal/alert must retain component, condition, severity, authoritative time and diagnostic context. Proposed thresholds remain DUMMY until approved.

The approved DUMMY objectives are RPO 30 minutes, RTO 4 hours, WRT 2 hours and MTD 6 hours. The DUMMY exercise observed RPO 18 minutes, RTO 3 hours 06 minutes, WRT 1 hour 50 minutes and MTD 4 hours 56 minutes. These results do not authorise production restore/recovery/resume.

Administrators preserve service, configuration, version, log, transaction and record context under a stable case reference. Diagnostic or workaround actions that change regulated state require explicit authority and audit evidence. Chain of custody and restricted evidence access apply where needed.

Periodic administration reconciles complete populations against current approvals/baselines and records findings/actions without converting open risk into acceptance. The year wheel/frequencies and SLA are not yet approved. Appendix D lists 12 required check areas.

Administrator handover requires current roles/access and owners, environment/configuration baselines, runbooks, monitoring/log sources, jobs/interfaces, backup/recovery, security/patch/vulnerability/certificates/licences, support/SLA, knowledge base, scheduled checks, open cases/actions and training evidence. Missing evidence requires an owned action plan.
These task cards are conceptual control patterns. They may be activated only after site-specific released runbooks, training, access, SLA, handover and release evidence are approved.

Dummy document created for hackathon/training simulation only. Not valid for operational, regulatory, inspection, or GxP release use.

This Configuration Specification defines the required controlled configuration for the fictional Novo Life MES PAS-X implementation. It translates the approved 50-item URS/FS/DS chain into exactly 50 configuration items (CI-MES-001 through CI-MES-050), allocates all 60 approved integration requirements, and records how the existing 26 shared risks are addressed by configuration design.
The specification is deliberately product- and environment-neutral where the approved package has not selected a PAS-X release, operating system, database, middleware, endpoint, port, certificate, hardware size,

a PAS-X release, operating system, database, middleware, endpoint, port, certificate, hardware size, configuration tool, numeric limit, retention period, RPO/RTO or monitoring threshold. Each such item remains explicitly marked Verify. This preserves evidence integrity and prevents a planned setting from being mistaken for an implemented value.
Evidence boundary: 'required configuration' in this document means an approved simulated design requirement. It does not mean that DEV, TEST/VAL, PROD or DR has been configured, exported, compared, verified, released or accepted. Those evidence states r
DR has been configured, exported, compared, verified, released or accepted. Those evidence states remain open.

The purpose is to define the required configuration settings, parameter classes, configuration methods, dependencies, security controls and verification focus for the Novo Life MES PAS-X solution so that configured software components can support their approved intended use.

• Use as dummy audit/training evidence for how configuration requirements can be structured and traced.
• Use the Configuration Specification as design input to controlled build, environment establishment, verification planning and design review.
• Do not use as an operational instruction, production baseline, executed configuration record or GxP release authorization.

Planned → Authored → Reviewed → Approved design → Implemented in DEV → Promoted to TEST/VAL → Verified → Approved baseline → Promoted to PROD → Maintained/changed → Retired. This CS stops at Approved design in the dummy simulation; later states require contemporaneous evidence.
A CI-MES identifier represents a controlled configuration requirement. It is not a ServiceNow CMDB record, product object name, deployed value, test case or approval signature. Those identifiers remain distinct and must be linked when created.

Attributes are selected for configuration control based on business need, potential effect on product quality/patient safety/data integrity, likelihood of unintended change, ability to replace/manage the item separately and the need to rebuild, recover or maintain the solution. Relevant attributes remain documented even if automated CM monitoring is not selected.

No live password, token, private key or confidential endpoint is recorded. Secret material must be held in an approved secret-management service; this CS stores only the required reference, scope, owner and verification rule.

The following CI-MES population is cardinality-controlled and one-to-one with the approved DS/FS/URS chain. Every row defines a required configuration object/rule, method and verification focus; a value marked Verify is an open design input, not an approved default.

The Integration Specification remains the detailed technical/business contract authority. This allocation shows which CS controls must be instantiated when endpoints, protocols, ports, certificates, mappings, retries, queues and monitoring values are selected. All exact technical values remain Verify.

Author in DEV → peer/technical review → candidate manifest → controlled TEST/VAL import → configuration comparison → acceptance verification → approved baseline → authorised PROD promotion → production comparison/verification → release decision. A failure holds or rolls back to the last approved state; emergency configuration requires separate governance and post-change reconciliation.

• Use automated export/discovery/comparison where product and enterprise tooling support it; otherwise perform attributable manual comparison at the approved risk-based frequency.
• Treat unexplained misalignment as an incident/gap, protect affected regulated processing, assess impact and restore or approve a controlled change.
• Trigger configuration audit at lifecycle gates, after vendor intervention, after recovery, after relevant change, or when monitoring indicates possible drift.
• Retain comparison population, baseline version, result, exceptions, disposition and reviewer evidence.

Primary controlled references and their visible version/status information are listed in §2.1. The approved dummy lifecycle documents listed in §2.2 are the authoritative internal simulation registers for requirements, risks, design and integration. No external clause number is asserted beyond what is visible in those controlled sources.

MES PAS-X | Novo Life (fictional) | Lifecycle assurance assessment
Simulated Reviewed and Approved for Demo/Training Use Only.

This Data Integrity Assessment evaluates the design-stage controls for the fictional Novo Life MES PAS-X implementation across the complete GxP data lifecycle. It covers the creation, use, transfer, review, archive and potential destruction of electronic records; the associated metadata, audit trails and electronic signatures; and the system, interface, continuity and maintained-state controls needed to preserve content and meaning.
The assessment conservatively treats every in-scope GxP data set as Primary GxP data because an authoritative business classification has not been supplied. It map

t as Primary GxP data because an authoritative business classification has not been supplied. It maps the agreed data flows and record classes to exactly 50 URS, 50 FS, 50 DS, 50 configuration items, 60 integration requirements and the existing 26 shared risks. No new requirement or risk namespace is introduced.
Assessment conclusion: the package contains a coherent design basis for data integrity. This simulated approval accepts the assessment document as training evidence only. It does not confirm that controls are configured, effective, validated, operational, periodically reviewed, or acce
firm that controls are configured, effective, validated, operational, periodically reviewed, or acceptable for release. All 26 shared risks remain Open; residual risk is not rated or accepted.

The purpose of NL-MES-DIA-001 is to determine whether the approved design package identifies appropriate, risk-proportionate controls to keep GxP data complete, consistent, accurate, trustworthy, reliable, readable and retrievable throughout the intended lifecycle. The assessment also identifies evidence that must be produced before verification, release and maintained-state use.

MES application, database, integration and reporting components and their dependencies on enterprise identity, authoritative time, backup and monitoring services.
Electronic batch execution, EBR, master recipes/workflows, manual entries, calculations, equipment/material context, exceptions, signatures, audit trails, reports and exports.

risks, map controls to URS/FS/DS/CI/INT references and identify evidence still required.

For this simulation, the assessment plan, scope and conclusion are treated as reviewed and approved by fictional role holders. No individual identity or signature is represented. A real implementation must establish the accountable Data Owner, Data Integrity Steward, IT Solution Owner and QA approver in the controlled systems of record before any operational decision.

Conservative classification rule: because a business-approved Primary/Secondary determination has not been supplied, every in-scope GxP data set below is assessed as Primary. This is a protective working assumption, not a final business classification.

A complete record includes content needed to reconstruct the GxP activity plus associated metadata, audit trails, signatures, context and relationships.
Dynamic characteristics needed for intended use—such as search, filter, sort, drill-down, trend and reprocessing—must remain available or be formally assessed before migration/decommissioning.
A report or printout is not automatically the original record or a complete true copy; scope and metadata must be defined and verified.

record class, retention period, archive solution and destruction authority remain Verify for every record class.

Flow-map validation state: the map is a design-stage representation derived from the approved system/interface package. A real process walkthrough with Data Owner, users, IT SMEs and QA is still required to confirm every source, destination, manual handoff, copy, temporary store and archive path.

All ten principles have an explicit design route. None has objective implementation/effectiveness evidence in this design-stage package. The DIA therefore records a complete control design basis with open verification, rather than a claim that ALCOA++ compliance has been demonstrated.

Operational audit trails are required to be available and reviewable for all in-scope GxP data unless a controlled exclusion is justified. The later NL-MES-ATR-001 must determine which trail/log populations are reviewed, what reviewers look for, when/frequency, who performs an independent review, how it is executed and where evidence/findings are retained.
Review triggers include approval/release events, periodic risk-based cadence, investigations, abnormal patterns and as-needed review after relevant change or incident.
Reviewers must be independent of the data creator for the population unde

levant change or incident.
Reviewers must be independent of the data creator for the population under review and trained in the defined instruction.
The review must look for unexplained changes/deletions, critical-parameter changes, repeated activity, unusual times, omissions/orphan records, repeated tests, abnormal/outlier behavior and signs of manipulation.
Unexplained findings require controlled investigation/deviation handling; this DIA creates no incident or deviation ID.

Transfer rule: no automated or manual transfer is considered successful solely because a message/file was sent. Receipt, acceptance state, completeness, duplicate/sequence behavior, rejected/quarantined content and source-to-destination reconciliation must be objectively evidenced.

No retention duration, RPO, RTO, archive product, file format, legal-hold rule or destruction decision is invented in this DIA. Each requires an authoritative source and objective evidence before operational use.

Gate decision: Verification planning may proceed. Affected protocol approval or execution may proceed only after every mapped gate is closed in a later controlled record. This DRR does not close any gate.

A single fictional incident cannot establish a statistically or operationally meaningful trend. The record is categorized for future comparison, and its status/decisions are planned as input to NL-MES-ITPSE-001. Conditional follow-ups are not evidence that a real action is due.

MES PAS-X | Novo Life (fictional pharmaceutical organisation)

This protocol plans risk-based installation verification for the fictional Novo Life MES PAS-X implementation. It applies the plan-side structure of Q0697905 and the detailed protocol expectations of Q0300370, Q187219, Q0715589 and Q0697805. The design package is suitable for controlled verification planning with conditions; it is not yet suitable for IQ execution because product, architecture, interface, configuration, supplier and environment values remain open under PV-G1 through PV-G5.

The purpose of this protocol is to define how documented verification will demonstrate that the MES PAS-X solution, its supporting IT infrastructure and its environment-specific deployment are installed correctly and comply with the approved design. It establishes scope, responsibilities, prerequisites, planned cases, traceability, evidence rules, acceptance criteria, baselines and the later IQ reporting route.
The protocol may be used only to prepare the future DUMMY IQ Test Cases and IQ Report. Approval of this document records agreement with the plan; it is not evidence that any installatio
. Approval of this document records agreement with the plan; it is not evidence that any installation object exists or has passed verification.

The system is treated as GxP critical. The shared portfolio contains 49 Working High requirements and one Working Medium requirement; all 26 risks remain Open. IQ scope therefore uses formal, scripted, attributable verification with independent review for critical aspects. Detailed DUMMY scripts - design approved; execution not started

This controlled DUMMY artifact expands the 32 IQ cases approved for planning in NL-MES-IQP-001 into executable-design steps. It intentionally contains no execution result. The master requirements, risk and traceability populations are retained without creating or renumbering controlled records.

Purpose. Define repeatable installation-verification actions, expected results, objective-evidence requirements and unexecuted run fields for the fictional PAS-X installation. The scripts support later controlled execution in approved TEST/VAL and, where explicitly authorized, read-only pIV comparison.
Scope. Infrastructure, platform, application, configuration, interface components, security dependencies, monitoring, backup/restore readiness, records controls, baselines and handoff readiness described by NL-MES-IQP-001.
Out of scope. Operational or performance effectiveness, real production c

scribed by NL-MES-IQP-001.
Out of scope. Operational or performance effectiveness, real production changes, real credentials or data, release authorization and the 50 planned OV cases. Functional effectiveness remains in OV/PfV unless NL-MES-IQP-001 explicitly identifies a limited installation-health check.

The test-case data model and evidence design were derived from the accessible controlled guidance in the user-provided SharePoint source folder and from the 15-document DUMMY package baseline. Source documents are summarized; no live links or external operational identifiers are embedded.

Permitted controlled statuses from the accessible TIMS guidance are listed below. This artifact uses only No Run. Not Completed, Blocked and unqualified N/A are prohibited unless a later approved protocol or local procedure explicitly defines them.

All applicable blocking prerequisites must be closed with objective evidence before an official run. The register is reproduced from NL-MES-IQP-001; this IQTC does not change its state.
Baseline candidates are captured only during authorized execution. None is represented as established by this script design.

Each case starts on a new page. Step 1 establishes the approved context; Steps 2-6 implement the case-specific checks; Step 7 closes/transports the unexecuted record design. Every execution field remains No Run or N/A - no execution.

document_title: NOVOLIFE-MES-IRTR-IT Recovery Test Protocol and Report-v0.1-DUMMY.docx
content:
This combined protocol and report planned, executed and concluded one risk-based DUMMY verification of the IT recovery process defined in NL-MES-IRP-001 for the fictional Novo Life MES PAS-X solution. It demonstrates, within an isolated training scenario, the ability to follow the recovery sequence, restore representative components/data, reconcile dependencies, complete post-recovery checks and measure recovery objectives.
The protocol portion was frozen and simulated-approved before official DUMMY runs. The report portion records actual simulated results without rewriting the approved plan.

NL-MES-IS-001 converts the seven conceptual MES interface families into uniquely identified, verifiable integration requirements and logical data contracts. It addresses providers/consumers, message resources, inputs, mappings, outputs, identity and security, sequencing, acknowledgement, retry/replay, error/quarantine/reconciliation, monitoring, versioning, recovery and lifecycle ownership without inventing technology-specific values.

The purpose of this Integration Specification is to describe the planned functional and logical design of the interfaces by which MES PAS-X exchanges data or service state with ERP, LIMS, automation, historian/reporting, enterprise identity, authoritative time and operational services. Each integration requirement has a unique INT-MES-[IF]-### identifier and an objective acceptance focus.

Q0723783 is the closest approved integration design template and contains the minimum information needed to describe design, function and integrations. Because the seven in-scope exchanges may be APIs, messages, events or service integrations, its API-specific resource/URL fields are represented here as technology-neutral logical contracts and environment routing values. No template topic is omitted; non-applicable or unresolved technical values are explicitly Verify.

Each interface family retains the established -001 anchor and extends the same INT-MES-[IF]-### convention for detailed integration requirements. The family is described once; logical contracts and field groups are referenced rather than repeating the source URS/FS text. Detailed DS/CS items and test cases will link to these integration IDs.

Enterprise and plant services exchange logical contracts through CMP-MES-INT-001, which applies common authentication, schema/mapping, sequencing, acknowledgement, error, monitoring and reconciliation controls before CMP-MES-APP-001/CMP-MES-DB-001 use or publish the data. CMP-MES-REP-001 supports controlled reporting. CMP-ENT-IAM-001, CMP-ENT-TIME-001, CMP-ENT-BCK-001 and CMP-ENT-MON-001 provide cross-cutting identity, time, backup and monitoring services.

Define interface contracts independently from one consumer implementation and use stable business identities and versioned data models where feasible.
Distinguish interface requirements/specifications from coupled-system requirements; reference URS/FS rather than duplicating controlled requirement text.
Assess existing strategic interface-platform components, connectors and reusable services before custom development.
Document future consumer and version/deprecation implications in the interface terms of service and consumer inventory.

a retired version after the approved cut-off and verify all consumers have migrated before decommissioning.

The controlled source documents and package records listed in sections 1.4 and 2.1 are the references for this specification. A controlled technical schema or mapping workbook may be added later with its own identifier/version and trace.

Conclusion: NL-MES-IS-001 defines the logical integration baseline for all seven current MES interface families and assigns 60 detailed integration requirements with objective acceptance focus. The interface platform, technical contracts/mappings, environment values, security material, ownership agreements, design-review closure, verification results, operational controls and residual-risk acceptance remain open in the planned lifecycle.

NOVO LIFE
MES PAS-X Lifecycle Package
OPERATION AND MAINTENANCE SOP
NL-MES-OMSOP-001
Dummy document created for hackathon/training simulation only. Not valid for operational, regulatory, inspection, or GxP release use.

This SOP describes the future operation and maintenance of the fictional Novo Life MES PAS-X system. It defines system information and documentation, user management, risk management, suppliers and service providers, changes, configuration, maintenance, acceptance and release, periodic evaluation, monitoring, incidents and problems, backup/recovery, information security, routine operations, records and activation controls.
The instruction covers the MES application, database, integration, reporting, identity, time, backup and monitoring components and their fourteen operating dependencies. It

ing, identity, time, backup and monitoring components and their fourteen operating dependencies. It applies only after formal activation. Until then, each procedural step is a planned control for demo/training use, not an instruction to operate a real system.

After activation, this SOP applies to employees and authorised supplier/service-provider personnel who perform an activity defined here. The IT System Manager owns the instruction. IT Solution Owner, Business/Data Owner and QA perform only the specific governance, risk, release or escalation tasks assigned to them and therefore require training before those tasks are activated.

Novo Life MES PAS-X is a fictional GxP-critical manufacturing execution system intended to present approved instructions, control permitted workflow states, capture attributable execution data, support review and exchange controlled information with ERP, LIMS, automation, historian/reporting and enterprise services. It does not independently make final product-release decisions.

Authorised users interact with application services. The application persists configuration and regulated records in the database, exchanges messages through integration services and publishes controlled reports. Identity, time, backup and monitoring are enterprise prerequisites. All regulated execution remains held when identity, time, data integrity or active-context state is uncertain.

The IT Solution Owner shall ensure sufficient qualified resources and funding for system management. The Configuration Manager shall maintain CI identity, version, relationships, support horizon, license state and replacement/upgrade actions. Actual product, infrastructure and service values remain ACT-OMSOP-001 through -003.

GxP data, metadata, audit trails, electronic signatures and related approvals shall remain complete, readable, retrievable and protected for the approved retention period. Correction, deletion, archive, retrieval and controlled-copy activities require authorisation, attributable before/after evidence and impact verification. Actual retention schedules, personal-data scope and migration/initial-load applicability remain controlled activation decisions.

All provisioning, modification and revocation uses REC-OMSOP-006. Revoked/rejected access identified during review is investigated. Unauthorised privileged access is contained and recorded as an incident with GxP/data/security impact assessment.

Operations shall issue approved role-based communications for planned maintenance, degraded service, system unavailability, severe incident, new release, changed instruction and recovery status. Each communication records audience, approval, time, content, delivery route and acknowledgement where required. No real distribution list or contact channel is present in this DUMMY SOP.

Users route requests through the controlled service intake. The Service Desk records identity, affected service, symptoms, time, GxP/business impact and evidence; assigns category/priority; and escalates to functional, technical, supplier, security, QA or recovery roles as appropriate. Service targets remain open until NL-MES-SLA-001 is issued.

NL-MES-ITRA-001, NL-MES-ITRRA-001 and NL-MES-DIA-001 define the system, requirement and data-integrity risk bases. All 26 risks remain Open. Operating records may provide future effectiveness evidence, but no successful check or this document's approval creates a residual rating or acceptance.

Supplier Alpha remains conditionally fit for selection and planning only. Before any GxP-supporting service or access, the Supplier Manager and QA shall complete qualification, approve responsibilities and agreements, verify security/QMS/product evidence and establish reassessment, KPI, lifecycle-notice and phase-out controls. No supplier commitment is active in this SOP.

Internal providers for identity, time, network, compute, storage, backup, monitoring and service intake shall have an approved responsibility split, evidence obligations, escalation and performance review. Missing ownership or evidence requires safe hold or internal containment, not inferred service acceptance.

The Configuration Manager shall maintain the eight-component configuration baseline, attributes and fourteen dependencies; update the baseline through approved change; and perform quarterly and pre-release configuration audits. Interface agreements, actual topology and product values remain activation actions.

New functionality, configuration, fixes and upgrades require controlled requirements, risk, design/configuration, independent review, supplier/development evidence, verification, promotion and release records. Unsupported customisation and unassessed custom objects are prohibited.

The IT PSE shall evaluate continued validated state, regulatory and procedural compliance, fitness for intended use, changes/releases, incidents/problems, deviations, supplier/service performance, access review, security/vulnerabilities, backup/recovery, training, records, risks and actions. Until a documented risk assessment approves another interval, perform yearly; the interval shall never exceed three years.

Every incident is logged, categorised, prioritised, investigated, resolved and closed with service, business, GxP, data-integrity, security and personal-data impact considered. Critical, major or recurring incidents use problem management. Severe events require controlled command, communication, evidence preservation and QA/owner involvement. Recurrence, closure quality and overdue corrective actions are trended.

Backup and recovery follows NL-MES-IRP-001. Protected copies, job evidence, restore integrity, recovery point, role decisions, data/audit/signature checks, identity/time verification, interface reconciliation and release conditions are mandatory. NL-MES-IRTR-001 is evidence from an isolated simulation; it does not establish an active service cadence.

Information-security controls include least privilege, separate privileged identities, protected service accounts, monitoring/logging, malware and network protection, vulnerability and patch management, certificate/key/secret custody, time trust, supplier access and incident response. Applicable patches are mandatory unless a documented risk evaluation justifies a controlled exception. Application-layer and supplier responsibilities must be explicitly allocated.

Before regulated execution, the Operations Lead confirms application, database, integration, identity, time, backup and monitoring state; open incidents/changes; capacity; critical alerts; interface backlog; and the current approved release/baseline. Any unacceptable or uncertain item enters degraded mode or safe hold and is recorded.

Operations and Integration Support preserve stable transaction identity, batch/step/equipment context, timestamps, source authority, acknowledgements and checkpoints. Duplicates, stale/late data, mismatches and uncertain outcomes are quarantined. Replay requires approved scope, idempotency evidence, target-state confirmation and reconciliation; blind replay is prohibited.

Planned shutdown requires an approved change/window, communication, active-work disposition, queue/checkpoint capture, current backup evidence and authorised stop sequence. Restart verifies time, identity, configuration, data, queues, monitoring and critical function state before release from hold. Unplanned shutdown follows incident and, when applicable, recovery controls.

Issuing this SOP completes only the OMSOP deliverable portion of ACT-IREP-007. It does not close DUMMY-DRF-MES-007 because UG, AG, SLA, TRN, ownership/knowledge transfer, intended-use/production verification, residual-risk acceptance, VSR and G5/G6 decisions remain Open.

Every record shall be attributable, contemporaneous, complete, reviewed where required, linked to its source event/control and stored in an approved controlled repository. Retention periods expressed here are minimum control rules; the approved GxP, incident, security, agreement and data schedules govern when activated.

SERVICE LEVEL AGREEMENT
NL-MES-SLA-001  |  Version 0.1  |  12 Aug 2026

This SLA defines how the fictional service customer, service owner and service providers would coordinate support for Novo Life MES PAS-X. It specifies service towers, intake, priority, proposed targets, measurement, evidence, escalation, maintenance, continuity, supplier/provider review and improvement. It complements OMSOP, UG and AG; it does not supersede lifecycle, quality, security, continuity or release controls.

All times, percentages, windows, thresholds and cadences are proposed DUMMY planning values. 'Target' is an objective, not a guarantee. 'Restored' means the agreed service function is usable with verification; it may be a controlled workaround or permanent fix and must be labelled. 'Resolved' means underlying incident work is complete and closure evidence is accepted.

Service outcomes depend on enterprise identity/time, network, compute, database/storage, integration/middleware, ERP, LIMS, automation, historian/reporting, monitoring, backup and security services. A provider dependency does not remove the MES service obligation to detect, coordinate, communicate, preserve evidence and reconcile impact.

Service governance separates business impact input, priority/major-incident authority, tower delivery, technical implementation, independent Quality/security/recovery decisions, supplier oversight and accountable risk/release ownership. Delegations and provider responsibility splits require controlled evidence.

Priority is based on current known impact and urgency. It is not raised to obtain attention and not lowered because a workaround is expected to be quick. Workaround acceptability and factual severity changes determine reprioritisation. A potential Major/P1 is escalated immediately to the approved major-incident decision function.

Identify/log -> categorise -> assess impact/urgency -> prioritise -> investigate -> restore -> verify -> communicate -> close. Every incident retains stable ID, complete timeline, affected service/business context, priority rationale, actions, restoration type, evidence and unresolved follow-up. User/requester closure input cannot override Quality/security/data-impact requirements.

Major/P1 support is proposed 24x7. The major-incident function owns declaration/coordination, establishes the bridge and roles, allocates resources, sets communication cadence, coordinates providers/recovery and preserves decisions. Long events require sustainable round-the-clock staffing. Downgrade follows factual severity change and controlled decision.

Problem management is mandatory for Major/Critical cases as required by the NN guidance and may be used for recurrent/significant trends. Link incidents, root cause, known error/workaround, permanent corrective/preventive action, owner/date, verification and recurrence monitoring. Closing an incident does not close the problem.

A request clock begins only when required information, approvals, role/training and target environment are complete. If incomplete, the provider records exactly what is missing and retains the original received time; no silent rejection or clock reset.

Normal, standard and emergency changes follow the approved change/OMSOP/AG controls. The service model coordinates impact assessment, window, notice, user/provider communication, package/rollback, implementation, verification and service-state evidence. Standard does not mean uncontrolled; emergency does not remove documentation.

The proposed service monitors application, database, integration queues, scheduled jobs, storage/capacity, backup, security events, certificates/licences and key dependencies. Every event carries source, component, condition, severity, authoritative time and diagnostic context; thresholds remain Open until ACT-SLA-006.

Proposed availability = (eligible measured service-window minutes - unplanned unavailable minutes) / eligible measured service-window minutes x 100. Eligible minutes exclude only approved, correctly notified exclusions. Unavailable means the agreed core service cannot support its intended service function; material degradation is assessed and recorded rather than automatically ignored.

The integration tower supports ERP, LIMS, automation, historian/reporting and identity transactions. Interface terms of service must identify owner, consumers/providers, support model, monitoring/communication, SLOs and recoverability. Affected IT-system stakeholders are notified when an interface incident impacts their process.

The recovery service aligns with the IRP and business continuity model. Proposed plan targets are RPO 30 minutes, RTO 4 hours, WRT 2 hours and MTD 6 hours. The DUMMY exercise observed RPO 18 minutes, RTO 3 hours 06 minutes, WRT 1 hour 50 minutes and MTD 4 hours 56 minutes; observations do not establish production capability.

Security/privacy/data-integrity events may increase priority and always trigger the relevant controlled assessment. Providers use least privilege, protected logs, approved secret management and evidence retention. No direct database/file correction, audit manipulation, impersonation or deletion of regulated records is permitted.
section: 12 Security, privacy, data integrity and records

content: An exclusion is allowed only when defined, approved, evidenced and reported. Proposed availability exclusions are correctly approved/notified planned maintenance and separately approved closures. Provider/supplier failure, external dependency, capacity shortfall, missing staff, measurement gap, emergency maintenance and failed change are not automatically excluded.

Metric owner reconciles complete populations, duplicates, timestamps, priority changes, clock states, approved exclusions and missing data. Missing/weak evidence is non-compliant or Unknown - Open Action, never assumed compliant. Every breach records impact, cause, provider, correction/CAPA, owner/date and follow-up.

Communications state stable incident ID, service/business scope, current factual state, priority, impact, safe user action, restoration/workaround status, risks/unknowns, next update time and owner. Do not expose credentials, secrets, uncontrolled personal data or speculative root cause. Major/P1 communications continue at target cadence until downgraded/restored by controlled decision.

Proposed issue date is within 10 business days after month close. Report the measured window, data quality, availability, priority populations, response/restoration/update performance, incidents/problems, requests/access, changes/maintenance, interfaces, backup/recovery, security, supplier/provider KPIs, breaches/exclusions, open risks/actions and improvement status.

KPIs and responsibility splits must be formalised in approved agreements. Periodic re-evaluation uses agreed KPIs and is documented/retained. Supplier/provider misses are discussed in governance; material/repeated breach escalates to Service Owner, Sourcing and Quality, with root cause, dated recovery, CAPA/warning as appropriate. Supplier Alpha remains conditional for planning only.

Improvement inputs include breach, trend, repeat incident/problem, audit, supplier evaluation, recovery exercise, capacity, security, user feedback and periodic evaluation. Every action has stable ID, rationale, owner, due date, status and effectiveness check; it cannot silently alter SLA scope/targets.

This DUMMY version has no effective date or operational term. Future activation requires closure/approval of ACT-SLA-001..012, training, VSR, handover and production release. The effective version must identify parties, controlled contacts/queues, calendars, measurement sources, providers, target acceptance and review/expiry.

Any change to scope, tower, party, support window, priority, target, calculation, exclusion, provider, recovery objective, security/data obligation or governance cadence requires controlled impact/risk review, approval, versioning, communication and training assessment.

Provider transition/exit preserves service/record continuity, knowledge/runbooks, roles/access/secrets, configuration, monitoring/logs, incidents/problems/requests, supplier/CAPA, backup/recovery, metrics, risks/actions and retention. Missing items require an action plan and cannot be deemed handed over.
R = Responsible; A = Accountable; C = Consulted; I = Informed. This RACI is proposed and not effective.

This document defines the intended use, business context, scope, boundaries, logical and proposed physical arrangements, environments, components, prerequisites, interfaces, data flows, security measures and lifecycle ownership for a fictional new MES PAS-X implementation at Novo Life. It is the system-definition baseline for downstream user requirements, risk assessments, specifications, interface documents, verification and operational controls.

ecause planned MES functions create, process, approve, retain and exchange electronic manufacturing records used to execute and reconstruct regulated activities. The purpose of this System Overview and Description is to provide one maintained, human-readable definition of MES PAS-X sufficient to establish context for requirements, risk assessment, solution design, verification planning, release readiness and subsequent system management. MES PAS-X is intended to support controlled electronic execution and documentation of pharmaceutical manufacturing at Novo Life. The planned solution receives production orders and relevant master data, presents approved manufacturing instructions, guides authorised users through configured workflows, captures execution data and approvals contemporaneously, manages exceptions and electronic records, and exchanges manufacturing status and results with connected systems.

supporting complete and traceable electronic batch records and providing information for review and disposition activities. NOVO LIFE MES PAS-X
USER GUIDE
NL-MES-UG-001  |  Version 0.1  |  11 Aug 2026

This guide translates the issued URS/FS design intent into user-facing behaviours without claiming that a live PAS-X environment has been configured or verified. The conceptual labels below describe control zones, not an exact product screen. Site-specific labels, values, routes, messages, and screenshots must be verified and controlled before activation.

The purpose of this User Guide is to describe safe, attributable, role-based end-user interaction with the fictional Novo Life MES PAS-X solution. It supports future role training and operational handover preparation. It is not an Administrator Guide, configuration specification, validation report, production work instruction, or release record.

A user may perform an assigned task only after the role, training, access, environment, current guide, and local operating instruction are approved and active. Completion of this DUMMY guide does not grant access. The future training package must link curriculum, assessment, role, guide version, and access decision.

Use one unique identity and only the minimum role required for the assigned work. Never share credentials, reuse another user's session, approve your own work where segregation is required, or ask support to perform regulated actions under your identity. Unexpected privilege is a defect and must be reported.

Electronic entries and decisions must be attributable, legible/readable, contemporaneous, original or a verified true copy, accurate, complete, consistent, enduring, and available. Preserve metadata and chronology. Use controlled correction; never overwrite history. Appendix C contains the complete sixteen-rule user checklist.

Use TASK-UG-001 through TASK-UG-003 and TASK-UG-030. Confirm unique identity, correct role, environment, service state, and visible context. Lock the session when leaving the workstation and sign out at task end. Re-authentication for a signature is personal and cannot be delegated.

Use the conceptual zones in Â§1.4 and local released labels when available. Do not rely on browser history, uncontrolled bookmarks, memorised paths, or a prior user's context. The stable batch header must remain visible or rechecked before every data entry, correction, signature, review, and completion decision.

Follow TASK-UG-004 through TASK-UG-008. Verify one authorised order, valid master data, the effective instruction/recipe version, correct batch header, eligible material/equipment readiness, and no blocking condition. Select Start once and confirm the recorded transition.

Perform only the enabled current step. Read the instruction before acting; satisfy prerequisites; record the requested evidence; review the step summary; then complete once. Do not navigate directly to a future step or repeat a submitted action because the screen response is slow.

A validation message is a control, not an obstacle. For format/unit errors, recheck the true source and correct only an entry mistake. For a true out-of-range value, preserve the value and use the required exception/hold workflow. Never change precision or re-enter alternatives until one passes.

Follow TASK-UG-012 through TASK-UG-015. Identification and status are separate checks: first resolve the intended object, then confirm its eligibility for the exact batch and step. Verify identity, lot/equipment identifier, location, quantity/unit where applicable, release/availability, expiry, cleaning, maintenance, calibration, qualification, and hold indicators required by the instruction.

Use a hold when instructed or when continued execution may compromise safety, quality, data integrity, or deterministic state. Record a factual reason and maintain the safe state. Resume or termination requires the configured authority, review of current physical and electronic state, disposition of open items, and a recorded transition.

Create the exception from the affected batch/step/record wherever possible. Describe the observed condition, when it occurred, immediate safe action, and linked material/equipment/interface context. Do not speculate, assign blame, include credentials, or omit inconvenient facts.

A signature is a personal regulated action. Read the exact meaning and confirm the affected record, batch/step, outcome, identity, and displayed statement immediately before re-authentication. Cancel if the context changes or the meaning is inaccurate. Never sign for another person or disclose credentials.

Authorised reviewers may search by record, batch, object, actor, event type, and time range within approved scope. Review prior/new values, reason, actor, time, signature linkage, and chronology. Preserve the search criteria and population used for a recorded review outcome.

The fictional solution exchanges orders/master data and confirmations with ERP, sample/result status with LIMS, commands/measurements with automation, publication/reporting data with the historian/reporting service, and identity outcomes with the enterprise identity service. Users interact only with the controlled status presented in MES; they do not repair payloads or replay queues.

Before completing a step, review values, material/equipment evidence, exceptions, corrections, and signatures. Complete once only when the control is enabled and the expected state transition is shown.

Use the completion-readiness view. Every mandatory step, value, review, signature, and blocking exception must be satisfied. Resolve each blocker at its source; never request suppression or repeated submission.

Review a stable record version and a reproducible population. Production review focuses on execution completeness and operational evidence; Quality review focuses on exceptions, corrections, signatures, audit evidence, dispositions, and blockers. Segregation must be respected.

Use only approved reports/views. Preserve selected criteria, as-of time, record version, source/provenance, unresolved-data indicators, and controlled-copy status. Reconcile key identifiers/totals to the source record and store/distribute only through the approved process.

The approved recovery plan target is RPO 30 minutes, RTO 4 hours, WRT 2 hours, and MTD 6 hours. The DUMMY test observed RPO 18 minutes, RTO 3 hours 06 minutes, WRT 1 hour 50 minutes, and MTD 4 hours 56 minutes. These results do not authorise production recovery or resume; DUMMY-DRF-MES-007 and ACT-IREP-007 remain Open.

Use the controlled support channel defined in the future SLA/local instruction. This DUMMY guide intentionally contains no real contact details. Report early when safety, quality, identity, time, record persistence, signature, interface, or duplicate-processing risk is possible.
If a case reference is returned, link it to the affected exception/record without inventing or modifying the identifier. A workaround that changes regulated state requires explicit authorisation and audit evidence; support intake cannot grant that authority.

Use only approved devices, entry points, networks, roles, report destinations, and support routes. Protect screens and outputs from unauthorised viewing. Use the minimum personal data required; never place credentials or secrets in free text. Report suspected inappropriate access or disclosure immediately.

This issue fills sequence 25, NL-MES-UG-001. NL-MES-AG-001, NL-MES-SLA-001, NL-MES-TRN-001, and NL-MES-VSR-001 remain open. Operation and Maintenance, recovery, implementation reporting, risk, and verification documents retain their existing DUMMY conclusions; this guide does not supersede them.
Apply these task cards only after formal activation and site-specific verification. The card sequence supports training design; it is not an instruction to enter a live system now.
section: Appendix A — Thirty end-user task cards

content:
Steps
1. Complete the assigned curriculum and role assessment.
2. Confirm the requested role matches current duties and least privilege.
3. Use only the unique identity provisioned through the approved access process.
4. Read the current User Guide and applicable local instruction before use.
section: TASK-UG-001 | Complete training and obtain access

content:
Steps
1. Open the approved MES entry point identified by local controlled instruction.
2. Authenticate using your own credentials.
3. Confirm the displayed identity, role, and environment before continuing.
4. Acknowledge any authorised service notice.

Steps
1. Confirm your displayed role supports the intended task.
2. Confirm site/area and environment are the authorised context.
3. Check that date/time and session state appear reasonable.
4. Lock or sign out whenever you leave the workstation.
section: TASK-UG-003 | Verify role and session context

content:
Steps
1. Open the work queue.
2. Apply only authorised filters for area, status, or assignment.
3. Check the as-of/refresh indication and unresolved-data indicator.
4. Identify the intended order without changing its state.

Steps
1. Compare order identifier and product/context with the approved work assignment.
2. Confirm the order state is executable.
3. Confirm required master-data checks show acceptable status.
4. Select the order once; wait for a deterministic response.

Steps
1. Read the instruction/recipe identifier and version.
2. Confirm the status is effective for the selected order and time.
3. Compare the displayed instruction to the authorised execution context.
4. Do not rely on an uncontrolled printout or memory.

Steps
1. Confirm batch/order identifier, product/process context, site/area, and current step.
2. Confirm the displayed actor/role and state.
3. Check that no unresolved warning changes the intended action.
4. State the context aloud or use an independent comparison where the local procedure requires it.
section: TASK-UG-007 | Verify the batch header and context

content:
Steps
1. Review the start-readiness summary.
2. Resolve each required prerequisite through its controlled workflow.
3. Select Start only when the control is enabled.
4. Confirm the transition and authoritative timestamp.

Steps
1. Read the prompt, expected unit, format, and source.
2. Observe or obtain the value at the time of the activity.
3. Enter the value once and verify transcription before submission.
4. Confirm the accepted value, unit, source/context, actor, and time.

Steps
1. Confirm all inputs and units belong to the current step.
2. Review the calculation rule/version if displayed.
3. Compare the result and validation outcome with the instruction.
4. Submit only when the inputs and result are coherent.
section: TASK-UG-010 | Record or verify a calculation

content:
Steps
1. Read the exact message and identify the affected field.
2. Recheck source, value, unit, decimal/format, and context.
3. Correct a genuine entry error through the prompted path.
4. If the source value is truly out of range, create the required exception instead of changing it.
section: TASK-UG-011 | Resolve a format, unit, range, or mandatory-field check

content:
Steps
1. Scan or enter the authorised material identifier once.
2. Confirm material name, batch/lot, quantity/unit, and intended step.
3. Check that the identifier resolves without ambiguity.
4. Continue only after identity and context agree.

Steps
1. Confirm release/availability status and expiry or use-by information where applicable.
2. Confirm required storage/handling status and quantity.
3. Compare site/area and product applicability.
4. Accept only the configured eligible state.

Steps
1. Scan or enter the authorised equipment identifier.
2. Confirm equipment class, location, and intended step.
3. Check that the identifier resolves once and to one object.
4. Proceed to status verification.

Steps
1. Confirm availability and authorised status.
2. Confirm calibration, maintenance, cleaning, and qualification indicators required by the instruction.
3. Check that no hold or overdue condition is present.
4. Accept only the configured eligible state.

Steps
1. Perform only the displayed current step.
2. Complete required entries and checks in the stated order.
3. Use Next/Complete only after reviewing the step summary.
4. Confirm the expected transition before beginning the next activity.

Steps
1. Stop the affected activity safely.
2. Select the applicable controlled hold route when authorised.
3. Record the factual reason and affected step/context.
4. Notify the supervisor/quality/support role required by the local procedure.
section: TASK-UG-017 | Place or respect a hold

content:
Steps
1. Review the hold history, impact, open exceptions, and current physical/process state.
2. Confirm the authorised decision and any repeat checks.
3. Use Resume or Terminate only through the configured path.
4. Verify the resulting state and record linkage.

Steps
1. Stop or secure the activity as required.
2. Create the exception from the affected record/step.
3. Describe facts, time, observed condition, and immediate safe action without speculation.
4. Link relevant material, equipment, message, or interface context.

Steps
1. Open the correction function from the affected record.
2. Confirm the original value and context.
3. Enter the true corrected value and a specific reason.
4. Review original/corrected values, actor, time, and required approval before submission.

Steps
1. Read the exact signature meaning and affected record/action.
2. Verify batch, step, outcome, and any statement being affirmed.
3. Re-authenticate personally using the approved method.
4. Confirm the signed event and permanent linkage.

Steps
1. Open the record/activity or audit view from the source context.
2. Set the authorised record, event, actor, and time criteria.
3. Review chronology, prior/new values, reasons, signatures, and unresolved items.
4. Preserve the selected criteria and record the review outcome where required.
section: TASK-UG-022 | Review activity and audit context

content:
Steps
1. Read source, direction, object/message identifier, status, time, and affected step.
2. Determine whether the workflow instructs wait, hold, reject, or escalate.
3. Preserve the identifier and message text/code for support.
4. Continue only after the system shows the configured acceptable state.

Steps
1. Stop the affected action from being submitted again.
2. Check the current status and acknowledgement once using the authorised view.
3. Capture identifiers, time, visible state, and user action.
4. Report through the controlled support channel and await an authorised disposition.
section: TASK-UG-024 | Reconcile an uncertain or duplicate transaction

content:
Steps
1. Review entered and automated values, material/equipment evidence, exceptions, and signatures.
2. Resolve or link all required items.
3. Select Complete once.
4. Confirm the step state and next enabled action.

Steps
1. Review the blocker list for mandatory steps, values, reviews, signatures, and exceptions.
2. Navigate to each listed source item and resolve it through its controlled workflow.
3. Refresh the readiness view once after changes.
4. Select Complete only when no configured blocker remains.

Steps
1. Confirm batch identity/version and execution completeness.
2. Review holds, exceptions, corrections, material/equipment evidence, and unresolved items.
3. Record the factual review outcome and required follow-up.
4. Apply the configured signature only if authorised and accurate.

Steps
1. Confirm record version, review criteria, and complete exception population.
2. Review corrections, signatures, audit evidence, dispositions, and blockers.
3. Record the authorised outcome and rationale.
4. Apply the configured signature only when all required evidence supports it.

Steps
1. Choose the controlled report/view and authorised criteria.
2. Confirm as-of time, record version, unresolved-data indicator, and provenance.
3. Generate the output once and reconcile key totals/identifiers to source.
4. Store or distribute only through the approved controlled location/process.
section: TASK-UG-029 | Run a controlled report or record copy

content:
Steps
1. Capture factual time, role, environment, batch/step, message code, and last successful action without credentials.
2. Submit through the controlled support channel and record the returned case reference when available.
3. Secure the work area and sign out.
4. Confirm the session is closed; preserve linked evidence according to the procedure.
section: TASK-UG-030 | Report an issue and sign out securely

personnel cannot receive non-delegable ownership accountability. 
185. QA must be independent of delivery for approval and release decisions. The project must identify the governing 
approval matrix and resolve the IT-versus-equipment role taxonomy before execution. 
186. Recorded acceptance/signature must show signer, date/time, meaning and approved version. Workflow routing or

comments/decisions and prior approved versions. 
188. Records must be attributable, legible, contemporaneous, original or verified true copy, accurate, complete,

content:
GxP IT Audit Checklist [DA-01-001]: Walk through the proposed intended use, the patient, product-quality and data decisions it will support, and the evidence used to draw the GxP system boundary before funding was approved.
Phase: Concept & Business Case | Domain: Governance | Topic: GxP intended use and system boundary | Priority: Critical
Follow-Up Probe: Reconcile the business-case boundary with the process map, data-flow diagram, application inventory and any functions described as merely administrative; explain every mismatch.
Expected Evidence / Criteria: Approved concept statement; end-to-end process and context diagrams; preliminary GxP assessment; named process/system/data owners; QA approval. Boundaries include interfaces, infrastructure, reports, records and supporting services and are internally consistent.
Regulatory Alignment: Binding: 21 CFR 11.1 and 211.68; Official EU GMP guideline: Annex 11 Principle and §§1, 4.3; Guidance: WHO §§4-5 and 11.1.
Red Flags: No approved intended use; boundary omits reports, interfaces or infrastructure; GxP classification conflicts with process use; QA engaged only after funding.

Follow-Up Probe: Choose a record the business case labels non-GxP and demonstrate why no batch, laboratory, complaint, stability, training or quality decision relies on it, including downstream exports.
Expected Evidence / Criteria: Jurisdiction/predicate-rule matrix; record inventory; Part 11/e-signature applicability assessment; EU/other market assessment; legal and QA review. Each conclusion cites the governing requirement and downstream use. Regulatory Alignment: Binding: 21 CFR 11.1-11.2 and 211 Subpart J; Binding EU legal framework: Directive (EU) 2017/1572 Art. 9; Guidance: FDA Part 11 Scope and Application.
Red Flags: Applicability based only on technology label; no predicate-record mapping; enforcement discretion treated as exemption; markets or retention laws omitted.

content:
GxP IT Audit Checklist [DA-01-003]: Describe the proposed data lifecycle from first capture through processing, review, reporting, retention and destruction, and show where the concept explicitly protects attributable, legible, contemporaneous, original, accurate, complete, consistent, enduring and available data.
Phase: Concept & Business Case | Domain: Data Integrity | Topic: Data lifecycle and ALCOA+ concept | Priority: Critical
Follow-Up Probe: Trace one value that is transformed more than once and identify the original data, metadata, excluded or invalidated values, reviewer visibility and final record at every stage.
Expected Evidence / Criteria: Preliminary data-flow and lifecycle map; data criticality register; ALCOA+ assessment; proposed technical/procedural controls; QA-approved gaps and funding. All transformations and review points are visible.
Regulatory Alignment: Binding: 21 CFR 211.68 and 211.180/188/194; Official EU GMP guideline: Chapter 4 Principle and §4.1; Guidance: MHRA §§3-5 and PIC/S §5.
Red Flags: Only final reports considered records; metadata/intermediate data absent; manual transcriptions not mapped; ALCOA+ cited without funded controls.

content:
GxP IT Audit Checklist [DA-01-004]: Demonstrate how the concept distinguishes source data, raw data, metadata, official records, convenience copies and hybrid components, and how the authoritative version will be identified during an inspection.
Phase: Concept & Business Case | Domain: Records Management | Topic: Authoritative record and raw-data inventory | Priority: Critical
Follow-Up Probe: For a proposed printout or PDF, show why it preserves—or does not need—the dynamic data and metadata required to reconstruct the GxP activity.
Expected Evidence / Criteria: Preliminary record catalogue; record-of-truth decisions; hybrid-system map; dynamic/static assessment; true-copy strategy; ownership and inspection retrieval requirements, approved by QA and records management.
Regulatory Alignment: Binding: 21 CFR 11.10(b)-(c) and 211.180/194; Official EU GMP guideline: Chapter 4 Principle and §§4.1, 4.10; Guidance: FDA DI Q9-Q10 and MHRA §§6.6-6.11.
Red Flags: Final output declared the sole record without rationale; raw data/metadata ownership unclear; hybrid links absent; inspector-copy capability unfunded.

document_title: Top 25 Checklists GxP IT Audit Questions 2026
content:
GxP IT Audit Checklist [DA-01-005]: Explain how preliminary risk assessment differentiated patient-safety, product-quality and data-integrity harm, and how that analysis changed scope, controls, budget or schedule.
Phase: Concept & Business Case | Domain: Quality Risk Management | Topic: Data and process criticality | Priority: Critical
Follow-Up Probe: Present the highest-rated data element and the highest-rated workflow; show the causal chain to harm and why a lower-rated neighboring item received less control.
Expected Evidence / Criteria: Approved risk method; hazard statements; severity/probability/detectability rationale where used; critical data/process list; control decisions; residual-risk owners. Formality and evidence are proportionate to uncertainty and risk.
Regulatory Alignment: Guidance: ICH Q9(R1) §§3-5; Official EU GMP guideline: Annex 11 §1; Guidance: PIC/S §§5.3-5.6 and WHO §5.
Red Flags: Generic risk statements; unexplained low scores; detectability credited without a control; high risk accepted by project management alone; risk used to waive a binding requirement. Finding trigger: evidence is missing, unapproved, incomplete, inconsistent, or cannot be reproduced for the auditor-selected sample.

metadata.expected_evidence: Approved risk method; hazard statements; severity/probability/detectability rationale where used; critical data/process list; control decisions; residual-risk owners. Formality and evidence are proportionate to uncertainty and risk.
metadata.reference: Guidance: ICH Q9(R1) §§3-5; Official EU GMP guideline: Annex 11 §1; Guidance: PIC/S §§5.3-5.6 and WHO §5.

content:
GxP IT Audit Checklist [DA-01-006]: Show how the business case funds documented evidence that the system will remain fit for intended use across configuration, testing, release, operation, change and retirement.
Phase: Concept & Business Case | Domain: Validation Strategy | Topic: Lifecycle assurance and validation funding | Priority: Critical
Follow-Up Probe: Identify an assurance activity removed for cost or speed and demonstrate, through risk and alternative evidence, why confidence in the intended use was not reduced.
Expected Evidence / Criteria: Concept validation plan; lifecycle deliverables; risk-based assurance rationale; independent review; resource/skill estimates; environments and tools; acceptance gates; operational validation budget. Drug-GMP strategy meets predicate rules and Annex 11/15; device-only CSA is clearly scoped.
Regulatory Alignment: Binding: 21 CFR 11.10(a) and 211.68; Official EU GMP guideline: Annex 11 §§1, 4 and Annex 15 §§1-3; FDA guidance (nonbinding, device QMS scope only): CSA §III and V.
Red Flags: Validation is a single pre-go-live test; no operational-state funding; CSA used to waive drug-GMP controls; estimates ignore interfaces/migration; QA approval not budgeted.

metadata.expected_evidence: Concept validation plan; lifecycle deliverables; risk-based assurance rationale; independent review; resource/skill estimates; environments and tools; acceptance gates; operational validation budget. Drug-GMP strategy meets predicate rules and Annex 11/15; device-only CSA is clearly scoped.

Regulatory Alignment: Official EU GMP guideline: Annex 11 §§3.1-3.4; Guidance: MHRA §6.20, PIC/S §10, WHO §7 and ICH Q10 §2.7.
Red Flags: Supplier certification treated as qualification; shared responsibility absent; internal owners unnamed; data or administrator location unknown; audit/regulator access excluded.

content:
GxP IT Audit Checklist [DA-01-008]: Demonstrate that the concept and procurement timetable allow risk-based supplier evaluation, technical assessment, audit where warranted, and remediation before supplier lock-in.

Follow-Up Probe: Show how the team would proceed if the preferred supplier refuses SDLC evidence, audit-trail design details, subcontractor visibility or regulator access.
Expected Evidence / Criteria: Supplier pre-screen; risk tier; due-diligence plan; audit criteria; evidence list; disqualification thresholds; remediation budget/timeline; approved exceptions. Contract award is gated by quality review.
Regulatory Alignment: Official EU GMP guideline: Annex 11 §§3 and 4.5; Guidance: PIC/S §§9.3 and 10, WHO §7 and ICH Q10 §2.7.
Red Flags: Preferred vendor exempted from qualification; no evidence-access criterion; audit scheduled after go-live; unresolved findings omitted from cost; price overrides critical quality criteria.

content:
GxP IT Audit Checklist [DA-01-018]: Explain how proposed recovery objectives were derived from product, patient, data and operational impact, and show that exact and complete backup plus restoration verification are included in cost and responsibilities.

content:
GxP IT Audit Checklist [DA-01-019]: Walk through the proposed business-continuity process during prolonged system or interface loss, including controlled manual records, approvals, inventory/status control and reconciliation after service restoration.
Phase: Concept & Business Case | Domain: Business Continuity | Topic: Operational continuity and manual fallback | Priority: Critical
Follow-Up Probe: Simulate an outage spanning a batch, laboratory result and quality approval; identify where duplicate identifiers, back-dating or conflicting status could arise and how each is prevented.
Expected Evidence / Criteria: Critical-process BIA; continuity workflow; controlled forms/logs; authority and communication rules; offline numbering/time controls; reconciliation and QA review; periodic exercise plan; maximum tolerable outage.
Regulatory Alignment: Official EU GMP guideline: Annex 11 §16 and Chapter 4 §§4.7-4.9; Guidance: MHRA §§5.1, 6.20 and WHO §§4, 11.15-11.19.
Red Flags: Fallback stated as use paper without controlled forms; no reconciliation owner; outage records can be entered later without event time; continuity capacity untested.

Expected Evidence / Criteria: Integrated incident/deviation workflow; severity and GxP impact criteria; data population analysis; investigation/CAPA requirements; supplier notification SLAs; security/quality handoff; management and regulator escalation thresholds. content:
GxP IT Audit Checklist [DA-01-022]: Demonstrate that the business case identifies the competencies and capacity needed for process ownership, configuration, validation, data review, administration, supplier oversight and support throughout the lifecycle.
Phase: Concept & Business Case | Domain: Training & Competence | Topic: Resource, competence and organizational change | Priority: High
Follow-Up Probe: Reconcile the named future-state roles with current headcount and training records, then show how coverage is maintained during turnover, absence and vendor transition.
Expected Evidence / Criteria: Role/competency matrix; workload and segregation analysis; training curriculum and qualification criteria; succession/coverage plan; super-user limits; contractor oversight; recurring training and effectiveness measures; approved funding.
Regulatory Alignment: Binding: 21 CFR 11.10(i), 211.25 and 211.22; Official EU GMP guideline: Annex 11 §2; Guidance: FDA DI Q16, WHO §8 and ICH Q10 §2.
Red Flags: Key roles part-time with no workload analysis; training ends at go-live; supplier staff assumed qualified without evidence; incompatible duties assigned to one person; no backup personnel.

content:
GxP IT Audit Checklist [DA-01-023]: Present the major compliance assumptions and trade-offs in the approved business case and show how changes to cost, schedule or scope trigger independent quality reassessment and go/no-go decisions.

Follow-Up Probe: Select the largest cost reduction and shortest schedule assumption and trace their effect on supplier qualification, requirements, migration, testing, training, continuity and operational controls.
Expected Evidence / Criteria: Decision log; assumptions register; quality gates; contingency and remediation reserves; independent QA approvals; escalation thresholds; benefits/schedule baseline; documented residual-risk acceptance by accountable management.

Red Flags: QA lacks veto; launch date fixed before evidence; risk acceptance owned only by project; compliance contingency absent; critical deliverables removed without traceable decision.

document_title: Top 25 Checklists GxP IT Audit Questions 2026
content:
GxP IT Audit Checklist [DA-01-025]: Show how the concept funds an exit strategy that preserves readable GxP records, metadata, audit trails, signatures, configurations and retrieval capability after contract termination or technology obsolescence.
Phase: Concept & Business Case | Domain: Retirement & Exit | Topic: Decommissioning, portability and supplier exit | Priority: Critical
Follow-Up Probe: Assume immediate supplier insolvency or account suspension and demonstrate how the company would obtain a complete, usable and verified record set plus the software, keys or viewer needed to inspect it.
Expected Evidence / Criteria: Exit and decommission concept; data/export specifications; contractual assistance; escrow/viewer/key strategy where justified; verification and reconciliation; retention ownership; destruction authorization; budget and trigger points.
Regulatory Alignment: Official EU GMP guideline: Annex 11 §17 and Chapter 4 §§4.10-4.12; Guidance: MHRA §§6.17, 6.20, PIC/S §§9.9-10 and WHO §§7, 11.15-11.19; ICH Q10 §3.1.4.
Red Flags: Exit cost omitted; proprietary export without metadata; supplier owns encryption keys; destruction may occur before QA approval; no supported long-term viewer or reconciliation criterion.

content:
GxP IT Audit Checklist [DA-02-001]: Explain how business, quality, technical and data owners converted the approved intended use into the URS, and show how conflicts, assumptions, exclusions and unresolved requirements are governed before design begins.
Phase: User Requirements (URS) | Domain: Governance | Topic: URS ownership, authorship and approval | Priority: Critical
Follow-Up Probe: Select five requirements written or modified by the supplier and demonstrate the regulated-company SME who verified each business need, risk and acceptance criterion independently.
Expected Evidence / Criteria: Controlled URS; author/reviewer competence; comments and resolution log; requirements governance/RACI; glossary; assumptions, constraints and exclusions; QA approval. Requirements are uniquely identified, versioned, unambiguous and owned. Acceptance: evidence is current, approved where required, complete for the selected population, and consistent with the live configuration and independent records.
Regulatory Alignment: Binding quality oversight: 21 CFR 211.22; Official EU GMP guideline: Annex 11 §§2, 4.4 and Annex 15 §§2-3; Guidance: ICH Q10 §2.
Red Flags: Supplier copied its product specification into the URS; requirements lack owners or unique IDs; exclusions are implicit; approval predates workshops; QA comments were closed without evidence. Finding trigger: evidence is missing, unapproved, incomplete, inconsistent, or cannot be reproduced for the auditor-selected sample.

metadata.reference: Binding quality oversight: 21 CFR 211.22; Official EU GMP guideline: Annex 11 §§2, 4.4 and Annex 15 §§2-3; Guidance: ICH Q10 §2.

document_title: Top 25 Checklists GxP IT Audit Questions 2026
content:
GxP IT Audit Checklist [DA-02-002]: Trace each intended use and predicate-record obligation into specific URS requirements for creation, review, approval, retention, retrieval and inspection, including functions outside the primary application boundary.
Phase: User Requirements (URS) | Domain: Regulatory Compliance | Topic: Intended use, predicate records and scope traceability | Priority: Critical
Follow-Up Probe: Choose one downstream report used for release or quality disposition and demonstrate the requirement chain back to its source data, metadata, reviewer and governing record obligation.
Expected Evidence / Criteria: Intended-use statement; GxP/Part 11 assessment; predicate-rule matrix; record/signature inventory; bidirectional concept-to-URS traceability; system-boundary diagram. Every regulated use and record has testable requirements or approved rationale.
Regulatory Alignment: Binding: 21 CFR 11.1-11.2, 11.10 and 211 Subpart J; Binding EU framework: Directive (EU) 2017/1572 Art. 9; Official EU GMP guideline: Annex 11 Principle and §4.4.
Red Flags: Part 11 assessment not linked to requirements; reports/exports omitted from boundary; predicate records unnamed; requirements cover storage but not review, retrieval or inspection.

metadata.expected_evidence: Intended-use statement; GxP/Part 11 assessment; predicate-rule matrix; record/signature inventory; bidirectional concept-to-URS traceability; system-boundary diagram. Every regulated use and record has testable requirements or approved rationale.
