document_title: Top 25 Checklists GxP IT Audit Questions 2026
content:
GxP IT Audit Checklist [DA-02-003]: Show how critical process steps, data elements, metadata, calculations, reports and configurations are identified in the URS and linked to preliminary risk decisions without using priority labels as a substitute for compliance.
Phase: User Requirements (URS) | Domain: Quality Risk Management | Topic: Critical function and data classification | Priority: Critical
Follow-Up Probe: Take a requirement marked low priority that handles a critical identifier or status and reconcile the rating with its downstream use and failure consequence.
Expected Evidence / Criteria: Critical data/process inventory; requirement attributes for GxP impact and criticality; risk references; rationale and owners; rules separating business priority from quality risk; approved traceability.
Regulatory Alignment: Guidance: ICH Q9(R1) §§3-5; Official EU GMP guideline: Annex 11 §§1 and 4.4; Guidance: MHRA §§4-5, PIC/S §5 and WHO §5.
Red Flags: MoSCoW priority used as risk; metadata/configuration not classified; low ratings lack causal rationale; criticality differs between URS and data inventory; mandatory controls marked optional.

metadata.expected_evidence: Critical data/process inventory; requirement attributes for GxP impact and criticality; risk references; rationale and owners; rules separating business priority from quality risk; approved traceability.

document_title: Top 25 Checklists GxP IT Audit Questions 2026
content:
GxP IT Audit Checklist [DA-02-004]: Demonstrate how each URS statement expresses an observable outcome, boundary condition and acceptance criterion that can establish fitness for intended use rather than merely repeating policy words such as secure, compliant or user-friendly.
Phase: User Requirements (URS) | Domain: Validation Strategy | Topic: Testable requirements and acceptance criteria | Priority: Critical
Follow-Up Probe: Select three high-risk requirements and show the positive, negative, boundary and failure-recovery evidence that could objectively prove each one before design is known.
Expected Evidence / Criteria: Requirement quality checklist; measurable acceptance criteria; risk/test attributes; traceability conventions; verification method and responsible reviewer; approved ambiguity resolutions. Drug-GMP assurance is grounded in predicate rules/Annex 11, not a device-only CSA waiver.
Regulatory Alignment: Binding: 21 CFR 11.10(a) and 211.68; Official EU GMP guideline: Annex 11 §§4.1, 4.4, 4.7 and Annex 15 §2; FDA guidance (nonbinding, device QMS scope only): CSA §V.A.
Red Flags: Subjective adjectives without measures; multiple controls bundled into one requirement; negative/error cases absent; acceptance delegated solely to supplier; CSA cited outside device scope to reduce evidence.

metadata.expected_evidence: Requirement quality checklist; measurable acceptance criteria; risk/test attributes; traceability conventions; verification method and responsible reviewer; approved ambiguity resolutions. Drug-GMP assurance is grounded in predicate rules/Annex 11, not a device-only CSA waiver.

document_title: Top 25 Checklists GxP IT Audit Questions 2026
content:
GxP IT Audit Checklist [DA-02-005]: Describe the URS requirements that preserve the full record context—originator, event time, system time, units, status, method, version, reason and relationships—from first capture through every transformation.
Phase: User Requirements (URS) | Domain: Data Integrity | Topic: Metadata, contemporaneity and ALCOA+ requirements | Priority: Critical
Follow-Up Probe: Choose one displayed value and show every metadata element needed to reconstruct who did what, when and under which configuration; identify where the URS requires each element to be retained and reviewable.
Expected Evidence / Criteria: Data/metadata dictionary; ALCOA+ requirement mapping; time-zone and clock rules; contemporaneous capture; provenance and lineage; completeness rules; review and retention requirements; controlled rationale for any excluded metadata.
Regulatory Alignment: Binding: 21 CFR 11.10(e) and 211.188/194; Official EU GMP guideline: Chapter 4 Principle and §§4.7-4.9; Guidance: FDA DI Q1, MHRA §§6.1-6.7 and WHO §4.
Red Flags: Only visible fields specified; event and entry times conflated; time zone absent; metadata may be overwritten; lineage ends at report; ALCOA+ appears only in a generic preamble.

content:

content:
GxP IT Audit Checklist [DA-02-008]: Demonstrate how the URS specifies unique attribution, role-based least privilege, joiner/mover/leaver timing, periodic review and ownership for human, service, interface and robotic identities.
Phase: User Requirements (URS) | Domain: Access & Security | Topic: Unique identity and least-privilege requirements | Priority: Critical
Follow-Up Probe: Map the full lifecycle of one external contractor and one nonhuman account, including creation approval, credential storage, allowed transactions, monitoring, review and revocation.

content:

content:
GxP IT Audit Checklist [DA-02-011]: Walk through each critical workflow and show how the URS requires permitted sequence, prerequisite evidence, role authority, status transitions and prevention or controlled override of out-of-order processing.
Phase: User Requirements (URS) | Domain: Workflow Controls | Topic: Operational, authority and sequence checks | Priority: Critical
Follow-Up Probe: Attempt to approve before required data exist, repeat a completed step, use an unauthorized role and reopen a released record; identify the specified response and retained evidence for each.
Expected Evidence / Criteria: State-transition and use-case requirements; prerequisite/operational checks; authority matrix; override reasons/approval; duplicate/replay prevention; status visibility; exception/audit behavior; acceptance criteria.

Red Flags: Happy path only; override unlogged; roles can self-approve; prerequisites described only in SOP despite configurable enforcement; released records can be reopened silently. content:
GxP IT Audit Checklist [DA-02-012]: Explain how the URS differentiates input sources and requires validity, completeness, range, format, unit, identifier and duplicate checks while preserving rejected attempts and controlled corrections where they are GxP-relevant.

content:

content:

content:
GxP IT Audit Checklist [DA-02-017]: Describe how the URS requires preservation or justified archival of legacy values, metadata, audit trails, signatures, status, links and record meaning, including reconciliation and handling of invalid or unmappable data.
Phase: User Requirements (URS) | Domain: Data Migration | Topic: Migration, conversion and legacy-history requirements | Priority: Critical
Follow-Up Probe: Select a legacy record with corrections, attachments and signatures and trace each component to the target or archive, including how a user proves completeness after migration.

document_title: Top 25 Checklists GxP IT Audit Questions 2026
content:
GxP IT Audit Checklist [DA-02-018]: Trace every record category to a requirement for retention start event, period, archive format, metadata/audit history, readability test, legal hold, authorized destruction and documented evidence of disposition.
Phase: User Requirements (URS) | Domain: Records Management | Topic: Retention, archive, legal hold and destruction requirements | Priority: Critical
Follow-Up Probe: Apply two different jurisdictional retention rules and a legal hold to the same linked record set; show how the URS prevents premature deletion of the record or its dependent metadata.
Expected Evidence / Criteria: Approved retention matrix; event-based rules; archive/search/readability; linkage preservation; hold and purge authorization; destruction evidence; anonymization where applicable; supplier/default conflicts resolved.
Regulatory Alignment: Binding: 21 CFR 11.10(c) and 211.180; Official EU GMP guideline: Annex 11 §17 and Chapter 4 §§4.10-4.12; Guidance: MHRA §6.17 and WHO §§11.15-11.19.
Red Flags: Retention period has no start event; child objects purge earlier; audit trails omitted; legal hold is manual and untested; vendor default overrides law; deletion leaves no evidence.

content:
GxP IT Audit Checklist [DA-02-019]: Show how the URS specifies exact and complete backup scope, frequency, protection, separation, monitoring and periodic restoration with reconciliation to justified RPO and RTO.
Phase: User Requirements (URS) | Domain: Resilience | Topic: Backup integrity and verified restoration requirements | Priority: Critical
Follow-Up Probe: Assume latent corruption, compromised administrator credentials and loss of the primary region; demonstrate the required recovery source, integrity proof and transaction-level reconciliation.
Expected Evidence / Criteria: Backup objects include data, metadata, audit trails, configuration, keys and dependencies; justified RPO/RTO; immutable/offline protection where risk warrants; restore frequency; acceptance/control totals; alerts and retained test evidence.
Regulatory Alignment: Binding: 21 CFR 211.68(b) and 11.10(c); Official EU GMP guideline: Annex 11 §§7, 16; Guidance: MHRA §6.17, PIC/S §9.9 and WHO §§11.15-11.18.

content:
GxP IT Audit Checklist [DA-02-020]: Walk through URS requirements for controlled offline operation during application, interface, identity or site outages and for complete, duplicate-free reconciliation when service returns.

content:
GxP IT Audit Checklist [DA-03-001]: Walk through the risk-assessment method, decision rules and governance used for this system, and demonstrate how the level of formality and documentation is proportionate to uncertainty, complexity and potential harm.
Phase: Risk Assessment & GAMP Categorisation | Domain: Quality Risk Management | Topic: Risk method, governance and formality | Priority: Critical
Follow-Up Probe: Reperform one high, one medium and one low decision with independent SMEs; explain score differences, assumptions and why the method would not allow an otherwise noncompliant control to be accepted.
Expected Evidence / Criteria: Approved QRM procedure; trained cross-functional team; defined scope, scales and decision rules; evidence-based hazards; documented assumptions/uncertainty; independent QA review; escalation and risk-acceptance authority. QRM does not waive binding controls.
Regulatory Alignment: Guidance: ICH Q9(R1) §§3-5; Official EU GMP guideline: Annex 11 §1; Guidance: PIC/S §§5.3-5.6 and WHO §5.
Red Flags: One-person assessment; all scores cluster low; severity reduced because controls exist; detectability credited without evidence; project owner accepts quality risk; binding requirement risk-scored away. Finding trigger: evidence is missing, unapproved, incomplete, inconsistent, or cannot be reproduced for the auditor-selected sample.

metadata.expected_evidence: Approved QRM procedure; trained cross-functional team; defined scope, scales and decision rules; evidence-based hazards; documented assumptions/uncertainty; independent QA review; escalation and risk-acceptance authority. QRM does not waive binding controls.

content:
GxP IT Audit Checklist [DA-03-002]: Demonstrate how the risk boundary follows the complete intended use across application, infrastructure, interfaces, records, people, procedures and external services rather than the procurement boundary.

Follow-Up Probe: Select one component labeled out of scope and trace whether its failure could alter a GxP decision, record, timestamp, access authorization or recovery capability.
Expected Evidence / Criteria: Approved intended use; context and data-flow diagrams; component/service inventory; dependency map; in/out rationale; process and data owners; linked URS and supplier responsibilities; QA approval.

Red Flags: Boundary equals vendor application only; identity, middleware or reporting excluded; diagrams conflict; out-of-scope rationale has no failure analysis; owners cannot identify dependencies.

metadata.expected_evidence: Approved intended use; context and data-flow diagrams; component/service inventory; dependency map; in/out rationale; process and data owners; linked URS and supplier responsibilities; QA approval.

content:
GxP IT Audit Checklist [DA-03-004]: Show how the assessment decomposed the system into software modules, configurations, custom code, reports, interfaces, infrastructure and supplier services at a level where distinct failure modes and controls can be evaluated.
Phase: Risk Assessment & GAMP Categorisation | Domain: System Inventory | Topic: Component, configuration and service decomposition | Priority: Critical
Follow-Up Probe: Compare the assessed inventory with the deployment bill of materials and identify every executable, scheduled job, low-code workflow or external service absent from the risk record.
Expected Evidence / Criteria: Versioned component/service inventory; architecture and software bill of materials where available; configuration/custom object list; ownership; category and criticality; traceability to functions, suppliers and environments.

Red Flags: Inventory at application-name level only; versions absent; low-code/custom objects unlisted; production differs from assessed baseline; supplier services and dependencies omitted.

document_title: Top 25 Checklists GxP IT Audit Questions 2026
content:
GxP IT Audit Checklist [DA-03-005]: For each critical function, explain the credible failure modes and causal path from incorrect, missing, delayed or unauthorized system behavior to patient safety, product quality or supply impact.
Phase: Risk Assessment & GAMP Categorisation | Domain: Patient/Product Risk | Topic: Failure modes and causal link to harm | Priority: Critical
Follow-Up Probe: Take the top-rated and a low-rated failure mode and challenge both against worst credible use, existing detection time and the possibility of correlated failures across batches or sites.
Expected Evidence / Criteria: Function-level hazard analysis; affected process/record/product; causal chain; severity rationale; failure detectability and timing; current/proposed controls; cross-batch/site exposure; residual risk and owner.

document_title: Top 25 Checklists GxP IT Audit Questions 2026
content:
GxP IT Audit Checklist [DA-03-024]: For every high or critical inherent risk, demonstrate that selected controls are specific, implemented by a named owner, testable, sustainable in operation and sufficient to justify the residual-risk conclusion.
Phase: Risk Assessment & GAMP Categorisation | Domain: Risk Control | Topic: Control effectiveness and residual-risk ownership | Priority: Critical
Follow-Up Probe: Remove the primary control for one high risk and show whether independent layers detect the failure before harm; explain any single-point dependence and monitoring threshold.
Expected Evidence / Criteria: Control descriptions linked to requirements/design/SOP; owner and timing; preventive/detective nature; effectiveness evidence/acceptance criteria; dependencies and common cause; residual rationale; appropriate quality/management approval; open actions gated.
Regulatory Alignment: Guidance: ICH Q9(R1) §§4.4-4.6 and ICH Q10 §§2, 4; Official EU GMP guideline: Annex 11 §1; Guidance: WHO §5.
Red Flags: Future control credited as effective; owner is a department not person/role; residual score drops without evidence; single detective control acts after release; project manager accepts quality risk.

metadata.expected_evidence: Control descriptions linked to requirements/design/SOP; owner and timing; preventive/detective nature; effectiveness evidence/acceptance criteria; dependencies and common cause; residual rationale; appropriate quality/management approval; open actions gated.

Red Flags: Review only at fixed document expiry; supplier/security/AI changes not triggers; prior rationale overwritten; risk actions can remain overdue through release; no owner monitors assumptions.

document_title: Top 25 Checklists GxP IT Audit Questions 2026
content:
GxP IT Audit Checklist [DA-04-001]: Explain how supplier criticality was determined from intended use, control reliance, data access, service substitutability, complexity and failure impact, and show how that rating set the depth of due diligence and approval.
Phase: Supplier Assessment & Qualification | Domain: Supplier Governance | Topic: Supplier criticality and qualification depth | Priority: Critical
Follow-Up Probe: Compare two suppliers with the same questionnaire score but different GxP reliance; demonstrate why their audit, evidence and ongoing-monitoring plans differ.
Expected Evidence / Criteria: Approved supplier-risk method; intended-use/control reliance map; criticality rationale; due-diligence/audit plan; evidence gaps; remediation and approval authority; requalification triggers. Assessment depth is risk-based and independent of spend or brand.
Regulatory Alignment: Official EU GMP guideline: Annex 11 §§1, 3; Guidance: PIC/S §§10.1-10.3, WHO §7, ICH Q9(R1) §§3-5 and ICH Q10 §2.7.
Red Flags: Tier based on annual spend; SaaS automatically low risk; subprocessor not rated; questionnaire determines approval without verification; remediation deferred until after contract/go-live.

document_title: Top 25 Checklists GxP IT Audit Questions 2026
content:
GxP IT Audit Checklist [DA-04-002]: Walk through the supplier QMS from leadership oversight through document control, training, deviation/CAPA, change, internal audit and management review, and demonstrate its effectiveness with recent records rather than policy statements.
Phase: Supplier Assessment & Qualification | Domain: Quality Management System | Topic: Supplier governance and QMS effectiveness | Priority: Critical
Follow-Up Probe: Select a repeated defect or audit finding and trace investigation, root cause, CAPA, effectiveness check and management escalation; reconcile any recurrence with the supplier's closure decision.
Expected Evidence / Criteria: Current QMS scope/certificates; procedures and organization; management-review metrics; internal audit; deviations/CAPA and effectiveness; training; document/record control; customer-impact escalation; quality independence. Sample records show timely, sustained control.
Regulatory Alignment: Official EU GMP guideline: Annex 11 §§3.2-3.4, 4.5; Guidance: PIC/S §§9.3, 10, WHO §7 and ICH Q10 §§2, 2.7, 4.
Red Flags: Certificate scope excludes product/service; CAPAs close without effectiveness; repeat findings hidden in separate systems; quality reports to sales/project; customer-impact assessment undocumented. Finding trigger: evidence is missing, unapproved, incomplete, inconsistent, or cannot be reproduced for the auditor-selected sample.

metadata.expected_evidence: Current QMS scope/certificates; procedures and organization; management-review metrics; internal audit; deviations/CAPA and effectiveness; training; document/record control; customer-impact escalation; quality independence. Sample records show timely, sustained control.

Phase: Supplier Assessment & Qualification | Domain: Software Lifecycle | Topic: Supplier SDLC and product lifecycle controls | Priority: Critical
Follow-Up Probe: Trace one high-impact requirement from backlog through code/configuration, review, test, defect disposition, build and released version; explain every missing link.
Expected Evidence / Criteria: Lifecycle procedures; version control and branch/review rules; requirements/design/test traceability; build/release integrity; environment segregation; defect/change records; support/EOL policy; sample end-to-end trace for current version.

Red Flags: Policies not applied to sampled release; no code review; production build not traceable to tested artifact; hotfix bypasses lifecycle; custom/configured components excluded; EOL surprise.

content:
GxP IT Audit Checklist [DA-04-005]: Walk through the deployed architecture and identify standard functions, tenant configuration, custom code, low-code components, reports, integrations and shared services, showing which lifecycle evidence and owner covers each.
Phase: Supplier Assessment & Qualification | Domain: Architecture | Topic: Product architecture, configuration and customization transparency | Priority: Critical
Follow-Up Probe: Reconcile the supplier's standard-product claim with the actual object inventory and demonstrate how hidden extensions or customer-specific scripts are versioned, tested and supported.
Expected Evidence / Criteria: Current architecture; component/version inventory; standard/configured/custom classification; extension repositories; supported configuration rules; dependency/bill-of-material evidence; ownership and support boundaries; customer-specific baseline.

Red Flags: Architecture is marketing-level; tenant customizations unlisted; production baseline cannot be exported; unsupported scripts used; component versions unknown; supplier/customer ownership overlaps.

Phase: Supplier Assessment & Qualification | Domain: Validation Evidence | Topic: Supplier documentation and customer-use applicability | Priority: Critical
Follow-Up Probe: Select a supplier test claimed as coverage for a critical customer requirement and show matching preconditions, configuration, data, expected result, execution evidence, reviewer independence and unresolved defects.
Expected Evidence / Criteria: Evidence-leverage assessment; document provenance/version; supplier QMS basis; requirement/configuration applicability; test records and deviations; gap analysis; customer verification plan; controlled access and retention; QA approval. content:
GxP IT Audit Checklist [DA-04-007]: Trace how test data, expected results, execution identity/time, environment, actual outcomes, deviations and defects are controlled so that passing status cannot be created by excluding failed or repeated runs.
Phase: Supplier Assessment & Qualification | Domain: Testing & Defects | Topic: Test integrity, deviations and defect transparency | Priority: Critical
Follow-Up Probe: Choose a test with multiple executions and reconcile every run, failure, changed expected result, defect and final release decision from immutable source evidence.
Expected Evidence / Criteria: Controlled test management; original execution evidence and audit history; environment/build identity; all runs retained; deviation/defect linkage; retest prerequisites; severity/customer-impact rationale; release acceptance and known-issue disclosure.
Regulatory Alignment: Binding customer duty: 21 CFR 11.10(a), 211.68; Official EU GMP guideline: Annex 11 §§4.6-4.7; Guidance: FDA DI principles Q2-Q3 and WHO §§11.1-11.5.
Red Flags: Failed runs deleted; expected result changed after execution; environment/build absent; defects closed as user error without investigation; customer-impacting known issues withheld; screenshots are sole evidence.

metadata.expected_evidence: Controlled test management; original execution evidence and audit history; environment/build identity; all runs retained; deviation/defect linkage; retest prerequisites; severity/customer-impact rationale; release acceptance and known-issue disclosure.

content:
GxP IT Audit Checklist [DA-04-008]: Explain how the supplier's security governance, risk management, independent assessments and certifications apply to the exact service, regions and subprocessors, and how gaps are translated into GxP risk rather than accepted by badge.
Phase: Supplier Assessment & Qualification | Domain: Cybersecurity | Topic: Security governance and assurance reports | Priority: Critical
Follow-Up Probe: Select one certification control exception and one penetration-test finding; trace remediation, residual exposure, customer notification and the GxP functions that depend on the control.
Expected Evidence / Criteria: Security governance/RACI; current independent reports and scope; statement of applicability; penetration/vulnerability results; remediation evidence; incident metrics; customer control dependencies; risk acceptance and ongoing evidence schedule.
Regulatory Alignment: Binding GxP: 21 CFR 11.10(c)-(e), 11.30; Official EU GMP guideline: Annex 11 §§3, 7, 12-13; Supplementary non-GxP: NIST SP 800-53 and ISO/IEC 27001.
Red Flags: Certificate scope excludes service/region; exceptions unavailable; pen-test summary is stale; security evidence treated as GxP validation; remediation dates conflict with risk acceptance.

Red Flags: Shared support IDs; customer cannot see privileged actions; leaver evidence sampled only locally; emergency access permanently enabled; subcontractors outside access review; direct database access unlogged.

content:
GxP IT Audit Checklist [DA-04-010]: Show how the product automatically captures and protects who, what, when and why for relevant record, configuration, master-data, access and administrator events, including prior/new values and customer control over enablement.
Phase: Supplier Assessment & Qualification | Domain: Audit Trails | Topic: Native audit-trail capability and tenant control | Priority: Critical
Follow-Up Probe: In a sandbox, alter, delete, reprocess and restore data, change a role and attempt to disable logging; reconcile every action to the resulting trail and immutable backend evidence.
Expected Evidence / Criteria: Event catalogue; field-level demonstrations; reason rules; trusted timestamps; immutable/protected storage; enablement/defaults; privileged-event coverage; retention/export/search; trail configuration baseline; known limitations and remediation.
Regulatory Alignment: Binding: 21 CFR 11.10(e); Official EU GMP guideline: Annex 11 §9; Guidance: MHRA §6.13, PIC/S §9.6 and WHO §§11.10-11.12.
Red Flags: Logs show only current value; no reason; supplier admin can disable/delete; audit trail off by default; tenant cannot export; configuration/access events missing; timestamps differ across services.

Follow-Up Probe: Assume a neighboring tenant exploit and a provider control failure; show how customer data exposure or corruption is prevented, detected, bounded, reported and evidenced.
Expected Evidence / Criteria: Detailed architecture/data-flow; responsibility matrix to control level; tenant-isolation evidence; control-plane access; configuration boundaries; monitoring and evidence catalogue; regions/dependencies; customer controls and residual gaps. Red Flags: RACI at provider/customer level only; tenant-isolation evidence absent; customer cannot observe control performance; shared control assigned to both or neither; hidden regional dependency.

document_title: Top 25 Checklists GxP IT Audit Questions 2026
content:
GxP IT Audit Checklist [DA-04-012]: Identify every subprocessor that can host, access, change, transmit, back up or support GxP data/services, and demonstrate risk-based qualification, contractual flow-down and ongoing change control.
Phase: Supplier Assessment & Qualification | Domain: Subcontractor Management | Topic: Subprocessor qualification and flow-down | Priority: Critical
Follow-Up Probe: Select the least visible fourth-party service and trace its access, location, control evidence, incident/change obligations and removal contingency to the customer agreement.
Expected Evidence / Criteria: Complete subprocessor register; service/data/access mapping; qualification evidence; flow-down of quality/security/retention/audit/incident/change duties; advance notice and objection rights; monitoring and exit alternatives.
Regulatory Alignment: Official EU GMP guideline: Annex 11 §3; Guidance: MHRA §6.20, PIC/S §10, WHO §7 and ICH Q10 §2.7.
Red Flags: Supplier says no subcontractors but cloud services exist; list is incomplete or marketing-only; no advance notice/objection; flow-down excludes inspection access; fourth-party incidents need not reach customer.

document_title: Top 25 Checklists GxP IT Audit Questions 2026
content:
GxP IT Audit Checklist [DA-04-014]: Demonstrate how the supplier specifies, tests and controls interface schemas, transformations, authentication, acknowledgements, retries, idempotency, error handling, version compatibility and retained transmission evidence.
Phase: Supplier Assessment & Qualification | Domain: Interfaces & APIs | Topic: Integration reliability, versioning and evidence | Priority: Critical
Follow-Up Probe: Recreate a breaking API change, partial payload and repeated retry; show customer notification, version coexistence, detection, reconciliation and records retained for investigation.
Expected Evidence / Criteria: Versioned interface/API specifications; field mappings; security; compatibility/deprecation policy; test evidence; monitoring/error queues; control totals/reconciliation; change notice; log retention; support ownership.
Regulatory Alignment: Binding: 21 CFR 11.10(a)-(c), (h), 211.68; Official EU GMP guideline: Annex 11 §§4.8, 5; Guidance: PIC/S §9.4 and WHO §9.
Red Flags: API can change without notice; mapping omits metadata; no idempotency/reconciliation; supplier deletes error logs quickly; authentication relies on shared credential; deprecation shorter than change cycle.

content:
GxP IT Audit Checklist [DA-04-015]: Show the exact backup scope, schedules, retention, isolation, encryption, monitoring and restoration process for tenant data, metadata, audit trails, configuration, files and keys.
Phase: Supplier Assessment & Qualification | Domain: Backup & Recovery | Topic: Backup completeness and restore verification | Priority: Critical
Follow-Up Probe: Select a completed restoration test and reconcile source and restored counts, hashes, relationships, audit history, application usability and exceptions rather than relying on job success status.
Expected Evidence / Criteria: Backup architecture/inventory; RPO coverage; immutable/separate protection where justified; monitored jobs; tenant-level and regional restore; periodic test plan/results; data integrity reconciliation; failure CAPA; customer evidence and responsibilities.
Regulatory Alignment: Binding: 21 CFR 211.68(b), 11.10(c); Official EU GMP guideline: Annex 11 §7; Guidance: MHRA §6.17, PIC/S §9.9 and WHO §§11.15-11.18.
Red Flags: Audit trails/configuration/keys excluded; restore tests are infrastructure-only; tenant restoration unavailable; backup shares admin domain; test exceptions not investigated; customer receives no evidence.

metadata.expected_evidence: Backup architecture/inventory; RPO coverage; immutable/separate protection where justified; monitored jobs; tenant-level and regional restore; periodic test plan/results; data integrity reconciliation; failure CAPA; customer evidence and responsibilities.

document_title: Top 25 Checklists GxP IT Audit Questions 2026
content:
GxP IT Audit Checklist [DA-04-016]: Demonstrate how the supplier derived and tested availability, capacity, RTO and RPO across application and external dependencies, and how customers are informed and supported during regional or prolonged disruption.
Phase: Supplier Assessment & Qualification | Domain: Business Continuity | Topic: Resilience, capacity and disaster recovery | Priority: Critical
Follow-Up Probe: Walk through the most recent exercise or real outage from detection to failover, data reconciliation, customer communication, return to normal and corrective actions, reconciling actual times with SLA claims.
Expected Evidence / Criteria: BIA; dependency and failure-mode analysis; capacity/load evidence; DR architecture; exercise results with actual RTO/RPO and reconciliation; communication/escalation; deviations/CAPA; customer continuity inputs and recurring schedule.
Regulatory Alignment: Official EU GMP guideline: Annex 11 §16; Guidance: MHRA §6.20, PIC/S §§9.9-10 and WHO §§7, 11.15-11.19; ICH Q10 §2.7.
Red Flags: Only tabletop exercise; no tenant/data reconciliation; actual RTO exceeds contract but reported as pass; hidden dependency not exercised; customer notifications delayed; CAPA absent.

metadata.expected_evidence: BIA; dependency and failure-mode analysis; capacity/load evidence; DR architecture; exercise results with actual RTO/RPO and reconciliation; communication/escalation; deviations/CAPA; customer continuity inputs and recurring schedule.
metadata.reference: Official EU GMP guideline: Annex 11 §16; Guidance: MHRA §6.20, PIC/S §§9.9-10 and WHO §§7, 11.15-11.19; ICH Q10 §2.7.

document_title: Top 25 Checklists GxP IT Audit Questions 2026
content:
GxP IT Audit Checklist [DA-04-017]: Demonstrate that the service can retain and retrieve complete readable records—including metadata, audit trails, attachments, signatures and relationships—for customer-defined periods and provide accurate human-readable and electronic copies promptly.

content:
GxP IT Audit Checklist [DA-05-012]: For every critical formula and rule, identify authoritative inputs, source reference, version, units, precision, rounding, boundary/missing-data behavior, effective date and stored evidence needed to reproduce the result.

Expected Evidence / Criteria: Approved calculation/rule specifications; exact formula/decision table; input provenance; unit and precision conventions; null/error behavior; version/effective dating; independent oracle; stored result lineage; recalculation and downstream-impact rules.

Red Flags: Formula described in prose only; rounding in code but not spec; missing data treated silently; version absent from result; same implementation used as expected-value oracle; recalculation overwrites history.

content:

content:

Phase: Performance Qualification (PQ) / UAT | Domain: Incident Mgmt | Topic: Realistic exception workflows | Priority: Critical
Follow-Up Probe: Take one exception that crosses business, IT, and quality boundaries and trace every status, decision, signature, notification, timeout, and audit event to closure.
Expected Evidence / Criteria: Evidence: exception process and criteria, representative UAT scenarios, records/audit trails, notifications, tickets/deviations, disposition and approval. Acceptance: exceptions remain visible, owned, time-bound, and traceable; no status permits uncontrolled continuation; closure is reconciled.

Red Flags: Equipment simulated without rationale; calibration/status not checked; single successful run; source data manually re-entered; process output not reconciled.

Follow-Up Probe: Interrupt one cross-system transaction after the source user completes it and require business users to detect, investigate, recover, and verify the final state using approved procedures.
Expected Evidence / Criteria: Evidence: end-to-end process/data-flow map, UAT scenarios, source/middleware/target records, control totals, alerts, error queue, recovery procedure, and business sign-off. Acceptance: users can determine status and ownership; no data are silently lost/duplicated; recovery preserves auditability and downstream consistency.
Regulatory Alignment: EU GMP Annex 11 Sections 4.3, 5 and 13; 21 CFR 11.10(a) and 11.10(f), where applicable.
Red Flags: Only middleware evidence; users cannot see failures; manual reprocessing lacks approval; target and source disagree after recovery; reconciliation ownership unclear.

Follow-Up Probe: Seed a plausible but significant unauthorized or anomalous change among routine events and demonstrate whether the reviewer identifies, interprets, escalates, and documents it.
Expected Evidence / Criteria: Evidence: review procedure/criteria, reviewer roles and training, representative audit datasets, seeded-event scenario, review output, escalation, and acceptance. Acceptance: reviewers retrieve complete data, distinguish significant events, document conclusions, and escalate correctly within a justified time.
Regulatory Alignment: EU GMP Annex 11 Section 9; 21 CFR 11.10(e); FDA data-integrity guidance; PIC/S PI 041-1.

Phase: Performance Qualification (PQ) / UAT | Domain: Access Management | Topic: Signature meaning in business context | Priority: Critical
Follow-Up Probe: Present a record with an unresolved exception and ask different roles to sign; show which signatures are blocked, what each permitted signature means, and how later change affects prior approval.
Expected Evidence / Criteria: Evidence: signature matrix, process rules, role mapping, UAT scenarios, signed records/copies, audit trails, user explanation, and SOP. Regulatory Alignment: EU GMP Annex 11 Section 14; 21 CFR 11.50, 11.70 and 11.200, where Part 11 applies.
Red Flags: Meaning is generic 'approved'; users cannot explain responsibility; premature signing allowed; later change leaves approval appearing current; signature absent from copy.

metadata.reference: EU GMP Annex 11 Section 14; 21 CFR 11.50, 11.70 and 11.200, where Part 11 applies.

Phase: Performance Qualification (PQ) / UAT | Domain: BCP | Topic: Manual workaround and continuity execution | Priority: Critical
Follow-Up Probe: Run a timed outage scenario that crosses a shift or handoff, then restore service and trace every manual record, approval, correction, and reconciliation decision into the electronic record.
Expected Evidence / Criteria: Evidence: continuity procedure, activation criteria, controlled forms/alternate system, trained users, scenario results, timing, manual records, restoration/reconciliation, deviations, and acceptance. Acceptance: critical process continues within justified time; records remain attributable and complete; reconciliation is controlled and independently verified.
Regulatory Alignment: EU GMP Annex 11 Section 16 and Sections 5-7; 21 CFR 11.10(c), where applicable.
Red Flags: Workaround tested as tabletop only; uncontrolled paper/forms; backdated entry; reconciliation count-only; shift handoff loses ownership; recovery exceeds process tolerance.

Red Flags: Review based on curated summaries rather than complete populations; missing cut-off; overdue critical actions omitted; unapproved residual risk; conclusion copied from prior review; material conflicts between source systems and report.

content:

Expected Evidence / Criteria: Current approved inventory, system description, architecture and data-flow diagrams, interface register, CMDB records, hosting and supplier inventory, and reconciliation record. document_title: Top 25 Checklists GxP IT Audit Questions 2026
content:

Phase: Operations & Periodic Review | Domain: Access Management | Topic: Privileged-access recertification | Priority: Critical

Expected Evidence / Criteria: Role catalogue, privilege matrix, named-user export, approval records, recertification results, segregation-of-duties analysis, privileged-session or activity logs, and exception records. Acceptance requires unique identities, least privilege, independence from regulated activity where feasible, timely exception removal, and documented monitoring of unavoidable conflicts.

Red Flags: Analysts or business users hold unrestricted administrator rights; shared admin credentials; unexplained local accounts; self-approval; incomplete technical population; overdue removal; audit logs unavailable or review performed by the same administrator.

metadata.reference: EU GMP Annex 11 Sections 12.1 to 12.4; 21 CFR 11.10(d), 11.10(g), and 11.300 where Part 11 applies; 21 CFR 211.68(b) for drug CGMP systems.

content:
GxP IT Audit Checklist [DA-11-006]: Using an auditor-selected GxP record, demonstrate how audit-trail review identifies, evaluates, and resolves every material creation, modification, deletion, reprocessing, status change, and security event relevant to the quality decision.

Follow-Up Probe: Show the complete event population for the same record directly from the system, including events not displayed in the routine review report, and explain how reviewers detect missing periods, disabled logging, administrator activity, clock differences, or repeated attempts that did not change the final value.
Expected Evidence / Criteria: Audit-trail configuration and risk assessment, review procedure and frequency, raw system-generated event export, reviewer record, linked source record, exception investigation, reviewer training, and periodic verification of audit-trail availability. Red Flags: Audit trail disabled, configurable by conflicted users, incomplete, unintelligible, or unavailable; review limited to final values; missing reasons; unexplained gaps; late review after batch or quality decision; admin actions excluded.

content:

Expected Evidence / Criteria: Signed record, signature manifestation, identity record, authentication configuration, signature and audit logs, record-version history, signature policy, and migration or archive test where relevant. Acceptance requires unique signer control, recorded name/date/time/meaning, permanent linkage, preservation after record lifecycle events, and no shared credentials.
Regulatory Alignment: EU GMP Annex 11 Section 14; 21 CFR 11.50, 11.70, 11.100, 11.200, and 11.300 where Part 11 applies.
Red Flags: Signature not tied to a record version; missing meaning or timestamp; shared credentials; signature can be copied or detached; correction changes signed content without new signature; archive or export loses linkage.

metadata.reference: EU GMP Annex 11 Section 14; 21 CFR 11.50, 11.70, 11.100, 11.200, and 11.300 where Part 11 applies.

content:

Follow-Up Probe: Repeat the retrieval for a record created before the latest major application, database, operating-system, or viewer change and explain how continued readability and meaning were verified when technology changed.

Red Flags: Old records cannot be retrieved promptly; proprietary viewer unavailable; metadata or audit trail omitted; integrity checks never performed; retention period guessed; technology changes not assessed; reliance on an unsupported production environment.

content:
GxP IT Audit Checklist [DA-11-009]: Reconcile the approved inventory of GxP data, metadata, audit trails, configurations, encryption material, and supporting components to the live backup job definitions and demonstrate that the backup scope remains complete after system changes.
Phase: Operations & Periodic Review | Domain: Backup & Disaster Recovery | Topic: Backup population completeness | Priority: Critical
Follow-Up Probe: Select one newly added or changed component and one apparently successful backup; prove that the required content was actually captured and usable rather than merely that the job ended with a success status.
Expected Evidence / Criteria: Data and component inventory, backup architecture and job definitions, retention and immutability settings, job and exception logs, scope reconciliation, change records, and content verification. Acceptance requires complete risk-based scope, monitored failures, protected copies, periodic reconciliation after change, and no unapproved exclusions.
Regulatory Alignment: EU GMP Annex 11 Section 7.2; 21 CFR 211.68(b); 21 CFR 11.10(c) where Part 11 applies; NIST SP 800-53 Rev. 5 control CP-9 as security guidance.
Red Flags: Scope cannot be reconciled; successful status accepted without content verification; audit trails, attachments, or keys excluded; backup changes outside change control; failed jobs aged or suppressed; no protected off-system copy where risk requires it.

metadata.reference: EU GMP Annex 11 Section 7.2; 21 CFR 211.68(b); 21 CFR 11.10(c) where Part 11 applies; NIST SP 800-53 Rev. 5 control CP-9 as security guidance.

content:
GxP IT Audit Checklist [DA-11-010]: Reperform the evidence chain for the last recovery exercise and show that the recovered service met approved recovery time and recovery point objectives while preserving record completeness, data meaning, audit trails, interfaces, security, and business-process usability.

Expected Evidence / Criteria: Approved recovery plan, business impact analysis, RTO and RPO, exercise protocol and raw timestamps, restored-data reconciliation, security and interface checks, business and Quality acceptance, deviations, CAPA, and retest. Acceptance requires objectives achieved or deviations formally assessed with effective remediation and no unexplained data loss.
Regulatory Alignment: EU GMP Annex 11 Sections 7.2 and 16; 21 CFR 211.68(b); NIST SP 800-34 Rev. 1 and NIST SP 800-53 Rev. 5 CP controls as nonbinding guidance.
Red Flags: Restore never tested; test excludes audit trails, interfaces, keys, or business verification; RTO or RPO missed without risk acceptance; failed step omitted; recovered data not reconciled; exercise performed only on unlike infrastructure.

metadata.reference: EU GMP Annex 11 Sections 7.2 and 16; 21 CFR 211.68(b); NIST SP 800-34 Rev. 1 and NIST SP 800-53 Rev. 5 CP controls as nonbinding guidance.

content:
GxP IT Audit Checklist [DA-11-011]: Trace a complete GxP data transfer from authoritative source through middleware to target and downstream report, demonstrating how completeness, accuracy, sequence, attribution, timestamps, and processing status are reconciled in routine operation.

Follow-Up Probe: Use the last failed, duplicate, delayed, partial, or out-of-order transfer and show how the system prevented silent loss or double processing, preserved the original event, controlled reprocessing, and assessed downstream quality impact.
Expected Evidence / Criteria: Interface inventory and data mapping, control totals or acknowledgements, queue and transaction logs, error and retry configuration, reconciliation reports, incident or deviation, reprocessing record, and downstream verification. Regulatory Alignment: EU GMP Annex 11 Sections 5, 7, 8, 9, and 13; 21 CFR 11.10(a), 11.10(e), 11.10(f), and 11.10(h) where Part 11 applies.
Red Flags: No end-to-end identifier or reconciliation; monitoring only transport availability; discarded error messages; uncontrolled replay; duplicate processing; manual correction outside audit trail; source and target totals disagree without investigation.

metadata.reference: EU GMP Annex 11 Sections 5, 7, 8, 9, and 13; 21 CFR 11.10(a), 11.10(e), 11.10(f), and 11.10(h) where Part 11 applies.

content:
GxP IT Audit Checklist [DA-11-012]: Starting from the full alert population, demonstrate how quality-relevant alarms are rationalized, prioritized, routed, acknowledged, investigated, and closed within defined limits, including periods when the primary responder is unavailable.

Expected Evidence / Criteria: Alert catalogue and rationale, thresholds, routing and escalation rules, on-call coverage, raw alert history, acknowledgement and response records, suppression approvals, deviations or incidents, trend review, and effectiveness actions. Regulatory Alignment: EU GMP Annex 11 Sections 1, 11, and 13; 21 CFR 211.68(a); ICH Q9(R1) Sections 3 and 4.
Red Flags: No complete alert population; alert floods or chronic recurrence; critical alert auto-closed; undocumented suppression; response SLA measured without quality impact; blind periods not assessed; no escalation outside business hours.

content:
GxP IT Audit Checklist [DA-11-013]: Show how the periodic evaluation derives and challenges incident, deviation, problem, and service-request trends from complete source populations rather than relying on ticket labels or manually selected quality events.
Phase: Operations & Periodic Review | Domain: Incident & Deviation Management | Topic: Operational event trend inclusion | Priority: High
Follow-Up Probe: Reclassify a sample of low-severity or non-GxP-labelled tickets against the system's intended use and data flows; explain any event that should have triggered a deviation, validation impact assessment, or broader retrospective review.

content:

Red Flags: Root cause stated as human error without systemic analysis; CAPA effectiveness equals task completion; recurrence query undocumented or narrow; repeat events relabelled; no cross-system assessment; failed effectiveness check not reopened.

Red Flags: Deployment population exceeds approved changes; minor changes never aggregated; repeated changes to same control; supplier releases omitted; incidents rise after changes; validation documents and system description not updated.

content:

Phase: Operations & Periodic Review | Domain: Configuration Management | Topic: Production configuration drift | Priority: Critical
Follow-Up Probe: The auditor will select a security, audit-trail, retention, calculation, interface, or workflow parameter from the live system and ask for its last change, approver, test evidence, and current baseline entry.
Expected Evidence / Criteria: Approved baseline, automated or controlled configuration export, comparison report, parameter ownership, authorized change records, temporary-change expiry, drift alerts, investigation, and re-baselining approval. Regulatory Alignment: EU GMP Annex 11 Sections 4.3, 10, and 11; 21 CFR 211.68(b); 21 CFR 11.10(k) where Part 11 applies.
Red Flags: No approved baseline; comparison omits critical parameters; manual snapshots without provenance; unexplained drift; expired feature flags; supplier settings inaccessible; direct changes visible only in audit logs after the fact.

content:

Red Flags: Assets missing from scan scope; risk accepted from CVSS alone; overdue critical vulnerabilities; compensating control asserted without telemetry; exception has no expiry; supplier constraint accepted indefinitely; patch not linked to validation impact.

content:

Acceptance requires coverage of critical events, protected and synchronized logs, tested detections, monitored collection failures, and retained evidence.

Red Flags: Critical log sources not onboarded; clocks not synchronized; administrators can alter logs; collection gaps invisible; alert never tested; retention shorter than record or investigation need; security events not assessed for GxP impact.

metadata.reference: EU GMP Annex 11 Sections 9, 12, and 13; 21 CFR 11.10(e) where Part 11 applies; NIST Cybersecurity Framework 2.0 Detect and Respond functions as nonbinding guidance.

Expected Evidence / Criteria: Quality or service agreement, shared-responsibility matrix, supplier qualification and reassessment, audit or assurance reports with bridge coverage, SLA and control metrics, incident and change notices, exceptions and CAPA, subprocessor inventory, and exit provisions. Regulatory Alignment: EU GMP Annex 11 Sections 3, 7, 11, 12, 13, and 16; 21 CFR 11.10 where applicable remains the regulated user's responsibility; NIST SP 800-53 Rev. 5 SR controls as nonbinding guidance.
Red Flags: Certification treated as complete evidence; expired bridge period; agreement omits GxP records or inspection access; supplier changes not notified; subprocessor unknown; exceptions not assessed; responsibility gap for backup, logs, incidents, or data return.

content:

Expected Evidence / Criteria: Service objectives, capacity model, monitoring data, threshold rationale, forecasts, performance incidents, data-impact checks, scaling or remediation changes, and management review. content:

Expected Evidence / Criteria: Role and curriculum mapping, effective SOPs and work instructions, training assignments and completion, competency assessment, access prerequisites, supervised qualification where needed, retraining after change or deviation, and effectiveness evidence. Red Flags: Access granted before training; training only attendance-based; obsolete procedure; vendor personnel omitted; deviation reveals procedure-content gap; recurring retraining without system or process correction; no competency evidence for critical tasks.

content:

Phase: Operations & Periodic Review | Domain: Business Continuity | Topic: Manual workaround control | Priority: Critical

Expected Evidence / Criteria: Approved continuity procedure, activation criteria, controlled forms or alternate system, role and contact lists, exercise records, source and reconciliation logs, deviation handling, Quality and business acceptance, and improvement actions. Red Flags: Workaround untested or only tabletop; uncontrolled blank forms or spreadsheets; no unique identifiers; backlog exceeds capacity; duplicate prevention absent; reconciliation incomplete; exercise ignores compound failure or long outage.

content:

Expected Evidence / Criteria: Periodic-review evidence package, residual-risk register, decision criteria, dissent or challenge records, accountable approvals, restrictions and interim controls, funded actions, escalation and suspension triggers, and follow-up monitoring. content:

metadata.reference: EU GMP Annex 11 Sections 4.3 and 10; 21 CFR 11.10(k); 21 CFR 211.68(b).

GxP IT Audit Checklist [DA-12-007]: Reconcile the approved change to the exact repository commit, peer review, automated build, dependency set, signed or hashed artifact, deployment execution, and live production version.
Phase: Change & Configuration Management | Domain: Software Configuration Management | Topic: Commit-build-deployment provenance | Priority: Critical
Follow-Up Probe: Demonstrate that the artifact deployed to production could not have been modified after test approval and that a rebuild from the approved source would produce an equivalent artifact; explain any manual step.

content:

Follow-Up Probe: Remove the assumption that the final value or batch result was acceptable and explain what evidence independently bounds the event's impact population and justifies the chosen severity and Quality escalation.
Expected Evidence / Criteria: Classification matrix, intended-use and risk records, event facts, affected functions and data, initial and revised classifications, escalation timestamps, Quality assessment, and rationale. Acceptance requires conservative classification under uncertainty, timely escalation, and revision as evidence develops.

Red Flags: Classification based on outage duration alone; final acceptable result used to dismiss potential impact; Quality notified late; uncertainty not considered; affected population guessed; severity downgraded before evidence.

content:

Phase: Incident, Problem & Deviation Management | Domain: Incident Detection & Response | Topic: Detection and notification timeliness | Priority: Critical
Follow-Up Probe: Identify the earliest evidence that existed before the official start time and show why monitoring, a user, or a supplier did not recognize it; quantify records and decisions created during the undetected interval.
Expected Evidence / Criteria: Native system and monitoring logs, alert routing, acknowledgement, ITSM timeline, communication, escalation criteria, Quality notification, and affected-transaction analysis. Acceptance requires an evidence-based start time, justified response intervals, and impact assessment covering the full exposure window.
Regulatory Alignment: EU GMP Annex 11 Section 13; ICH Q9(R1) Sections 4.3 and 4.4; NIST SP 800-61 Rev. 3 as nonbinding incident-response guidance.
Red Flags: Official start equals ticket time despite earlier evidence; alert unacknowledged; after-hours gap; Quality escalation delayed; exposure window not used for sampling; SLA met only by redefining start time.

Phase: Incident, Problem & Deviation Management | Domain: Incident Response | Topic: Containment and evidence preservation | Priority: Critical
Follow-Up Probe: Show each restart, rollback, log rotation, cache clear, file deletion, account disablement, or configuration change performed during response and prove that evidence was captured first or the loss was explicitly assessed.
Expected Evidence / Criteria: Containment decision record, forensic or evidence-preservation procedure, native logs and snapshots, chain of custody where appropriate, responder actions, emergency changes, backup copies, and Quality oversight. Acceptance requires preserved originals, attributable actions, controlled access, and documented limitations where evidence was lost.
Regulatory Alignment: EU GMP Annex 11 Sections 7, 9, 10, 12, and 13; 21 CFR 11.10(c) and 11.10(e); NIST SP 800-61 Rev. 3 as nonbinding guidance.
Red Flags: System wiped or restarted before capture; logs overwritten; response actions use shared account; no original evidence; chain of custody unclear; emergency changes undocumented; evidence gap dismissed without impact assessment.

Follow-Up Probe: Show the query or reconstruction logic that defines the affected population, then challenge it with records created immediately before and after the window, queued or cached transactions, replicas, reports, exports, and manual workarounds.
Expected Evidence / Criteria: Exposure-window rationale, function and data-flow analysis, reproducible population query, record list, downstream-use mapping, field and metadata checks, batch or quality impact, Quality disposition, and independent review. Regulatory Alignment: EU GMP Annex 11 Sections 5, 7, 9, and 13; FDA Data Integrity and Compliance With Drug CGMP Q&A; PIC/S PI 041-1; 21 CFR 211.192 where applicable.
Red Flags: Population derived from ticket estimate; queued or downstream data omitted; boundary not tested; released records not assessed; final values checked without metadata or history; query not reproducible; Quality disposition absent.

Expected Evidence / Criteria: Security timeline, identities and assets affected, privilege and attack-path analysis, native and centralized logs, configuration and file-integrity checks, record and audit-trail review, data exfiltration assessment, GxP impact, recovery, and Quality approval. content:
GxP IT Audit Checklist [DA-13-012]: Demonstrate how the investigation distinguished root cause, contributing causes, detection-control failure, and organizational or process conditions using evidence that can reproduce and explain the observed event.
Phase: Incident, Problem & Deviation Management | Domain: Problem Management | Topic: Evidence-based root cause | Priority: Critical
Follow-Up Probe: Present the strongest competing causal hypothesis, show the discriminating evidence used to reject it, and explain which facts remain uncertain and how that uncertainty changes corrective action or monitoring.
Expected Evidence / Criteria: Problem statement, complete timeline, evidence catalogue, technical and process analysis, hypotheses, experiments or reproduction, causal chain, contributing factors, detection failure, uncertainty, cross-functional review, and approved conclusion. Acceptance requires evidence sufficient to explain occurrence and recurrence and actions addressing the causal mechanism.
Regulatory Alignment: EU GMP Annex 11 Section 13; ICH Q9(R1) Sections 4.2, 4.3, and 5; PIC/S PI 041-1 Sections 6 and 9.
Red Flags: Root cause is 'human error,' 'software glitch,' or 'network issue' without causal evidence; competing hypotheses absent; event not reproducible or bounded; detection failure ignored; uncertainty concealed; supplier statement accepted verbatim.

content:
GxP IT Audit Checklist [DA-13-013]: Show how the investigation searched for recurrence and analogous failure across alternate error codes, ticket categories, sites, versions, interfaces, manual corrections, supplier services, and near misses.
Phase: Incident, Problem & Deviation Management | Domain: Problem Management | Topic: Recurrence and similar-event search | Priority: High
Follow-Up Probe: Rerun the search using broader technical and business synonyms and compare the newly found population with the one used to conclude that the event was isolated.
Expected Evidence / Criteria: Documented search strategy, systems and time window, query terms and logic, results, clustering method, applicability decisions, historical impact review, and CAPA scope. Acceptance requires reproducible, sufficiently broad search and escalation when similar events are identified.
Regulatory Alignment: EU GMP Annex 11 Sections 11 and 13; ICH Q9(R1) Sections 4.3 and 4.6; PIC/S PI 041-1 Sections 6 and 9.
Red Flags: Search limited to exact error code or same system; query not retained; low-severity and supplier cases excluded; similar events relabelled; historical product or data impact not revisited; systemic pattern declared isolated.

content:

Phase: Incident, Problem & Deviation Management | Domain: Human Factors & Quality Culture | Topic: Human-error causal challenge | Priority: High
Follow-Up Probe: Place a competent person unfamiliar with the event in the same controlled scenario and show whether the process and system reliably lead to the correct action without relying on memory or informal knowledge.
Expected Evidence / Criteria: Task analysis, procedure and training content, competence, workload and environment, access and UI controls, system checks, supervision, interviews, recurrence data, and redesigned controls. Acceptance requires systemic assessment and CAPA beyond retraining where the process permits predictable error.
Regulatory Alignment: EU GMP Annex 11 Sections 1, 2, 6, 12, and 13; 21 CFR 11.10(f), 11.10(g), and 11.10(i); PIC/S PI 041-1 Section 6.
Red Flags: Root cause ends at operator mistake; CAPA is retraining only; procedure ambiguous; system permits invalid sequence; workload or incentives ignored; same error recurs; punitive response discourages reporting. Finding trigger: evidence is missing, unapproved, incomplete, inconsistent, or cannot be reproduced for the auditor-selected sample.

content:
GxP IT Audit Checklist [DA-13-016]: Establish a defensible common timeline across application, database, operating system, identity, interface, cloud, monitoring, supplier, and quality records, accounting for time zones, daylight-saving changes, clock drift, latency, and log buffering.

content:

content:
GxP IT Audit Checklist [DA-13-020]: Map each confirmed root and contributing cause, detection failure, and scope weakness to a corrective or preventive action and demonstrate that the action changes the causal mechanism rather than only documenting or retraining around it.
Phase: Incident, Problem & Deviation Management | Domain: CAPA Management | Topic: Cause-to-action traceability | Priority: Critical
Follow-Up Probe: Remove the proposed training and procedure actions from the plan and show which technical, process, governance, or supplier control prevents recurrence; explain any causal factor left without an action.
Expected Evidence / Criteria: Approved causal analysis, cause-to-CAPA map, action design and owner, risk priority, interim controls, technical and process implementation, cross-system applicability, validation or change records, due dates, and Quality approval. Acceptance requires full causal coverage and proportionate preventive action.
Regulatory Alignment: EU GMP Annex 11 Section 13; ICH Q9(R1) Sections 4.4 to 4.6; PIC/S PI 041-1 Sections 6 and 9.

content:

Red Flags: Effectiveness equals completion; observation period too short; query exact-match only; near misses excluded; source data incomplete; check performed by action owner without independent review; failed result not reopened.

content:
GxP IT Audit Checklist [DA-14-001]: Reconstruct the approved retirement decision and demonstrate how business, Quality, records, security, privacy, legal, supplier, continuity, and technical owners agreed the system boundary, timing, successor capability, retained obligations, and exit criteria.
Phase: Decommissioning, Data Retention & Migration | Domain: Decommissioning Governance | Topic: Retirement decision and scope | Priority: Critical
Follow-Up Probe: Identify the strongest dependency or regulated use arguing against shutdown and show the objective evidence that it was replaced, archived, risk-controlled, or formally accepted before the final irreversible step.
Expected Evidence / Criteria: Approved retirement business case, GxP and regulatory assessment, scope and dependency analysis, accountable owners, successor and archive decisions, risk assessment, legal and retention review, exit criteria, timeline, and Quality approval. Acceptance requires complete scope, no unresolved critical dependency, and explicit control of retained obligations.
Regulatory Alignment: EU GMP Annex 11 lifecycle principle and Sections 1, 4.3, 7, 16, and 17; ICH Q9(R1) Sections 3 and 4.
Red Flags: Retirement approved by project or IT alone; scope differs from live inventory; open deviations, legal holds, or regulated uses omitted; exit criteria vague; irreversible shutdown scheduled before evidence completion; Quality approval absent.

content:
GxP IT Audit Checklist [DA-14-002]: Discover and reconcile every upstream and downstream interface, scheduled job, report, device, directory group, service account, database, file share, integration token, monitoring rule, backup, and business process that depends on the retiring system.
Phase: Decommissioning, Data Retention & Migration | Domain: Configuration & Dependency Management | Topic: Complete dependency inventory | Priority: Critical
Follow-Up Probe: The auditor will select a dependency from live network, scheduler, identity, or log telemetry that is absent from the retirement inventory and ask how its data, process, and continuity impact was assessed.
Expected Evidence / Criteria: Approved system description, CMDB, network and API discovery, scheduler and interface inventories, database and storage catalogues, account and token lists, monitoring and backup configurations, dependency owners, and reconciliation. Acceptance requires all observed dependencies resolved and no unexplained live traffic or scheduled activity before shutdown.
Regulatory Alignment: EU GMP Annex 11 Sections 4.3, 5, 10, 16, and 17; 21 CFR 11.10(a) and 11.10(k) where Part 11 applies.
Red Flags: Inventory copied from obsolete diagram; live traffic after cut-off; low-frequency jobs omitted; local files or reports unknown; service accounts remain active; shared database dependency unresolved; replacement not owner-accepted.

content:

Expected Evidence / Criteria: Data and record catalogue, record definitions, data models, file and object stores, audit-trail and signature schema, report inventory, hybrid-record map, owners, retention rules, and disposition decisions. Acceptance requires complete lifecycle context and explicit treatment of nonstandard and hidden record components.

Red Flags: Inventory limited to PDFs or reports; raw data, metadata, audit trails, attachments, or rejected records omitted; record owner unknown; hybrid components separated; disposition inferred rather than approved. content:

content:
GxP IT Audit Checklist [DA-14-010]: Demonstrate how every migration exception is uniquely identified, preserved, investigated, risk-assessed, corrected under control, independently verified, reprocessed once, and included in final reconciliation.
Phase: Decommissioning, Data Retention & Migration | Domain: Migration Exceptions | Topic: Rejected and quarantined records | Priority: Critical

content:
GxP IT Audit Checklist [DA-14-011]: Demonstrate that the migration or archive preserves every required audit event, prior value, new value, actor, timestamp, action, reason, record linkage, and review status in an intelligible and reviewable form.
Phase: Decommissioning, Data Retention & Migration | Domain: Audit Trail | Topic: Audit-trail preservation | Priority: Critical
Follow-Up Probe: Compare a raw source audit-trail export with the target or archive for events created by administrators, failed actions, deletions, configuration changes, and periods where user-facing reports normally filter events.
Expected Evidence / Criteria: Source audit schema and configuration, full event population, mapping, transformation rules, target or archive events, intelligible display and electronic copy, event and record linkage, review capability, reconciliation, and access control. Acceptance requires complete history and no loss of meaning or reviewability.
Regulatory Alignment: EU GMP Annex 11 Sections 9 and 17; 21 CFR 11.10(e); FDA Data Integrity Q&A; PIC/S PI 041-1.
Red Flags: Only audit-trail PDF retained; prior values or reasons omitted; admin or failed events filtered; record linkage broken; timestamps transformed without trace; audit events not searchable or reviewable; source destroyed before reconciliation.

content:

Regulatory Alignment: EU GMP Annex 11 Sections 14 and 17; 21 CFR 11.50, 11.70, 11.100, and 11.200.

Finding trigger: evidence is missing, unapproved, incomplete, inconsistent, or cannot be reproduced for the auditor-selected sample.

content:

Phase: Decommissioning, Data Retention & Migration | Domain: Metadata & Hybrid Records | Topic: Time, attachments, and contextual integrity | Priority: High

Red Flags: Timestamps normalized without original zone; attachments matched by filename only; links broken; unsupported files skipped; annotations omitted; paper-electronic index lost; duplicate files overwrite; hash or size not reconciled.

Acceptance requires preserved association, meaning, chronology, and integrity.

Follow-Up Probe: Select a record created near the cutover boundary and show how duplicate creation, update in the wrong system, clock difference, and delayed interface delivery were detected and reconciled.
Expected Evidence / Criteria: Cutover plan, freeze and authority matrix, synchronized timeline, user and interface controls, queue and backlog inventory, communication, boundary reconciliation, duplicate checks, deviations, and acceptance. Acceptance requires one unambiguous authoritative record for every interval and resolved transition exceptions.
Regulatory Alignment: EU GMP Annex 11 Sections 4.8, 5, 7, 9, 10, and 16; 21 CFR 11.10(a), 11.10(e), and 11.10(f).
Red Flags: Authority rule unclear; both systems writable; boundary times differ; late queue omitted; user access not aligned to freeze; duplicate records; manual backlog unreconciled; source changed after final extract.

Phase: Decommissioning, Data Retention & Migration | Domain: Validation / Assurance | Topic: Archive and migration verification | Priority: Critical
Follow-Up Probe: Show the highest-risk requirement with reduced or no scripted testing and demonstrate why other objective evidence provides sufficient assurance; then present the last failed test and its full resolution chain.
Expected Evidence / Criteria: Validation or assurance plan, risk and requirement trace, test strategy, controlled tools and environments, positive and negative tests, raw execution evidence, deviations and defects, reconciliation, retrieval and recovery tests, summary, and Quality approval. content:

Phase: Decommissioning, Data Retention & Migration | Domain: Archiving Operations | Topic: Retrieval, readability, and inspection copies | Priority: Critical
Follow-Up Probe: Repeat the retrieval for the oldest cohort and for a record created before a major format, viewer, operating-system, or archive-platform change; explain every manual or specialist step required.
Expected Evidence / Criteria: Archive search and retrieval procedure, access authorization, native or preserved representation, metadata and audit history, signature linkage, copies, integrity verification, retrieval SLA, platform-change tests, and exception handling. Acceptance requires reproducible timely retrieval with complete meaning and no dependence on the retired production environment.
Regulatory Alignment: EU GMP Annex 11 Sections 7.1, 8, 9, 14, and 17; 21 CFR 11.10(b) and 11.10(c).
Red Flags: Retrieval requires retired application; oldest records unreadable; metadata or audit trail absent; signatures unresolved; electronic copy proprietary or incomplete; manual reconstruction undocumented; SLA missed without action.

content:

Phase: Decommissioning, Data Retention & Migration | Domain: Archiving Operations | Topic: Ongoing archive integrity and technology refresh | Priority: Critical
Follow-Up Probe: Show the last failed integrity, retrieval, or compatibility check, identify every potentially affected object, and demonstrate correction, retrospective scope, retest, and trend action.
Expected Evidence / Criteria: Periodic-check procedure and risk-based frequency, complete archive population, integrity and retrieval results, access and security reviews, backup and recovery tests, capacity and lifecycle monitoring, exceptions, remediation, refresh plan, and Quality review. Acceptance requires complete monitored coverage and effective response to failures.
Regulatory Alignment: EU GMP Annex 11 Sections 7.1, 7.2, 11, 16, and 17; 21 CFR 11.10(c); NIST SP 800-53 Rev. 5 CP and SI controls as nonbinding guidance.
Red Flags: Only storage availability monitored; integrity check samples too narrow; failed object scope unknown; viewer lifecycle ignored; no restore test; archive exceptions aged; refresh occurs after support expiry; Quality not reviewing trends.

content:

Phase: Decommissioning, Data Retention & Migration | Domain: Access Management & Security | Topic: Post-retirement archive access | Priority: Critical

Expected Evidence / Criteria: Archive role design, named-user and service-account populations, approvals and reviews, leaver cleanup, privileged-access restrictions, immutable or write-protected controls, access and export logs, alerts, and exceptions. Red Flags: Project accounts remain; archive access not reviewed; shared administrator; write access unnecessary; exports unlogged; former supplier access active; lower storage or backup layer omitted; leaver process excludes archive.

content:
GxP IT Audit Checklist [DA-14-019]: Demonstrate how encryption keys, signing certificates, trust chains, secrets, tokens, algorithms, and recovery material needed to access or verify retained records remain available, protected, attributable, and replaceable throughout retention.
Phase: Decommissioning, Data Retention & Migration | Domain: Cryptographic Lifecycle | Topic: Long-term keys, certificates, and secrets | Priority: Critical
Follow-Up Probe: Simulate loss or expiry of the primary key or certificate and show the tested recovery, escrow, re-encryption, verification, and audit path without weakening access control or losing proof of historical signature validity.
Expected Evidence / Criteria: Cryptographic dependency inventory, ownership, key and certificate lifecycle, escrow and backup, algorithm and expiry monitoring, recovery or re-encryption tests, access controls and logs, destruction rules, and technology-refresh plan. Regulatory Alignment: EU GMP Annex 11 Sections 7, 12, 16, and 17; 21 CFR 11.10(c) and 11.10(d); NIST SP 800-53 Rev. 5 SC and CP controls as nonbinding guidance.
Red Flags: Key owner unknown; single key copy; certificate expiry unmonitored; recovery untested; vendor key unavailable after contract; re-encryption changes provenance without control; destruction occurs before retention ends. Finding trigger: evidence is missing, unapproved, incomplete, inconsistent, or cannot be reproduced for the auditor-selected sample.

document_title: Top 25 Checklists GxP IT Audit Questions 2026
content:
GxP IT Audit Checklist [DA-14-020]: Demonstrate how personal data is minimized and deleted or anonymized when no longer lawfully required while regulated records, legal holds, audit trails, and evidentiary integrity remain protected.
Phase: Decommissioning, Data Retention & Migration | Domain: Data Privacy | Topic: Retention-limited deletion and minimization | Priority: High
Follow-Up Probe: Select one deletion request or expired personal-data class that intersects a GxP record and show the legal basis, field-level disposition, propagation to replicas and exports, and proof that the retained record remains complete and meaningful.
Expected Evidence / Criteria: Data inventory and classification, lawful-basis and retention mapping, minimization and deletion rules, legal-hold checks, field-level design, anonymization validation where used, propagation to archives, replicas, and suppliers, execution logs, exceptions, and approvals. Acceptance requires lawful, consistent, and auditable disposition without loss of required GxP evidence.
Regulatory Alignment: GDPR Articles 5, 17, 25, 30, and 32 where applicable; EU GMP Annex 11 Sections 7, 9, and 17; applicable predicate-rule retention requirements.
Red Flags: All data retained indefinitely as GxP; deletion breaks audit trail or attribution; replicas and supplier copies ignored; anonymization reversible or unvalidated; legal hold not checked; deletion evidence unavailable.

document_title: Top 25 Checklists GxP IT Audit Questions 2026
content:
GxP IT Audit Checklist [DA-14-021]: Account for every backup, replica, snapshot, export, staging area, test copy, disaster-recovery environment, and removable medium and demonstrate its approved retention, access restriction, migration, expiry, or destruction.
Phase: Decommissioning, Data Retention & Migration | Domain: Backup & Data Disposition | Topic: Residual copies and backup retirement | Priority: Critical
Follow-Up Probe: Select a copy outside the primary production account or data center and prove who can restore it, which keys and software it needs, when it expires, how legal holds apply, and how destruction is verified.
Expected Evidence / Criteria: Copy topology and inventory, backup and snapshot catalogues, DR and test environments, exports and media register, retention and hold rules, access, key dependencies, expiration or destruction jobs, certificates, and reconciliation. Acceptance requires complete accounting and no restorable uncontrolled copy.
Regulatory Alignment: EU GMP Annex 11 Sections 7.2, 12, 16, and 17; 21 CFR 211.68(b); GDPR Articles 5 and 32 where personal data apply; NIST SP 800-88 Rev. 2 as nonbinding sanitization guidance.
Red Flags: Copy inventory incomplete; snapshots in personal or supplier account; no expiry; restore access retained broadly; legal hold not propagated; test copies forgotten; destruction claimed without verification; keys persist after data destruction.

content:
GxP IT Audit Checklist [DA-14-022]: Demonstrate the controlled sequence used to stop interfaces, jobs, APIs, file transfers, notifications, monitoring, user accounts, service accounts, certificates, tokens, remote support, and network routes without losing late data or leaving unauthorized pathways.
Phase: Decommissioning, Data Retention & Migration | Domain: Interface & Identity Shutdown | Topic: Orderly termination of technical pathways | Priority: Critical
Follow-Up Probe: Show live telemetry after the claimed shutdown and explain any authentication attempt, network connection, scheduled execution, queue item, file arrival, or data write, including how it was contained and reconciled.
Expected Evidence / Criteria: Shutdown plan and dependency order, cut-off and queue reconciliation, interface partner confirmation, job and account inventories, revocation and route changes, monitoring period, live telemetry, exceptions, and approvals. Acceptance requires zero unresolved traffic, active identity, or late data after final cut-off.
Regulatory Alignment: EU GMP Annex 11 Sections 5, 10, 12, 13, 16, and 17; 21 CFR 11.10(d), 11.10(g), and 11.300 where Part 11 applies.
Red Flags: Interfaces stopped before queues reconcile; service accounts active; certificates or tokens valid; late files discarded; network route remains; monitoring removed before observation period; partner not notified; live writes after shutdown.

content:
GxP IT Audit Checklist [DA-14-023]: Trace the supplier exit from contract obligations through complete data and metadata return, format usability, transition support, subprocessor coverage, access revocation, residual-copy destruction, evidence availability, and final service termination.
Phase: Decommissioning, Data Retention & Migration | Domain: Supplier Exit Management | Topic: Data return, continuity, and destruction | Priority: Critical
