content:
GxP IT Audit Checklist [DA-14-025]: Demonstrate that final decommissioning approval was based on complete migration or archive acceptance, reconciled records, resolved exceptions, terminated dependencies and access, governed residual copies, preserved inspection capability, updated inventories, and explicit long-term ownership.
Phase: Decommissioning, Data Retention & Migration | Domain: Decommissioning Closure | Topic: Final report and residual obligations | Priority: Critical
Follow-Up Probe: Choose the strongest unresolved exception or retained dependency at closure and show who accepted the residual risk, how it is monitored, when it expires, what event triggers reopening, and who funds corrective action after the project team disbands.
Expected Evidence / Criteria: Final decommissioning report, evidence index, source and target reconciliation, deviations and CAPA, retrieval and recovery acceptance, access and interface termination, supplier exit, backup and asset disposition, CMDB and inventory updates, residual-risk register, long-term owner and review schedule, and Quality approval. Acceptance requires no hidden critical dependency and durable governance after project closure.
Regulatory Alignment: EU GMP Annex 11 lifecycle principle and Sections 4.2, 7, 10, 12, 16, and 17; 21 CFR 11.10(b) to 11.10(e) where Part 11 applies; ICH Q9(R1) Sections 4.5 and 4.6.
Red Flags: Final approval predates evidence; open critical exceptions hidden; archive owner or budget absent; access or interface still active; inventory not updated; residual risk has no expiry or monitoring; source destroyed before verified retrieval; project disbands with open CAPA.

document_title: Top 25 Checklists GxP IT Audit Questions 2026
content:
GxP IT Audit Checklist [DA-01-001]: Walk through the proposed intended use, the patient, product-quality and data decisions it will support, and the evidence used to draw the GxP system boundary before funding was approved.
Phase: 01 Concept Business Case | Domain: Governance | Topic: GxP intended use and system boundary | Priority: Critical
Follow-Up Probe: Reconcile the business-case boundary with the process map, data-flow diagram, application inventory and any functions described as merely administrative; explain every mismatch.
Expected Evidence / Criteria: Approved concept statement; end-to-end process and context diagrams; preliminary GxP assessment; named process/system/data owners; QA approval. Boundaries include interfaces, infrastructure, reports, records and supporting services and are internally consistent.
Regulatory Alignment: Binding: 21 CFR 11.1 and 211.68; Official EU GMP guideline: Annex 11 Principle and §§1, 4.3; Guidance: WHO §§4-5 and 11.1.
Red Flags: No approved intended use; boundary omits reports, interfaces or infrastructure; GxP classification conflicts with process use; QA engaged only after funding.

Follow-Up Probe: Choose a record the business case labels non-GxP and demonstrate why no batch, laboratory, complaint, stability, training or quality decision relies on it, including downstream exports.

Red Flags: Applicability based only on technology label; no predicate-record mapping; enforcement discretion treated as exemption; markets or retention laws omitted.

content:
GxP IT Audit Checklist [DA-01-003]: Describe the proposed data lifecycle from first capture through processing, review, reporting, retention and destruction, and show where the concept explicitly protects attributable, legible, contemporaneous, original, accurate, complete, consistent, enduring and available data.
Phase: 01 Concept Business Case | Domain: Data Integrity | Topic: Data lifecycle and ALCOA+ concept | Priority: Critical
Follow-Up Probe: Trace one value that is transformed more than once and identify the original data, metadata, excluded or invalidated values, reviewer visibility and final record at every stage.
Expected Evidence / Criteria: Preliminary data-flow and lifecycle map; data criticality register; ALCOA+ assessment; proposed technical/procedural controls; QA-approved gaps and funding. All transformations and review points are visible.
Regulatory Alignment: Binding: 21 CFR 211.68 and 211.180/188/194; Official EU GMP guideline: Chapter 4 Principle and §4.1; Guidance: MHRA §§3-5 and PIC/S §5.
Red Flags: Only final reports considered records; metadata/intermediate data absent; manual transcriptions not mapped; ALCOA+ cited without funded controls.

content:
GxP IT Audit Checklist [DA-01-004]: Demonstrate how the concept distinguishes source data, raw data, metadata, official records, convenience copies and hybrid components, and how the authoritative version will be identified during an inspection.
Phase: 01 Concept Business Case | Domain: Records Management | Topic: Authoritative record and raw-data inventory | Priority: Critical
Follow-Up Probe: For a proposed printout or PDF, show why it preserves—or does not need—the dynamic data and metadata required to reconstruct the GxP activity.
Expected Evidence / Criteria: Preliminary record catalogue; record-of-truth decisions; hybrid-system map; dynamic/static assessment; true-copy strategy; ownership and inspection retrieval requirements, approved by QA and records management.

Red Flags: Final output declared the sole record without rationale; raw data/metadata ownership unclear; hybrid links absent; inspector-copy capability unfunded.

document_title: Top 25 Checklists GxP IT Audit Questions 2026
content:
GxP IT Audit Checklist [DA-01-005]: Explain how preliminary risk assessment differentiated patient-safety, product-quality and data-integrity harm, and how that analysis changed scope, controls, budget or schedule.
Phase: 01 Concept Business Case | Domain: Quality Risk Management | Topic: Data and process criticality | Priority: Critical
Follow-Up Probe: Present the highest-rated data element and the highest-rated workflow; show the causal chain to harm and why a lower-rated neighboring item received less control.
Expected Evidence / Criteria: Approved risk method; hazard statements; severity/probability/detectability rationale where used; critical data/process list; control decisions; residual-risk owners. Formality and evidence are proportionate to uncertainty and risk.
Regulatory Alignment: Guidance: ICH Q9(R1) §§3-5; Official EU GMP guideline: Annex 11 §1; Guidance: PIC/S §§5.3-5.6 and WHO §5.
Red Flags: Generic risk statements; unexplained low scores; detectability credited without a control; high risk accepted by project management alone; risk used to waive a binding requirement. Finding trigger: evidence is missing, unapproved, incomplete, inconsistent, or cannot be reproduced for the auditor-selected sample.

metadata.expected_evidence: Approved risk method; hazard statements; severity/probability/detectability rationale where used; critical data/process list; control decisions; residual-risk owners. Formality and evidence are proportionate to uncertainty and risk.

content:
GxP IT Audit Checklist [DA-01-006]: Show how the business case funds documented evidence that the system will remain fit for intended use across configuration, testing, release, operation, change and retirement.
Phase: 01 Concept Business Case | Domain: Validation Strategy | Topic: Lifecycle assurance and validation funding | Priority: Critical
Follow-Up Probe: Identify an assurance activity removed for cost or speed and demonstrate, through risk and alternative evidence, why confidence in the intended use was not reduced.
Expected Evidence / Criteria: Concept validation plan; lifecycle deliverables; risk-based assurance rationale; independent review; resource/skill estimates; environments and tools; acceptance gates; operational validation budget. Drug-GMP strategy meets predicate rules and Annex 11/15; device-only CSA is clearly scoped.
Regulatory Alignment: Binding: 21 CFR 11.10(a) and 211.68; Official EU GMP guideline: Annex 11 §§1, 4 and Annex 15 §§1-3; FDA guidance (nonbinding, device QMS scope only): CSA §III and V.
Red Flags: Validation is a single pre-go-live test; no operational-state funding; CSA used to waive drug-GMP controls; estimates ignore interfaces/migration; QA approval not budgeted.

metadata.expected_evidence: Concept validation plan; lifecycle deliverables; risk-based assurance rationale; independent review; resource/skill estimates; environments and tools; acceptance gates; operational validation budget. Drug-GMP strategy meets predicate rules and Annex 11/15; device-only CSA is clearly scoped.

content:
GxP IT Audit Checklist [DA-02-002]: Trace each intended use and predicate-record obligation into specific URS requirements for creation, review, approval, retention, retrieval and inspection, including functions outside the primary application boundary.
Phase: 02 URS | Domain: Regulatory Compliance | Topic: Intended use, predicate records and scope traceability | Priority: Critical
Follow-Up Probe: Choose one downstream report used for release or quality disposition and demonstrate the requirement chain back to its source data, metadata, reviewer and governing record obligation.
Expected Evidence / Criteria: Intended-use statement; GxP/Part 11 assessment; predicate-rule matrix; record/signature inventory; bidirectional concept-to-URS traceability; system-boundary diagram. Every regulated use and record has testable requirements or approved rationale.

Red Flags: Part 11 assessment not linked to requirements; reports/exports omitted from boundary; predicate records unnamed; requirements cover storage but not review, retrieval or inspection.

document_title: Top 25 Checklists GxP IT Audit Questions 2026
content:
GxP IT Audit Checklist [DA-02-003]: Show how critical process steps, data elements, metadata, calculations, reports and configurations are identified in the URS and linked to preliminary risk decisions without using priority labels as a substitute for compliance.
Phase: 02 URS | Domain: Quality Risk Management | Topic: Critical function and data classification | Priority: Critical
Follow-Up Probe: Take a requirement marked low priority that handles a critical identifier or status and reconcile the rating with its downstream use and failure consequence.
Expected Evidence / Criteria: Critical data/process inventory; requirement attributes for GxP impact and criticality; risk references; rationale and owners; rules separating business priority from quality risk; approved traceability.

Red Flags: MoSCoW priority used as risk; metadata/configuration not classified; low ratings lack causal rationale; criticality differs between URS and data inventory; mandatory controls marked optional.

content:
GxP IT Audit Checklist [DA-02-004]: Demonstrate how each URS statement expresses an observable outcome, boundary condition and acceptance criterion that can establish fitness for intended use rather than merely repeating policy words such as secure, compliant or user-friendly.
Phase: 02 URS | Domain: Validation Strategy | Topic: Testable requirements and acceptance criteria | Priority: Critical
Follow-Up Probe: Select three high-risk requirements and show the positive, negative, boundary and failure-recovery evidence that could objectively prove each one before design is known.
Expected Evidence / Criteria: Requirement quality checklist; measurable acceptance criteria; risk/test attributes; traceability conventions; verification method and responsible reviewer; approved ambiguity resolutions. Drug-GMP assurance is grounded in predicate rules/Annex 11, not a device-only CSA waiver.
Regulatory Alignment: Binding: 21 CFR 11.10(a) and 211.68; Official EU GMP guideline: Annex 11 §§4.1, 4.4, 4.7 and Annex 15 §2; FDA guidance (nonbinding, device QMS scope only): CSA §V.A.
Red Flags: Subjective adjectives without measures; multiple controls bundled into one requirement; negative/error cases absent; acceptance delegated solely to supplier; CSA cited outside device scope to reduce evidence.

Drug-GMP assurance is grounded in predicate rules/Annex 11, not a device-only CSA waiver.

document_title: Top 25 Checklists GxP IT Audit Questions 2026
content:
GxP IT Audit Checklist [DA-02-005]: Describe the URS requirements that preserve the full record context—originator, event time, system time, units, status, method, version, reason and relationships—from first capture through every transformation.
Phase: 02 URS | Domain: Data Integrity | Topic: Metadata, contemporaneity and ALCOA+ requirements | Priority: Critical
Follow-Up Probe: Choose one displayed value and show every metadata element needed to reconstruct who did what, when and under which configuration; identify where the URS requires each element to be retained and reviewable.
Expected Evidence / Criteria: Data/metadata dictionary; ALCOA+ requirement mapping; time-zone and clock rules; contemporaneous capture; provenance and lineage; completeness rules; review and retention requirements; controlled rationale for any excluded metadata.
Regulatory Alignment: Binding: 21 CFR 11.10(e) and 211.188/194; Official EU GMP guideline: Chapter 4 Principle and §§4.7-4.9; Guidance: FDA DI Q1, MHRA §§6.1-6.7 and WHO §4.
Red Flags: Only visible fields specified; event and entry times conflated; time zone absent; metadata may be overwritten; lineage ends at report; ALCOA+ appears only in a generic preamble.

content:

content:
GxP IT Audit Checklist [DA-02-008]: Demonstrate how the URS specifies unique attribution, role-based least privilege, joiner/mover/leaver timing, periodic review and ownership for human, service, interface and robotic identities.
Phase: 02 URS | Domain: Access & Security | Topic: Unique identity and least-privilege requirements | Priority: Critical
Follow-Up Probe: Map the full lifecycle of one external contractor and one nonhuman account, including creation approval, credential storage, allowed transactions, monitoring, review and revocation.
Expected Evidence / Criteria: Identity classes; authentication requirements; role/permission matrix; account lifecycle SLAs; service-account owner and secret controls; periodic review; inactive/terminated lockout; federation dependencies; traceable approvals.

content:

content:
GxP IT Audit Checklist [DA-02-011]: Walk through each critical workflow and show how the URS requires permitted sequence, prerequisite evidence, role authority, status transitions and prevention or controlled override of out-of-order processing.

content:

Red Flags: No unit/source validation; rejected values vanish; corrections overwrite originals; device identity not recorded; data-entry time substituted for event time; errors can be bypassed without reason.

content:
GxP IT Audit Checklist [DA-02-013]: Show how each interface requirement defines source and target records, field-level transformations, units/precision, identifiers, sequencing, acknowledgements, retries, duplicate control, reconciliation and retention of transmission evidence.

Follow-Up Probe: Create a partial payload followed by retry and out-of-order delivery; explain how the requirements prevent duplicate or inconsistent records and make unresolved differences visible to a named owner.
Expected Evidence / Criteria: Interface requirements/specification inputs; source-to-target mapping; transformation rules; control totals; error queues; retry/idempotency; time synchronization; monitoring/alerts; reconciliation frequency/owner; log retention.

Red Flags: Mappings omit metadata; no control totals; retries create duplicates; rejected messages can be deleted; ownership changes at middleware; interface evidence retained shorter than records.

content:
GxP IT Audit Checklist [DA-02-014]: Demonstrate how the URS defines each GxP calculation or rule, authoritative inputs, version, units, precision, rounding, boundary behavior, invalid/missing-data handling and reproducible output.
Phase: 02 URS | Domain: Calculations | Topic: Algorithms, precision and reproducibility | Priority: Critical
Follow-Up Probe: Recalculate a boundary case and a value that changes after source correction; show which version applies, how prior output is retained and when downstream decisions must be reassessed.
Expected Evidence / Criteria: Calculation/rule catalogue; approved formulas and references; input provenance; precision/rounding/time-zone rules; version/effective dating; error behavior; explainability and traceability; independent verification criteria.

Red Flags: Formula source absent; spreadsheet result differs from URS; rounding defined only in code; version not stored with output; missing data treated as zero; recalculation overwrites history.

document_title: Top 25 Checklists GxP IT Audit Questions 2026
content:
GxP IT Audit Checklist [DA-02-015]: Explain how the URS identifies critical configuration and master data, assigns creation/change/approval authority, preserves effective versions and prevents unapproved values from influencing records.
Phase: 02 URS | Domain: Configuration & Master Data | Topic: Controlled parameters and reference data | Priority: Critical
Follow-Up Probe: Select one limit, workflow rule and product/specification value; trace who may propose, verify, approve, activate, backdate and retire it and which existing records remain linked to the prior version.
Expected Evidence / Criteria: Critical configuration/master-data inventory; lifecycle and approval requirements; segregation; effective dating/versioning; dual verification where risk warrants; audit trail; migration/reconciliation; rollback and impact assessment.

Red Flags: Critical parameters not inventoried; same user creates and approves; effective version not retained; changes bypass formal change control; backdating possible; records do not identify applied version.

content:

document_title: Top 25 Checklists GxP IT Audit Questions 2026
content:
GxP IT Audit Checklist [DA-02-017]: Describe how the URS requires preservation or justified archival of legacy values, metadata, audit trails, signatures, status, links and record meaning, including reconciliation and handling of invalid or unmappable data.
Phase: 02 URS | Domain: Data Migration | Topic: Migration, conversion and legacy-history requirements | Priority: Critical
Follow-Up Probe: Select a legacy record with corrections, attachments and signatures and trace each component to the target or archive, including how a user proves completeness after migration.
Expected Evidence / Criteria: Data-scope and mapping requirements; source/target counts and control totals; metadata/history/signature rules; transformation approval; exception/quarantine; repeatability; verification sampling rationale; legacy access and cutover reconciliation.

document_title: Top 25 Checklists GxP IT Audit Questions 2026
content:
GxP IT Audit Checklist [DA-02-018]: Trace every record category to a requirement for retention start event, period, archive format, metadata/audit history, readability test, legal hold, authorized destruction and documented evidence of disposition.
Phase: 02 URS | Domain: Records Management | Topic: Retention, archive, legal hold and destruction requirements | Priority: Critical
Follow-Up Probe: Apply two different jurisdictional retention rules and a legal hold to the same linked record set; show how the URS prevents premature deletion of the record or its dependent metadata.
Expected Evidence / Criteria: Approved retention matrix; event-based rules; archive/search/readability; linkage preservation; hold and purge authorization; destruction evidence; anonymization where applicable; supplier/default conflicts resolved.
Regulatory Alignment: Binding: 21 CFR 11.10(c) and 211.180; Official EU GMP guideline: Annex 11 §17 and Chapter 4 §§4.10-4.12; Guidance: MHRA §6.17 and WHO §§11.15-11.19.
Red Flags: Retention period has no start event; child objects purge earlier; audit trails omitted; legal hold is manual and untested; vendor default overrides law; deletion leaves no evidence.

metadata.expected_evidence: Approved retention matrix; event-based rules; archive/search/readability; linkage preservation; hold and purge authorization; destruction evidence; anonymization where applicable; supplier/default conflicts resolved.

GxP IT Audit Checklist [DA-02-019]: Show how the URS specifies exact and complete backup scope, frequency, protection, separation, monitoring and periodic restoration with reconciliation to justified RPO and RTO.

content:
GxP IT Audit Checklist [DA-03-001]: Walk through the risk-assessment method, decision rules and governance used for this system, and demonstrate how the level of formality and documentation is proportionate to uncertainty, complexity and potential harm.
Phase: 03 Risk GAMP | Domain: Quality Risk Management | Topic: Risk method, governance and formality | Priority: Critical
Follow-Up Probe: Reperform one high, one medium and one low decision with independent SMEs; explain score differences, assumptions and why the method would not allow an otherwise noncompliant control to be accepted.
Expected Evidence / Criteria: Approved QRM procedure; trained cross-functional team; defined scope, scales and decision rules; evidence-based hazards; documented assumptions/uncertainty; independent QA review; escalation and risk-acceptance authority. QRM does not waive binding controls.
Regulatory Alignment: Guidance: ICH Q9(R1) §§3-5; Official EU GMP guideline: Annex 11 §1; Guidance: PIC/S §§5.3-5.6 and WHO §5.
Red Flags: One-person assessment; all scores cluster low; severity reduced because controls exist; detectability credited without evidence; project owner accepts quality risk; binding requirement risk-scored away. Finding trigger: evidence is missing, unapproved, incomplete, inconsistent, or cannot be reproduced for the auditor-selected sample.

metadata.expected_evidence: Approved QRM procedure; trained cross-functional team; defined scope, scales and decision rules; evidence-based hazards; documented assumptions/uncertainty; independent QA review; escalation and risk-acceptance authority. QRM does not waive binding controls.

document_title: Top 25 Checklists GxP IT Audit Questions 2026
content:
GxP IT Audit Checklist [DA-03-002]: Demonstrate how the risk boundary follows the complete intended use across application, infrastructure, interfaces, records, people, procedures and external services rather than the procurement boundary.
Phase: 03 Risk GAMP | Domain: Scope & Governance | Topic: Intended use and risk boundary | Priority: Critical
Follow-Up Probe: Select one component labeled out of scope and trace whether its failure could alter a GxP decision, record, timestamp, access authorization or recovery capability.
Expected Evidence / Criteria: Approved intended use; context and data-flow diagrams; component/service inventory; dependency map; in/out rationale; process and data owners; linked URS and supplier responsibilities; QA approval.

content:

content:

content:

content:

Follow-Up Probe: Select a supplier test claimed as coverage for a critical customer requirement and show matching preconditions, configuration, data, expected result, execution evidence, reviewer independence and unresolved defects.

content:
GxP IT Audit Checklist [DA-05-017]: Trace the complete record set across transactional storage, files, indexes, audit stores, configuration, encryption keys and backups, showing integrity protection, failure detection, RPO and validated restoration/reconciliation.
Phase: 05 Functional Design | Domain: Backup & Recovery | Topic: Storage integrity, backup and restoration design | Priority: Critical
Follow-Up Probe: Restore to a point spanning an in-flight transaction and corrupted index; demonstrate how consistency, missing/duplicate records, audit chronology, links and key availability are proven before return to use.
Expected Evidence / Criteria: Storage and consistency architecture; transactional boundaries; integrity/checksum controls; backup coverage/schedule/isolation; key recovery; RPO; restore sequence/dependencies; application-level reconciliation/control totals; acceptance, authorization and retained evidence.
Regulatory Alignment: Binding: 21 CFR 211.68(b), 11.10(c); Official EU GMP guideline: Annex 11 §§7, 16; Guidance: MHRA §6.17, PIC/S §9.9 and WHO §§11.15-11.18.
Red Flags: Search/index/file stores omitted; no point-in-time consistency; keys not recoverable independently; restore success equals service start; no transaction reconciliation; backups share compromised control plane.

metadata.expected_evidence: Storage and consistency architecture; transactional boundaries; integrity/checksum controls; backup coverage/schedule/isolation; key recovery; RPO; restore sequence/dependencies; application-level reconciliation/control totals; acceptance, authorization and retained evidence.
metadata.reference: Binding: 21 CFR 211.68(b), 11.10(c); Official EU GMP guideline: Annex 11 §§7, 16; Guidance: MHRA §6.17, PIC/S §9.9 and WHO §§11.15-11.18.

document_title: Top 25 Checklists GxP IT Audit Questions 2026
content:
GxP IT Audit Checklist [DA-05-018]: Demonstrate how record-class retention start events, linked-object dependencies, archive format/viewer, readability checks, legal holds, authorized purge and destruction evidence are implemented without severing context.
Phase: 05 Functional Design | Domain: Records Management | Topic: Archive, retention, hold and destruction design | Priority: Critical
Follow-Up Probe: Apply a legal hold to one item within a linked record set while the normal retention period expires; derive which objects, audit history and indexes remain and how eventual release/destruction is approved.
Expected Evidence / Criteria: Retention-rule model; record-class mapping and start events; dependency graph; archive/index/viewer; format migration/readability test; hold inheritance; purge authorization/segregation; immutable destruction log; supplier/customer responsibilities and decommission compatibility. Acceptance: evidence is current, approved where required, complete for the selected population, and consistent with the live configuration and independent records.
Regulatory Alignment: Binding: 21 CFR 11.10(c), 211.180; Official EU GMP guideline: Annex 11 §17 and Chapter 4 §§4.10-4.12; Guidance: MHRA §6.17 and WHO §§11.15-11.19.
Red Flags: Retention begins at record creation regardless of rule; child objects purge independently; audit history excluded; legal hold does not propagate; purge admin self-approves; no long-term viewer/readability test.

metadata.expected_evidence: Retention-rule model; record-class mapping and start events; dependency graph; archive/index/viewer; format migration/readability test; hold inheritance; purge authorization/segregation; immutable destruction log; supplier/customer responsibilities and decommission compatibility. document_title: Top 25 Checklists GxP IT Audit Questions 2026
content:
GxP IT Audit Checklist [DA-05-019]: Walk through design behavior during application, interface, identity, network and supplier outages, including controlled offline records, unique identifiers, event times, authority, queued transactions and complete reconciliation after recovery.
Phase: 05 Functional Design | Domain: Business Continuity | Topic: Outage-mode workflow and reconciliation design | Priority: Critical
Follow-Up Probe: Simulate two sites working offline while messages queue and a record is corrected in the source; show conflict resolution, chronology, duplicate prevention, approvals and QA-visible reconciliation evidence.
Expected Evidence / Criteria: Outage-mode state and data flows; controlled forms/local cache; identifier allocation; event versus synchronization time; degraded authentication/authority; message queue and idempotency; reconciliation totals/exceptions; QA release gate; capacity and exercise acceptance criteria.
Regulatory Alignment: Official EU GMP guideline: Annex 11 §16 and Chapter 4 §§4.7-4.9; Guidance: MHRA §5.1, PIC/S §9.9 and WHO §§4, 11.15-11.19.
Red Flags: Design says revert to paper without identifiers/controls; offline approvals share accounts; synchronization overwrites source; queued duplicates possible; no reconciliation gate before release.

metadata.expected_evidence: Outage-mode state and data flows; controlled forms/local cache; identifier allocation; event versus synchronization time; degraded authentication/authority; message queue and idempotency; reconciliation totals/exceptions; QA release gate; capacity and exercise acceptance criteria.

document_title: Top 25 Checklists GxP IT Audit Questions 2026
content:
GxP IT Audit Checklist [DA-05-020]: Show how the design protects GxP confidentiality, integrity, chronology and availability through trust boundaries, encryption/key management, secure configuration, trusted time, security monitoring and preserved forensic evidence.
Phase: 05 Functional Design | Domain: Cybersecurity | Topic: Encryption, trusted time, monitoring and forensic design | Priority: Critical
Follow-Up Probe: Model stolen privileged credentials used to change clocks, configuration and records before exfiltration; identify exact preventive controls, correlated alerts, immutable evidence and affected-record query.
Expected Evidence / Criteria: Threat-linked control architecture; network/trust zones; encryption in transit/at rest and key ownership/rotation/recovery; secure baseline; trusted time hierarchy/drift alerts; security log schema/correlation/retention; monitoring response; forensic preservation; GxP/PQS escalation. Acceptance: evidence is current, approved where required, complete for the selected population, and consistent with the live configuration and independent records.
Regulatory Alignment: Binding GxP: 21 CFR 11.10(c)-(e), 11.30; Official EU GMP guideline: Annex 11 §§7, 9, 12-13; Supplementary non-GxP: NIST SP 800-53 and ISO/IEC 27001.
Red Flags: Encryption/key ownership vague; clocks independently editable; SIEM actor IDs cannot map to records; security logs retained too briefly; admin can alter evidence; incident design cannot query affected GxP data.

metadata.expected_evidence: Threat-linked control architecture; network/trust zones; encryption in transit/at rest and key ownership/rotation/recovery; secure baseline; trusted time hierarchy/drift alerts; security log schema/correlation/retention; monitoring response; forensic preservation; GxP/PQS escalation. document_title: Top 25 Checklists GxP IT Audit Questions 2026
content:
GxP IT Audit Checklist [DA-05-021]: Demonstrate how specifications, code, configuration, master data, infrastructure and supplier releases are versioned, promoted through segregated environments, impact-assessed, tested, approved, deployed and rolled back while preserving the production baseline.
Phase: 05 Functional Design | Domain: Change & Configuration | Topic: Baseline, environment and release design | Priority: Critical
Follow-Up Probe: Trace an emergency configuration fix from detection to production and retrospective review, then prove which exact baseline was active for records created before, during and after the change.
Expected Evidence / Criteria: Configuration-item inventory; version/repository controls; environment and promotion design; segregation/approval; release manifest; impact/traceability/regression; deployment verification; rollback; emergency path; supplier notice; record-to-version association and periodic-evaluation data.
Regulatory Alignment: Binding: 21 CFR 11.10(k), 211.68; Official EU GMP guideline: Annex 11 §§10-11; Guidance: ICH Q10 §§3.2.3-3.2.4 and ICH Q9(R1) §4.6.
Red Flags: Configuration stored in uncontrolled workbook; production edited directly; environments share data/credentials; release manifest incomplete; rollback untested; records cannot identify applied baseline.

metadata.expected_evidence: Configuration-item inventory; version/repository controls; environment and promotion design; segregation/approval; release manifest; impact/traceability/regression; deployment verification; rollback; emergency path; supplier notice; record-to-version association and periodic-evaluation data.
metadata.reference: Binding: 21 CFR 11.10(k), 211.68; Official EU GMP guideline: Annex 11 §§10-11; Guidance: ICH Q10 §§3.2.3-3.2.4 and ICH Q9(R1) §4.6.

content:
GxP IT Audit Checklist [DA-05-022]: Show how monitoring, application errors, audit events, interface queues, security alerts and user reports feed a design that preserves evidence, identifies affected records/batches, supports root cause and links incidents to deviations, CAPA and change.
Phase: 05 Functional Design | Domain: Incident & CAPA | Topic: Detection, diagnostics and affected-record analysis design | Priority: Critical
Follow-Up Probe: Create an intermittent calculation or interface defect that affects only certain versions; demonstrate the query, logs, configuration history and lineage needed to bound every impacted record and prove the remainder unaffected.
Expected Evidence / Criteria: Monitoring/event catalogue and thresholds; correlation identifiers; version/configuration and lineage links; error/retry evidence; immutable diagnostic retention; affected-population query/report; PQS/ITSM integration; privacy-controlled support data; root-cause/CAPA/change linkage. Acceptance: evidence is current, approved where required, complete for the selected population, and consistent with the live configuration and independent records.
Regulatory Alignment: Binding: 21 CFR 211.192 and 11.10(e), (k); Official EU GMP guideline: Annex 11 §13; Guidance: FDA DI Q15/Q18, MHRA §§3.8-3.9, PIC/S §12 and WHO §13.
Red Flags: Logs lack record/version correlation; diagnostics expire before trend detection; supplier has sole access; no query to bound affected population; error retries erase first failure; IT tickets cannot link to PQS.

metadata.expected_evidence: Monitoring/event catalogue and thresholds; correlation identifiers; version/configuration and lineage links; error/retry evidence; immutable diagnostic retention; affected-population query/report; PQS/ITSM integration; privacy-controlled support data; root-cause/CAPA/change linkage. document_title: Top 25 Checklists GxP IT Audit Questions 2026
content:
GxP IT Audit Checklist [DA-05-023]: Reconcile the technical design with the quality agreement and shared-responsibility matrix for tenant configuration, privileged access, audit evidence, change, backup, incidents, data location, subprocessors, inspection and exit.
Phase: 05 Functional Design | Domain: Supplier & Cloud | Topic: Shared-control and multi-tenant design allocation | Priority: Critical
Follow-Up Probe: Choose a control performed partly by supplier and customer and trace its complete data/evidence flow, monitoring threshold, failure escalation and fallback; identify any step assigned to neither party.
Expected Evidence / Criteria: Control-level RACI tied to architecture; tenant-isolation and configuration design; supplier/customer access; evidence APIs/reports; SLAs/alerts; data/subprocessor locations; release/incident interfaces; backup/exit design; contract/specification consistency and owner acceptance.
Regulatory Alignment: Official EU GMP guideline: Annex 11 §3; Guidance: MHRA §6.20, PIC/S §10, WHO §7 and ICH Q10 §2.7.
Red Flags: RACI contradicts design/contract; shared control has no end-to-end owner; supplier-only evidence inaccessible; tenant defaults differ from specification; subprocessor/data location absent; exit not technically designed.

metadata.expected_evidence: Control-level RACI tied to architecture; tenant-isolation and configuration design; supplier/customer access; evidence APIs/reports; SLAs/alerts; data/subprocessor locations; release/incident interfaces; backup/exit design; contract/specification consistency and owner acceptance.

content:
GxP IT Audit Checklist [DA-05-024]: Explain the design for model and prompt/version control, input/output provenance, performance boundaries, nondeterminism, human review, drift, security, adverse-output handling, supplier updates, reproducibility and fallback for each GxP use.
Phase: 05 Functional Design | Domain: Artificial Intelligence | Topic: Model, prompt, data and oversight design | Priority: Critical
Follow-Up Probe: Inject an adversarial or out-of-distribution input and then change the provider model; show how the design labels uncertainty, blocks or escalates output, preserves evidence, detects drift and reconstructs the exact decision context.
Expected Evidence / Criteria: AI component/data-flow and threat model; approved model/prompt/configuration registry; input/output/context logging; data rights/provenance; performance/failure criteria; human authority/override; drift monitoring; model-change and rollback; deterministic controls where needed; incident and affected-record design. Red Flags: Model/provider version not stored; prompts/configuration uncontrolled; human reviewer sees no source context; outputs enter records automatically; no drift/failure threshold; affected records cannot be queried; draft Annex 22 misrepresented.

content:
GxP IT Audit Checklist [DA-05-025]: Demonstrate that the specifications expose observable outcomes, diagnostic evidence and controllable test conditions for critical normal, boundary, negative, recovery and misuse cases, and that design outputs define role-specific training and competence needs.
Phase: 05 Functional Design | Domain: Validation & Human Factors | Topic: Design testability, error cases and training inputs | Priority: Critical
Follow-Up Probe: Select a control said to be tested indirectly and a control relying on trained behavior; show the independent evidence, failure injection, user observation and acceptance criteria that prove each works under realistic workload.
Expected Evidence / Criteria: Design-to-test traceability; test hooks/logs/data reset and environment controls; positive/negative/boundary/recovery use cases; objective acceptance criteria; independent oracles; usability/task analysis; error messages/help; role/competency and training-design inputs; residual procedural controls with effectiveness measures.
Regulatory Alignment: Binding: 21 CFR 11.10(a), (i), 211.25, 211.68; Official EU GMP guideline: Annex 11 §§2, 4.7 and Annex 15 §§1-3; FDA guidance (nonbinding, device QMS scope only): CSA §V.A.4-V.A.6.
Red Flags: Acceptance cannot be observed objectively; tests depend on production-only logs; negative/recovery cases omitted; expected oracle uses same code; trained users credited without usability evidence; CSA used outside device scope to avoid documentation.

content:
GxP IT Audit Checklist [DA-06-002]: Demonstrate how the regulated user established that internal and supplier development activities operated under an appropriate quality system, including defect control, review independence, records retention, and release discipline.
Phase: 06 Config Development | Domain: Supplier Mgmt | Topic: Development quality system | Priority: High
Follow-Up Probe: Show the quality records for the component with the highest defect density and reconcile the supplier's stated process to actual commits, reviews, test failures, and released binaries.
Expected Evidence / Criteria: Evidence: supplier assessment, quality agreement, development plan, lifecycle procedures, audit report, defect metrics, review records, release records, and regulated-user acceptance. Acceptance: responsibilities are explicit, actual practice matches the assessed process, critical gaps are remediated or formally controlled, and evidence is available to inspectors.
Regulatory Alignment: EU GMP Annex 11 Sections 3.1-3.4 and 4.5-4.6; ICH Q9(R1) quality risk management.
Red Flags: Generic supplier questionnaire; no right to evidence; material subcontractor unknown; supplier process not reconciled to actual records; unresolved critical audit observations.

content:
GxP IT Audit Checklist [DA-06-003]: Show how traceability proves both that every approved GxP requirement is implemented and tested and that every GxP-relevant code or configuration element has a justified upstream requirement and risk control.
Phase: 06 Config Development | Domain: CSV | Topic: Bidirectional lifecycle traceability | Priority: Critical
Follow-Up Probe: Starting from a randomly selected production-facing configuration rule, trace backward to intended use and risk, then forward to positive, negative, and regression tests without relying on manually curated hyperlinks alone.
Expected Evidence / Criteria: Evidence: controlled requirements, design/configuration specifications, risk assessment, repository tags, traceability matrix, test cases/results, and orphan analysis. Acceptance: identifiers are stable; forward and reverse coverage is complete for GxP scope; exceptions are justified and approved; the matrix reconciles to source systems.
Regulatory Alignment: EU GMP Annex 11 Sections 4.1, 4.4, 4.6 and 4.7; 21 CFR 11.10(a), where Part 11 applies.
Red Flags: Trace matrix generated after testing; broken or circular references; orphan code/configuration; requirements marked tested by unrelated evidence; unexplained excluded requirements. Finding trigger: evidence is missing, unapproved, incomplete, inconsistent, or cannot be reproduced for the auditor-selected sample.

content:
GxP IT Audit Checklist [DA-06-004]: Explain how source code, scripts, configuration-as-code, and report definitions are protected so that the approved version can be attributed, reviewed, reproduced, and linked to the deployed release.
Phase: 06 Config Development | Domain: Change Mgmt | Topic: Source repository integrity | Priority: Critical
Follow-Up Probe: Rebuild or independently hash one released artifact from its signed tag and reconcile the result to the artifact repository and deployment record; explain any binary difference.
Expected Evidence / Criteria: Evidence: repository access model, protected-branch settings, immutable tags, commit history, pull-request approvals, artifact hashes/signatures, build log, and retention controls. Acceptance: released artifacts are uniquely linked to reviewed source; histories are retained and tamper-evident; privileged bypass is restricted and monitored.
Regulatory Alignment: EU GMP Annex 11 Sections 4.1, 4.6 and 10; 21 CFR 11.10(k); NIST SP 800-218 is supporting secure-development guidance, not a GMP regulation.
Red Flags: Shared developer accounts; mutable release tags; direct commits to protected branches; artifact lacks hash/provenance; administrators can erase history without detection.

metadata.reference: EU GMP Annex 11 Sections 4.1, 4.6 and 10; 21 CFR 11.10(k); NIST SP 800-218 is supporting secure-development guidance, not a GMP regulation.

content:
GxP IT Audit Checklist [DA-06-005]: Walk me through the controlled promotion path from development to test to production and show how the process prevents developers or suppliers from introducing untested content directly into the production-bound package.
Phase: 06 Config Development | Domain: Change Mgmt | Topic: Environment segregation and promotion | Priority: Critical
Follow-Up Probe: Use the most recent urgent release to prove that the promoted artifact, configuration, database script, and approval set were identical to those tested, including any manual step.
Expected Evidence / Criteria: Evidence: environment diagram, role matrix, pipeline controls, promotion logs, artifact identifiers, approvals, exception procedure, and privileged activity review. Acceptance: duties are segregated; the tested artifact is promoted without unauthorized mutation; bypass is exceptional, approved, logged, and retrospectively reviewed.
Regulatory Alignment: EU GMP Annex 11 Sections 10 and 12; 21 CFR 11.10(d), 11.10(g) and 11.10(k), where Part 11 applies.
Red Flags: Developer production access; manual package replacement; environment-specific edits after testing; bypass has become routine; approvals occur after deployment. Finding trigger: evidence is missing, unapproved, incomplete, inconsistent, or cannot be reproduced for the auditor-selected sample.

content:
GxP IT Audit Checklist [DA-06-006]: Demonstrate how development, administration, testing, release approval, and production deployment privileges are separated according to risk and how unavoidable conflicts are detected and independently reviewed.
Phase: 06 Config Development | Domain: Access Management | Topic: Developer privilege and segregation of duties | Priority: Critical
Follow-Up Probe: Select the most privileged developer and reconstruct all repository, pipeline, vault, cloud, database, and application actions during the last release window.
Expected Evidence / Criteria: Evidence: end-to-end entitlement model, named-user exports, privileged-access records, conflict rules, approvals, session logs, and review results. Acceptance: access is least-privilege and attributable; toxic combinations are prevented or time-bound with independent monitoring; leavers and role changes are promptly reflected.
Regulatory Alignment: EU GMP Annex 11 Sections 2, 10 and 12.1-12.4; 21 CFR 11.10(d), 11.10(g) and 11.300, where applicable.
Red Flags: Shared accounts; persistent production access; no cross-platform conflict analysis; self-approval; privileged sessions not logged or reviewed.

metadata.reference: EU GMP Annex 11 Sections 2, 10 and 12.1-12.4; 21 CFR 11.10(d), 11.10(g) and 11.300, where applicable.

content:
GxP IT Audit Checklist [DA-06-007]: Show how review depth and reviewer independence are determined from GxP risk and how the review establishes more than stylistic compliance for critical logic and configuration.
Phase: 06 Config Development | Domain: CSV | Topic: Independent code and configuration review | Priority: High
Follow-Up Probe: Take a defect that escaped review and show what the reviewer examined, what evidence was recorded, why the defect was missed, and how the review method was improved.
Expected Evidence / Criteria: Evidence: review standard, risk-based review criteria, reviewer competence, annotated pull requests, static-analysis results, defect records, and closure evidence. Red Flags: Reviewer is the author; blanket approvals; no evidence of logic review; critical static-analysis findings waived without risk assessment; repeated escaped defects.

GxP IT Audit Checklist [DA-06-008]: Demonstrate how the organization establishes provenance for each production-bound artifact, including source revision, dependency versions, build environment, compiler or interpreter, build identity, and integrity verification.
Phase: 06 Config Development | Domain: Cybersecurity | Topic: Build provenance and reproducibility | Priority: Critical
Follow-Up Probe: Attempt a controlled rebuild of a sampled release or explain every difference between the reproduced and deployed artifact using retained, attributable evidence.
Expected Evidence / Criteria: Evidence: immutable build definition, locked dependency manifest, runner identity, build log, artifact repository metadata, checksum/signature, and deployment verification. Acceptance: provenance is complete; builds are repeatable to a justified level; artifacts are protected from substitution and trace to approved source.
Regulatory Alignment: EU GMP Annex 11 Sections 4.1, 4.5-4.7 and 10; NIST SP 800-218 supporting guidance.
Red Flags: Mutable artifacts; unpinned dependencies; developer workstation builds; no checksum at deployment; unavailable build logs; release cannot be reproduced.

document_title: Top 25 Checklists GxP IT Audit Questions 2026
content:
GxP IT Audit Checklist [DA-06-009]: Explain how third-party libraries, containers, plugins, and embedded components are inventoried, approved, monitored for vulnerability and obsolescence, and assessed for GxP impact before inclusion in a release.
Phase: 06 Config Development | Domain: Cybersecurity | Topic: Third-party component and vulnerability governance | Priority: High
Follow-Up Probe: Choose a component with a known critical vulnerability or end-of-support date and trace detection, exploitability assessment, compensating control, validation impact, decision authority, and remediation deadline.
Expected Evidence / Criteria: Evidence: component inventory or SBOM, approved-source policy, scanning records, vulnerability triage, support status, risk acceptance, change and regression evidence. Acceptance: inventory matches the built artifact; critical issues are timely resolved or formally controlled; GxP and data-integrity impact are assessed.
Regulatory Alignment: EU GMP Annex 11 Sections 1, 3, 4.5 and 10; NIST SP 800-218 supporting guidance; ICH Q9(R1).
Red Flags: No component inventory; SBOM differs from binary; unsupported library ignored because system is validated; indefinite risk acceptance; vulnerability scan excludes production package.

metadata.expected_evidence: Evidence: component inventory or SBOM, approved-source policy, scanning records, vulnerability triage, support status, risk acceptance, change and regression evidence. Acceptance: inventory matches the built artifact; critical issues are timely resolved or formally controlled; GxP and data-integrity
metadata.reference: EU GMP Annex 11 Sections 1, 3, 4.5 and 10; NIST SP 800-218 supporting guidance; ICH Q9(R1).

document_title: Top 25 Checklists GxP IT Audit Questions 2026
content:
GxP IT Audit Checklist [DA-06-010]: Show how insecure defaults, sample accounts, diagnostic functions, unnecessary services, and excessive permissions are identified and removed or justified in the configured solution before qualification.
Phase: 06 Config Development | Domain: Cybersecurity | Topic: Secure defaults and hardening in configuration | Priority: Critical
Follow-Up Probe: Compare a fresh vendor installation to the approved hardened build and account for every retained default account, open port, debug function, and elevated permission.
Expected Evidence / Criteria: Evidence: hardening standard, vendor baseline, configuration delta, threat/risk assessment, scan results, exception approvals, and regression tests. Acceptance: unnecessary capability is disabled; residual exposure is justified and monitored; hardening is reproducible and included in the controlled baseline.

Expected Evidence / Criteria: Evidence: approved baseline, vendor compatibility matrix, installation output, package/version export, patch record, support statement, and variance assessment. Acceptance: installed versions and options are supported and approved; discrepancies are risk-assessed; evidence is reproducible and attributable.

Red Flags: Unsupported version; baseline omits options or locale; evidence is screenshot only; patch applied after IQ without impact assessment; vendor compatibility unverified. Finding trigger: evidence is missing, unapproved, incomplete, inconsistent, or cannot be reproduced for the auditor-selected sample.

Red Flags: Uncontrolled local admins; fail-open authentication; claims mapped differently from design; expired trust certificate; shared break-glass credential.

metadata.reference: EU GMP Annex 11 Sections 12.1-12.4; 21 CFR 11.10(d), 11.10(g) and 11.300, where applicable.

content:
GxP IT Audit Checklist [DA-07-009]: Demonstrate how every installed service, integration, database, scheduler, and automation account is uniquely inventoried, owned, least-privileged, non-interactive where appropriate, and linked to a controlled secret.
Phase: 07 IQ | Domain: Access Management | Topic: Service-account installation and ownership | Priority: Critical
Follow-Up Probe: Choose one high-privilege service account and trace its creation approval, target entitlements, secret storage, use in logs, rotation, dependency impact, and emergency revocation test.
Expected Evidence / Criteria: Evidence: account inventory, owner, purpose, privilege mapping, identity-source record, vault reference, application configuration, authentication logs, and rotation/revocation procedure. Acceptance: accounts are attributable to accountable owners, privileges are justified, interactive use is prevented or controlled, and secrets are not embedded.
Regulatory Alignment: EU GMP Annex 11 Sections 12.1-12.4; 21 CFR 11.10(d) and 11.10(g), where applicable.
Red Flags: Owner is generic IT; shared account; password in script; interactive login allowed without monitoring; privilege exceeds function; account absent from inventory.

Follow-Up Probe: For an auditor-selected privileged leaver or mover, show every access path that survived the HR event, including local accounts, API tokens, remote-support accounts, cached credentials, group inheritance, and owned service accounts, and explain any activity after the effective time.
Expected Evidence / Criteria: HR source record, IAM workflow, application and infrastructure account exports, group membership, token and remote-access inventory, activity logs, service-account ownership transfer, SLA metrics, and exceptions. Acceptance requires end-to-end completeness, timely execution, no unexplained post-termination activity, and risk-assessed exceptions.
Regulatory Alignment: EU GMP Annex 11 Sections 12.1 and 12.3; 21 CFR 11.10(d) and 11.10(g) where Part 11 applies.
Red Flags: Sampling only completed tickets; termination timestamp later than observed activity; unmanaged local or vendor accounts; inherited entitlements omitted; service accounts still owned by leavers; no retrospective impact assessment for delayed removal.

metadata.expected_evidence: HR source record, IAM workflow, application and infrastructure account exports, group membership, token and remote-access inventory, activity logs, service-account ownership transfer, SLA metrics, and exceptions. Acceptance requires end-to-end completeness, timely execution, no unexplained post-term
metadata.reference: EU GMP Annex 11 Sections 12.1 and 12.3; 21 CFR 11.10(d) and 11.10(g) where Part 11 applies.

document_title: Top 25 Checklists GxP IT Audit Questions 2026
content:
GxP IT Audit Checklist [DA-11-005]: Demonstrate how every non-human identity is inventoried, uniquely purposed, least-privileged, credential-managed, monitored, and assigned to a current accountable owner throughout operation.
Phase: 11 Ops Periodic Review | Domain: Access Management | Topic: Non-human and service accounts | Priority: High
Follow-Up Probe: Choose one high-privilege service account and show what prevents interactive use, credential sharing, unapproved secret extraction, and silent activity; then demonstrate the last credential rotation without disrupting or bypassing the validated process.
Expected Evidence / Criteria: Service-account inventory, purpose and owner, entitlement mapping, vault records, rotation history, interactive-login restrictions, activity logs and alerts, dependency mapping, and exception approvals. Acceptance requires no orphaned identities, controlled secrets, attributable use, least privilege, and tested rotation or revocation.
Regulatory Alignment: EU GMP Annex 11 Sections 12.1 to 12.4; 21 CFR 11.10(d), 11.10(g), and 11.300 where Part 11 applies; NIST SP 800-53 Rev. 5 controls AC-2 and IA-5 as security guidance.
Red Flags: Unknown owner or purpose; shared credential in code or tickets; interactive login permitted without justification; no rotation; account activity outside expected jobs; inventory reconstructed manually for the audit.

metadata.expected_evidence: Service-account inventory, purpose and owner, entitlement mapping, vault records, rotation history, interactive-login restrictions, activity logs and alerts, dependency mapping, and exception approvals. Acceptance requires no orphaned identities, controlled secrets, attributable use, least privilege
metadata.reference: EU GMP Annex 11 Sections 12.1 to 12.4; 21 CFR 11.10(d), 11.10(g), and 11.300 where Part 11 applies; NIST SP 800-53 Rev. 5 controls AC-2 and IA-5 as security guidance.

document_title: Top 25 Checklists GxP IT Audit Questions 2026
content:
GxP IT Audit Checklist [DA-11-006]: Using an auditor-selected GxP record, demonstrate how audit-trail review identifies, evaluates, and resolves every material creation, modification, deletion, reprocessing, status change, and security event relevant to the quality decision.
Phase: 11 Ops Periodic Review | Domain: Audit Trail | Topic: Risk-based audit-trail review | Priority: Critical
Follow-Up Probe: Show the complete event population for the same record directly from the system, including events not displayed in the routine review report, and explain how reviewers detect missing periods, disabled logging, administrator activity, clock differences, or repeated attempts that did not change the final value.
Expected Evidence / Criteria: Audit-trail configuration and risk assessment, review procedure and frequency, raw system-generated event export, reviewer record, linked source record, exception investigation, reviewer training, and periodic verification of audit-trail availability. Acceptance requires complete intelligible events, independent and timely review, documented reasons for GxP changes, and traceable resolution before the associated decision where required.
Regulatory Alignment: EU GMP Annex 11 Sections 9 and 12.4; 21 CFR 11.10(e); FDA Data Integrity and Compliance With Drug CGMP Q&A; PIC/S PI 041-1.
Red Flags: Audit trail disabled, configurable by conflicted users, incomplete, unintelligible, or unavailable; review limited to final values; missing reasons; unexplained gaps; late review after batch or quality decision; admin actions excluded.

metadata.expected_evidence: Audit-trail configuration and risk assessment, review procedure and frequency, raw system-generated event export, reviewer record, linked source record, exception investigation, reviewer training, and periodic verification of audit-trail availability. Acceptance requires complete intelligible events
metadata.reference: EU GMP Annex 11 Sections 9 and 12.4; 21 CFR 11.10(e); FDA Data Integrity and Compliance With Drug CGMP Q&A; PIC/S PI 041-1.

document_title: Top 25 Checklists GxP IT Audit Questions 2026
content:
GxP IT Audit Checklist [DA-11-007]: Select a completed electronic signature and prove from the live record and underlying controls that the signer identity, date and time, signature meaning, credential use, and permanent linkage to the exact signed record version remain unambiguous and non-transferable.
Phase: 11 Ops Periodic Review | Domain: Electronic Signatures | Topic: Signature meaning and record linkage | Priority: Critical
Follow-Up Probe: Demonstrate what happens when the signed record is subsequently corrected, migrated, exported, or archived, and show that the signature cannot be excised, copied to another record, or displayed against a changed version without an attributable event.
Expected Evidence / Criteria: Signed record, signature manifestation, identity record, authentication configuration, signature and audit logs, record-version history, signature policy, and migration or archive test where relevant. Acceptance requires unique signer control, recorded name/date/time/meaning, permanent linkage, preservation after record lifecycle events, and no shared credentials.
Regulatory Alignment: EU GMP Annex 11 Section 14; 21 CFR 11.50, 11.70, 11.100, 11.200, and 11.300 where Part 11 applies.
Red Flags: Signature not tied to a record version; missing meaning or timestamp; shared credentials; signature can be copied or detached; correction changes signed content without new signature; archive or export loses linkage.

metadata.expected_evidence: Signed record, signature manifestation, identity record, authentication configuration, signature and audit logs, record-version history, signature policy, and migration or archive test where relevant. Acceptance requires unique signer control, recorded name/date/time/meaning, permanent linkage, pres
metadata.reference: EU GMP Annex 11 Section 14; 21 CFR 11.50, 11.70, 11.100, 11.200, and 11.300 where Part 11 applies.

document_title: Top 25 Checklists GxP IT Audit Questions 2026
content:
GxP IT Audit Checklist [DA-11-008]: Retrieve an auditor-selected record from the oldest active retention cohort and demonstrate that its content, context, critical metadata, audit trail, and associated signatures remain accurate, readable, intelligible, and available for review without relying on undocumented expert intervention.
Phase: 11 Ops Periodic Review | Domain: Data Integrity | Topic: Retention-period accessibility and readability | Priority: Critical
Follow-Up Probe: Repeat the retrieval for a record created before the latest major application, database, operating-system, or viewer change and explain how continued readability and meaning were verified when technology changed.
Expected Evidence / Criteria: Retention schedule, record inventory, storage and archive architecture, retrieval procedure, periodic readability and integrity checks, sample record with metadata and audit trail, and technology-change impact assessments. Acceptance requires timely retrieval, complete content and context, verified integrity, controlled access, and documented remediation of failed checks.
Regulatory Alignment: EU GMP Annex 11 Sections 7.1 and 17; 21 CFR 11.10(b) and 11.10(c) where Part 11 applies; applicable predicate-rule retention requirements.
Red Flags: Old records cannot be retrieved promptly; proprietary viewer unavailable; metadata or audit trail omitted; integrity checks never performed; retention period guessed; technology changes not assessed; reliance on an unsupported production environment.

metadata.expected_evidence: Retention schedule, record inventory, storage and archive architecture, retrieval procedure, periodic readability and integrity checks, sample record with metadata and audit trail, and technology-change impact assessments. Acceptance requires timely retrieval, complete content and context, verified
metadata.reference: EU GMP Annex 11 Sections 7.1 and 17; 21 CFR 11.10(b) and 11.10(c) where Part 11 applies; applicable predicate-rule retention requirements.

document_title: Top 25 Checklists GxP IT Audit Questions 2026
content:
GxP IT Audit Checklist [DA-11-009]: Reconcile the approved inventory of GxP data, metadata, audit trails, configurations, encryption material, and supporting components to the live backup job definitions and demonstrate that the backup scope remains complete after system changes.
Phase: 11 Ops Periodic Review | Domain: Backup & Disaster Recovery | Topic: Backup population completeness | Priority: Critical
Follow-Up Probe: Select one newly added or changed component and one apparently successful backup; prove that the required content was actually captured and usable rather than merely that the job ended with a success status.
Expected Evidence / Criteria: Data and component inventory, backup architecture and job definitions, retention and immutability settings, job and exception logs, scope reconciliation, change records, and content verification. Acceptance requires complete risk-based scope, monitored failures, protected copies, periodic reconciliation after change, and no unapproved exclusions.
Regulatory Alignment: EU GMP Annex 11 Section 7.2; 21 CFR 211.68(b); 21 CFR 11.10(c) where Part 11 applies; NIST SP 800-53 Rev. 5 control CP-9 as security guidance.
Red Flags: Scope cannot be reconciled; successful status accepted without content verification; audit trails, attachments, or keys excluded; backup changes outside change control; failed jobs aged or suppressed; no protected off-system copy where risk requires it.

metadata.expected_evidence: Data and component inventory, backup architecture and job definitions, retention and immutability settings, job and exception logs, scope reconciliation, change records, and content verification. Acceptance requires complete risk-based scope, monitored failures, protected copies, periodic reconcilia
metadata.reference: EU GMP Annex 11 Section 7.2; 21 CFR 211.68(b); 21 CFR 11.10(c) where Part 11 applies; NIST SP 800-53 Rev. 5 control CP-9 as security guidance.

document_title: Top 25 Checklists GxP IT Audit Questions 2026
content:
GxP IT Audit Checklist [DA-11-010]: Reperform the evidence chain for the last recovery exercise and show that the recovered service met approved recovery time and recovery point objectives while preserving record completeness, data meaning, audit trails, interfaces, security, and business-process usability.
Phase: 11 Ops Periodic Review | Domain: Business Continuity | Topic: Restore and recovery effectiveness | Priority: Critical
Follow-Up Probe: Show the last failed or partially successful restore step, how the failure was detected, what data interval or functionality was at risk, and whether the retest proved the corrective action rather than repeating only the successful path.
Expected Evidence / Criteria: Approved recovery plan, business impact analysis, RTO and RPO, exercise protocol and raw timestamps, restored-data reconciliation, security and interface checks, business and Quality acceptance, deviations, CAPA, and retest. Acceptance requires objectives achieved or deviations formally assessed with effective remediation and no unexplained data loss.
Regulatory Alignment: EU GMP Annex 11 Sections 7.2 and 16; 21 CFR 211.68(b); NIST SP 800-34 Rev. 1 and NIST SP 800-53 Rev. 5 CP controls as nonbinding guidance.
Red Flags: Restore never tested; test excludes audit trails, interfaces, keys, or business verification; RTO or RPO missed without risk acceptance; failed step omitted; recovered data not reconciled; exercise performed only on unlike infrastructure.

metadata.expected_evidence: Approved recovery plan, business impact analysis, RTO and RPO, exercise protocol and raw timestamps, restored-data reconciliation, security and interface checks, business and Quality acceptance, deviations, CAPA, and retest. Acceptance requires objectives achieved or deviations formally assessed wit
metadata.reference: EU GMP Annex 11 Sections 7.2 and 16; 21 CFR 211.68(b); NIST SP 800-34 Rev. 1 and NIST SP 800-53 Rev. 5 CP controls as nonbinding guidance.

document_title: Top 25 Checklists GxP IT Audit Questions 2026
content:
GxP IT Audit Checklist [DA-11-011]: Trace a complete GxP data transfer from authoritative source through middleware to target and downstream report, demonstrating how completeness, accuracy, sequence, attribution, timestamps, and processing status are reconciled in routine operation.
Phase: 11 Ops Periodic Review | Domain: Interfaces & Integrations | Topic: Operational reconciliation of data transfers | Priority: Critical
Follow-Up Probe: Use the last failed, duplicate, delayed, partial, or out-of-order transfer and show how the system prevented silent loss or double processing, preserved the original event, controlled reprocessing, and assessed downstream quality impact.
Expected Evidence / Criteria: Interface inventory and data mapping, control totals or acknowledgements, queue and transaction logs, error and retry configuration, reconciliation reports, incident or deviation, reprocessing record, and downstream verification. Acceptance requires end-to-end traceability, controlled error handling, no silent loss or duplication, and documented impact assessment.
Regulatory Alignment: EU GMP Annex 11 Sections 5, 7, 8, 9, and 13; 21 CFR 11.10(a), 11.10(e), 11.10(f), and 11.10(h) where Part 11 applies.
Red Flags: No end-to-end identifier or reconciliation; monitoring only transport availability; discarded error messages; uncontrolled replay; duplicate processing; manual correction outside audit trail; source and target totals disagree without investigation.

metadata.expected_evidence: Interface inventory and data mapping, control totals or acknowledgements, queue and transaction logs, error and retry configuration, reconciliation reports, incident or deviation, reprocessing record, and downstream verification. Acceptance requires end-to-end traceability, controlled error handling
metadata.reference: EU GMP Annex 11 Sections 5, 7, 8, 9, and 13; 21 CFR 11.10(a), 11.10(e), 11.10(f), and 11.10(h) where Part 11 applies.

document_title: Top 25 Checklists GxP IT Audit Questions 2026
content:
GxP IT Audit Checklist [DA-11-012]: Starting from the full alert population, demonstrate how quality-relevant alarms are rationalized, prioritized, routed, acknowledged, investigated, and closed within defined limits, including periods when the primary responder is unavailable.
Phase: 11 Ops Periodic Review | Domain: Operations Monitoring | Topic: Alarm and alert response | Priority: High
Follow-Up Probe: Select one suppressed, auto-closed, repeated, or missed alert and reconstruct what occurred in the regulated process during the blind period; explain how the impact population was identified and why recurrence is controlled.
Expected Evidence / Criteria: Alert catalogue and rationale, thresholds, routing and escalation rules, on-call coverage, raw alert history, acknowledgement and response records, suppression approvals, deviations or incidents, trend review, and effectiveness actions. Acceptance requires complete population visibility, risk-based response limits, controlled suppression, and impact assessment for missed alerts.
Regulatory Alignment: EU GMP Annex 11 Sections 1, 11, and 13; 21 CFR 211.68(a); ICH Q9(R1) Sections 3 and 4.
Red Flags: No complete alert population; alert floods or chronic recurrence; critical alert auto-closed; undocumented suppression; response SLA measured without quality impact; blind periods not assessed; no escalation outside business hours.

document_title: Top 25 Checklists GxP IT Audit Questions 2026
content:
GxP IT Audit Checklist [DA-11-013]: Show how the periodic evaluation derives and challenges incident, deviation, problem, and service-request trends from complete source populations rather than relying on ticket labels or manually selected quality events.
Phase: 11 Ops Periodic Review | Domain: Incident & Deviation Management | Topic: Operational event trend inclusion | Priority: High
Follow-Up Probe: Reclassify a sample of low-severity or non-GxP-labelled tickets against the system's intended use and data flows; explain any event that should have triggered a deviation, validation impact assessment, or broader retrospective review.
Expected Evidence / Criteria: Incident and deviation taxonomy, linkage rules, complete ITSM and quality-event extracts, trend method, reclassification controls, management review, and actions. Acceptance requires reconciled populations, documented inclusion and exclusion logic, challenge of repeat events, and escalation of potential GxP impact.
Regulatory Alignment: EU GMP Annex 11 Sections 11 and 13; ICH Q9(R1) Section 4; PIC/S PI 041-1 Sections 6 and 9.
Red Flags: IT and Quality populations do not reconcile; GxP impact determined by service-desk category alone; recurring events fragmented; exclusions lack rationale; data corrections treated as requests rather than events; trend omits supplier cases.

metadata.reference: EU GMP Annex 11 Sections 11 and 13; ICH Q9(R1) Section 4; PIC/S PI 041-1 Sections 6 and 9.

document_title: Top 25 Checklists GxP IT Audit Questions 2026
content:
GxP IT Audit Checklist [DA-11-014]: For the highest-risk recurring problem, demonstrate that root cause and CAPA effectiveness were established with objective evidence and that recurrence was assessed across related systems, sites, records, and supplier services.
Phase: 11 Ops Periodic Review | Domain: Problem & CAPA Management | Topic: Recurrence and CAPA effectiveness | Priority: High
Follow-Up Probe: Show the search logic used to declare no recurrence, then broaden it to synonyms, different ticket categories, similar error codes, manual corrections, and near misses; explain any events the original effectiveness check missed.
Expected Evidence / Criteria: Problem investigation, causal evidence, CAPA plan, implementation records, cross-system applicability assessment, defined effectiveness measure and observation period, complete recurrence query, results, and Quality approval. Acceptance requires cause-specific measures, adequate time and population, no unexplained recurrence, and escalation when effectiveness is not demonstrated.
Regulatory Alignment: EU GMP Annex 11 Sections 11 and 13; ICH Q9(R1) Sections 4.4 and 4.6; PIC/S PI 041-1 Sections 6 and 9.
Red Flags: Root cause stated as human error without systemic analysis; CAPA effectiveness equals task completion; recurrence query undocumented or narrow; repeat events relabelled; no cross-system assessment; failed effectiveness check not reopened.

metadata.expected_evidence: Problem investigation, causal evidence, CAPA plan, implementation records, cross-system applicability assessment, defined effectiveness measure and observation period, complete recurrence query, results, and Quality approval. Acceptance requires cause-specific measures, adequate time and population,
metadata.reference: EU GMP Annex 11 Sections 11 and 13; ICH Q9(R1) Sections 4.4 and 4.6; PIC/S PI 041-1 Sections 6 and 9.

document_title: Top 25 Checklists GxP IT Audit Questions 2026
content:
GxP IT Audit Checklist [DA-11-015]: Using the complete change and release history since the previous evaluation, demonstrate how cumulative effects on intended use, data integrity, security, performance, interfaces, supplier dependencies, and validation status were assessed.
Phase: 11 Ops Periodic Review | Domain: Change Management | Topic: Cumulative change impact | Priority: Critical
Follow-Up Probe: Identify individually minor changes that touched the same critical function or control and explain why their combined effect did not require revised requirements, risk assessment, regression testing, or revalidation.
Expected Evidence / Criteria: Complete change population, releases and supplier changes, affected-component mapping, cumulative-impact method, revised risk and traceability records, regression evidence, periodic-evaluation conclusion, and Quality approvals. Acceptance requires reconciliation to deployment and configuration history and explicit assessment of repeated changes to critical functions.
Regulatory Alignment: EU GMP Annex 11 Sections 4.2, 10, and 11; 21 CFR 11.10(a) and 11.10(k); 21 CFR 211.68(b); ICH Q9(R1) Section 4.6.
Red Flags: Deployment population exceeds approved changes; minor changes never aggregated; repeated changes to same control; supplier releases omitted; incidents rise after changes; validation documents and system description not updated.

metadata.expected_evidence: Complete change population, releases and supplier changes, affected-component mapping, cumulative-impact method, revised risk and traceability records, regression evidence, periodic-evaluation conclusion, and Quality approvals. metadata.reference: EU GMP Annex 11 Sections 4.2, 10, and 11; 21 CFR 11.10(a) and 11.10(k); 21 CFR 211.68(b); ICH Q9(R1) Section 4.6.

document_title: Top 25 Checklists GxP IT Audit Questions 2026
content:
GxP IT Audit Checklist [DA-11-016]: Compare the live production configuration to the approved baseline and demonstrate how authorized differences, temporary settings, feature flags, emergency changes, and supplier-managed parameters are detected and governed.
Phase: 11 Ops Periodic Review | Domain: Configuration Management | Topic: Production configuration drift | Priority: Critical
Follow-Up Probe: The auditor will select a security, audit-trail, retention, calculation, interface, or workflow parameter from the live system and ask for its last change, approver, test evidence, and current baseline entry.
Expected Evidence / Criteria: Approved baseline, automated or controlled configuration export, comparison report, parameter ownership, authorized change records, temporary-change expiry, drift alerts, investigation, and re-baselining approval. Acceptance requires complete critical-parameter coverage and no unexplained production difference.
Regulatory Alignment: EU GMP Annex 11 Sections 4.3, 10, and 11; 21 CFR 211.68(b); 21 CFR 11.10(k) where Part 11 applies.
Red Flags: No approved baseline; comparison omits critical parameters; manual snapshots without provenance; unexplained drift; expired feature flags; supplier settings inaccessible; direct changes visible only in audit logs after the fact.

metadata.expected_evidence: Approved baseline, automated or controlled configuration export, comparison report, parameter ownership, authorized change records, temporary-change expiry, drift alerts, investigation, and re-baselining approval. document_title: Top 25 Checklists GxP IT Audit Questions 2026
content:
GxP IT Audit Checklist [DA-11-017]: Trace the vulnerability population for the system to patch, mitigation, acceptance, or retirement decisions and demonstrate how product quality, data integrity, availability, exploitability, supplier constraints, and validation impact determine remediation priority.
Phase: 11 Ops Periodic Review | Domain: Cybersecurity | Topic: Vulnerability and patch risk decisions | Priority: Critical
Follow-Up Probe: Select the oldest high or critical vulnerability and show the actual affected asset and version, exposure path, compensating-control telemetry, accountable risk acceptance, reassessment cadence, and evidence that the control would detect exploitation.
Expected Evidence / Criteria: Asset and software inventory, scanner and supplier advisories, vulnerability records, applicability validation, risk decisions, patch changes and tests, compensating controls and logs, exception expiry, and periodic review. Acceptance requires complete scope, timely risk-based action, approved and time-bound exceptions, and verified compensating controls.
Regulatory Alignment: EU GMP Annex 11 Sections 1, 11, and 12; NIST Cybersecurity Framework 2.0 and NIST SP 800-53 Rev. 5 SI and RA controls as nonbinding security guidance.
Red Flags: Assets missing from scan scope; risk accepted from CVSS alone; overdue critical vulnerabilities; compensating control asserted without telemetry; exception has no expiry; supplier constraint accepted indefinitely; patch not linked to validation impact.

metadata.expected_evidence: Asset and software inventory, scanner and supplier advisories, vulnerability records, applicability validation, risk decisions, patch changes and tests, compensating controls and logs, exception expiry, and periodic review.
