metadata.reference: EU GMP Annex 11 Sections 1, 11, and 12; NIST Cybersecurity Framework 2.0 and NIST SP 800-53 Rev. 5 SI and RA controls as nonbinding security guidance.

document_title: Top 25 Checklists GxP IT Audit Questions 2026
content:
GxP IT Audit Checklist [DA-11-018]: Demonstrate that security logging covers the events capable of affecting regulated data or validated configuration and that detections remain effective when logs are delayed, malformed, tampered with, or unavailable.
Phase: 11 Ops Periodic Review | Domain: Cybersecurity | Topic: Security event logging and detection | Priority: High
Follow-Up Probe: Generate or locate an auditor-selected high-risk event such as failed privileged access, audit-log disablement, mass export, configuration change, or unusual service-account use and trace it from source through collection, correlation, alert, investigation, and retention.
Expected Evidence / Criteria: Logging risk assessment, event and source inventory, time synchronization, retention, access controls, SIEM ingestion health, detection rules, alert tests, incident records, and gap monitoring. Acceptance requires coverage of critical events, protected and synchronized logs, tested detections, monitored collection failures, and retained evidence.
Regulatory Alignment: EU GMP Annex 11 Sections 9, 12, and 13; 21 CFR 11.10(e) where Part 11 applies; NIST Cybersecurity Framework 2.0 Detect and Respond functions as nonbinding guidance.
Red Flags: Critical log sources not onboarded; clocks not synchronized; administrators can alter logs; collection gaps invisible; alert never tested; retention shorter than record or investigation need; security events not assessed for GxP impact.

metadata.expected_evidence: Logging risk assessment, event and source inventory, time synchronization, retention, access controls, SIEM ingestion health, detection rules, alert tests, incident records, and gap monitoring. Acceptance requires coverage of critical events, protected and synchronized logs, tested detections, monit
metadata.reference: EU GMP Annex 11 Sections 9, 12, and 13; 21 CFR 11.10(e) where Part 11 applies; NIST Cybersecurity Framework 2.0 Detect and Respond functions as nonbinding guidance.

document_title: Top 25 Checklists GxP IT Audit Questions 2026
content:
GxP IT Audit Checklist [DA-11-019]: For one critical provider-managed control, demonstrate how the regulated company obtains sufficient ongoing assurance from contract obligations, service evidence, performance data, exceptions, and independent verification rather than relying solely on a certification.
Phase: 11 Ops Periodic Review | Domain: Supplier & Cloud Oversight | Topic: Operational supplier assurance | Priority: Critical
Follow-Up Probe: Select the most recent supplier incident, control exception, subprocessor change, or forced release and show when you were notified, how GxP impact was assessed, what evidence the supplier supplied, and how your Quality unit challenged closure.
Expected Evidence / Criteria: Quality or service agreement, shared-responsibility matrix, supplier qualification and reassessment, audit or assurance reports with bridge coverage, SLA and control metrics, incident and change notices, exceptions and CAPA, subprocessor inventory, and exit provisions. Acceptance requires clear accountability, timely evidence access, evaluated exceptions, and risk-based independent checks.
Regulatory Alignment: EU GMP Annex 11 Sections 3, 7, 11, 12, 13, and 16; 21 CFR 11.10 where applicable remains the regulated user's responsibility; NIST SP 800-53 Rev. 5 SR controls as nonbinding guidance.
Red Flags: Certification treated as complete evidence; expired bridge period; agreement omits GxP records or inspection access; supplier changes not notified; subprocessor unknown; exceptions not assessed; responsibility gap for backup, logs, incidents, or data return.

metadata.reference: EU GMP Annex 11 Sections 3, 7, 11, 12, 13, and 16; 21 CFR 11.10 where applicable remains the regulated user's responsibility; NIST SP 800-53 Rev. 5 SR controls as nonbinding guidance.

document_title: Top 25 Checklists GxP IT Audit Questions 2026
content:
GxP IT Audit Checklist [DA-11-020]: Demonstrate how capacity, response time, job completion, error rate, queue depth, storage growth, and availability trends are converted into risk-based actions before degraded service affects data completeness or regulated decisions.
Phase: 11 Ops Periodic Review | Domain: Performance & Reliability | Topic: Capacity and reliability trends | Priority: High
Follow-Up Probe: Select the period with worst performance and show which records, interfaces, calculations, users, or batch decisions were exposed; explain why thresholds and forecasts detected the condition early enough.
Expected Evidence / Criteria: Service objectives, capacity model, monitoring data, threshold rationale, forecasts, performance incidents, data-impact checks, scaling or remediation changes, and management review. Acceptance requires critical-process linkage, defined action thresholds, reliable data, timely actions, and assessment of any excursion.
Regulatory Alignment: EU GMP Annex 11 Sections 1 and 11; 21 CFR 11.10(a) where Part 11 applies; 21 CFR 211.68(a) for applicable drug CGMP systems.
Red Flags: Only uptime reported; thresholds lack business basis; capacity breach accepted without data-impact review; recurring peak failures; monitoring gaps; manual workarounds unrecorded; forecast action repeatedly deferred.

metadata.reference: EU GMP Annex 11 Sections 1 and 11; 21 CFR 11.10(a) where Part 11 applies; 21 CFR 211.68(a) for applicable drug CGMP systems.

document_title: Top 25 Checklists GxP IT Audit Questions 2026
content:
GxP IT Audit Checklist [DA-11-021]: For each role capable of creating, reviewing, administering, changing, recovering, or investigating GxP records, demonstrate that current procedures and task-specific competence were effective before the person performed unsupervised work.
Phase: 11 Ops Periodic Review | Domain: Training & Competency | Topic: Role competence and procedure currency | Priority: High
Follow-Up Probe: Select a person involved in the last deviation, emergency change, failed restore, or audit-trail exception and compare their actual actions with training content, effective procedure version, access grant date, and demonstrated competence.
Expected Evidence / Criteria: Role and curriculum mapping, effective SOPs and work instructions, training assignments and completion, competency assessment, access prerequisites, supervised qualification where needed, retraining after change or deviation, and effectiveness evidence. Acceptance requires no unsupervised activity before qualification and procedures aligned to current system behavior.
Regulatory Alignment: EU GMP Annex 11 Section 2; 21 CFR 11.10(i) where Part 11 applies; PIC/S PI 041-1 Sections 6.5 and 6.6.
Red Flags: Access granted before training; training only attendance-based; obsolete procedure; vendor personnel omitted; deviation reveals procedure-content gap; recurring retraining without system or process correction; no competency evidence for critical tasks.

Acceptance requires no unsupervised activity b
metadata.reference: EU GMP Annex 11 Section 2; 21 CFR 11.10(i) where Part 11 applies; PIC/S PI 041-1 Sections 6.5 and 6.6.

document_title: Top 25 Checklists GxP IT Audit Questions 2026
content:
GxP IT Audit Checklist [DA-11-022]: Demonstrate through the most recent exercise or outage that the manual or alternative process can be activated within the approved time and produces complete, attributable, controlled records that are accurately reconciled when the system returns.
Phase: 11 Ops Periodic Review | Domain: Business Continuity | Topic: Manual workaround control | Priority: Critical
Follow-Up Probe: Extend the scenario beyond the planned exercise duration and explain how blank forms, identifiers, calculations, approvals, duplicate prevention, backlog, storage, and later transcription remain controlled when staff, network, or identity services are also unavailable.
Expected Evidence / Criteria: Approved continuity procedure, activation criteria, controlled forms or alternate system, role and contact lists, exercise records, source and reconciliation logs, deviation handling, Quality and business acceptance, and improvement actions. GxP IT Audit Checklist [DA-12-017]: For the latest provider-initiated release, demonstrate how advance notice, release content, shared-responsibility changes, GxP impact, tenant configuration, assurance evidence, regression, deployment timing, and acceptance were controlled.
Phase: 12 Change Config Mgmt | Domain: Supplier & Cloud Change | Topic: Provider-initiated release control | Priority: Critical
Follow-Up Probe: Use a forced, emergency, silent, or inadequately notified supplier change and show when it first became visible in your environment, how you detected the actual differences, and how affected records and decisions were retrospectively assessed.
Expected Evidence / Criteria: Contract and change-notification terms, release notice and notes, supplier assurance evidence, tenant impact assessment, configuration comparison, risk-based regression, deployment confirmation, acceptance, incidents, and escalation. Acceptance requires timely notice or effective independent detection, assessed shared responsibilities, and controlled use after release.
Regulatory Alignment: EU GMP Annex 11 Sections 3, 4.5, 10, and 11; 21 CFR 11.10(a) and 11.10(k) where Part 11 applies.
Red Flags: Supplier release not represented internally; notice after deployment; release notes accepted without tenant verification; feature enabled silently; assurance evidence unavailable; contract lacks notification; impacted SOP or test not updated.

content:
GxP IT Audit Checklist [DA-12-018]: Reconstruct the most recent high-risk emergency change minute by minute from trigger through authorization, implementation, verification, release, retrospective review, re-baselining, and closure.
Phase: 12 Change Config Mgmt | Domain: Emergency Change Management | Topic: Emergency-change reconstruction | Priority: Critical
Follow-Up Probe: List each standard control bypassed because of urgency and show the contemporaneous compensating control; then identify any action performed before authorization or evidence created after the fact and assess its impact.
Expected Evidence / Criteria: Emergency criteria, incident or trigger, contemporaneous approval, actor and command or deployment logs, risk assessment, focused tests, monitoring, business and Quality verification, retrospective review within SLA, baseline update, and follow-up actions. Acceptance requires justified emergency status, preserved chronology, controlled bypasses, and completed retrospective assurance.
Regulatory Alignment: EU GMP Annex 11 Sections 4.2, 10, and 13; 21 CFR 11.10(k); 21 CFR 211.68(b).
Red Flags: Emergency status used for convenience; implementation precedes authorization; generic account; no command logs; testing absent; retrospective review overdue; baseline not updated; repeat emergency for same cause; Quality unaware.

document_title: Top 25 Checklists GxP IT Audit Questions 2026
content:
GxP IT Audit Checklist [DA-12-019]: Demonstrate how direct edits to production code, configuration, database objects, master data, reports, and infrastructure are prevented where feasible and detected promptly when technically possible.
Phase: 12 Change Config Mgmt | Domain: Configuration Management | Topic: Direct-production edit detection | Priority: Critical
Follow-Up Probe: Perform or locate an authorized test of a direct-change detection and show the native audit event, alert, investigation, change linkage, state comparison, and restoration; explain any production layer with no equivalent detection.
Expected Evidence / Criteria: Technical restrictions, privileged-access model, file or configuration integrity monitoring, database and cloud audit logs, drift comparison, alert rules and tests, incidents, and emergency process. Acceptance requires prevention or timely detection across all critical layers and independent review of any direct edit.
Regulatory Alignment: EU GMP Annex 11 Sections 9, 10, and 12; 21 CFR 11.10(d), 11.10(e), 11.10(g), and 11.10(k); 21 CFR 211.68(b).
Red Flags: Direct edits technically unrestricted and unmonitored; drift scans omit critical layers; supplier activity invisible; audit events mutable; alert never tested; detected edit closed without data or validated-state impact assessment. Finding trigger: evidence is missing, unapproved, incomplete, inconsistent, or cannot be reproduced for the auditor-selected sample.

metadata.expected_evidence: Technical restrictions, privileged-access model, file or configuration integrity monitoring, database and cloud audit logs, drift comparison, alert rules and tests, incidents, and emergency process. Acceptance requires prevention or timely detection across all critical layers and independent review

document_title: Top 25 Checklists GxP IT Audit Questions 2026
content:
GxP IT Audit Checklist [DA-12-020]: Demonstrate that rollback criteria, decision authority, technical backout steps, data reconciliation, communication, and maximum decision time were defined and realistically tested before implementation.
Phase: 12 Change Config Mgmt | Domain: Business Continuity | Topic: Rollback and backout readiness | Priority: Critical
Follow-Up Probe: Apply the scenario in which the schema or data has changed after go-live and simple code rollback would create incompatibility; show how forward-fix, restore, transaction replay, and preservation of intervening GxP records are controlled.
Expected Evidence / Criteria: Backout and decision plan, data-state assumptions, backups or snapshots, rehearsal or lower-environment test, timing, roles, reconciliation method, go/no-go and rollback criteria, monitoring, and approval. Acceptance requires executable steps, protected intervening records, realistic timing, and tested data recovery or forward-fix strategy.
Regulatory Alignment: EU GMP Annex 11 Sections 7.2, 10, and 16; 21 CFR 211.68(b); ICH Q9(R1) Section 4.
Red Flags: Rollback is only 'restore backup'; intervening records not addressed; criteria vague; authority unavailable; timing exceeds tolerable outage; plan untested; production rollback failed without deviation; incompatible schema ignored.

metadata.expected_evidence: Backout and decision plan, data-state assumptions, backups or snapshots, rehearsal or lower-environment test, timing, roles, reconciliation method, go/no-go and rollback criteria, monitoring, and approval. content:
GxP IT Audit Checklist [DA-12-021]: Show how the change updated backup scope, retention, restore sequence, recovery automation, encryption or key dependencies, and recovery documentation, and prove the revised configuration can be restored.
Phase: 12 Change Config Mgmt | Domain: Backup & Disaster Recovery | Topic: Change impact on recoverability | Priority: Critical
Follow-Up Probe: Select the first backup after change and recover it to an isolated environment; demonstrate that new data stores, audit trails, attachments, secrets, and interfaces are present and usable and that obsolete components do not create ambiguity.
Expected Evidence / Criteria: Changed-component inventory, backup and recovery impact assessment, updated jobs and plans, first-job verification, restore test, data and configuration reconciliation, RTO or RPO review, deviations, and approval. Acceptance requires complete revised scope and demonstrated recoverability before reliance on the changed service.
Regulatory Alignment: EU GMP Annex 11 Sections 7.2, 10, and 16; 21 CFR 211.68(b); NIST SP 800-53 Rev. 5 CP-9 and CP-10 as nonbinding guidance.
Red Flags: Backup impact marked not applicable despite new data store; first backup unverified; keys or secrets omitted; recovery document stale; restore not tested after major change; retired job continues while new component is unprotected.

content:
GxP IT Audit Checklist [DA-12-022]: Demonstrate that every affected SOP, work instruction, form, report definition, master-data rule, support runbook, training assignment, and role profile became effective in the correct sequence relative to deployment.
Phase: 12 Change Config Mgmt | Domain: Documentation & Training | Topic: Operational-readiness updates | Priority: High
Follow-Up Probe: Select a user or support action performed immediately after release and show which procedure version and training status governed it; explain any interval when the new system behavior and controlled instructions were inconsistent.
Expected Evidence / Criteria: Impact assessment, document and curriculum list, revised approved documents, effective dates, training assignments and completion, access prerequisites, runbooks, communication, and post-release observation. Acceptance requires controlled sequencing and no unsupervised affected activity before readiness.
Regulatory Alignment: EU GMP Annex 11 Sections 2, 4.1, and 10; 21 CFR 11.10(i) and 11.10(k) where Part 11 applies.
Red Flags: Deployment precedes effective procedure or training; old forms remain accessible; runbook not updated; change impact says no training despite changed workflow; users operate before qualification; master-data rule undocumented.

document_title: Top 25 Checklists GxP IT Audit Questions 2026
content:
GxP IT Audit Checklist [DA-12-023]: Using production evidence, demonstrate that the change achieved its intended outcome without introducing unexpected effects during the defined observation period.
Phase: 12 Change Config Mgmt | Domain: Post-Implementation Verification | Topic: Production outcome verification | Priority: High
Follow-Up Probe: Compare the pre-change baseline with the worst post-change metric, incident, alert, data correction, failed transaction, or user workaround and explain how the review searched for silent effects rather than confirming only deployment success.
Expected Evidence / Criteria: Defined success and failure criteria, observation period, production monitoring, transaction and data-quality checks, incident and user-feedback population, interface reconciliation, security and performance data, review and approval. Acceptance requires evidence against pre-defined criteria and controlled action for adverse trends.
Regulatory Alignment: EU GMP Annex 11 Sections 10, 11, and 13; 21 CFR 11.10(a); ICH Q9(R1) Section 4.6.
Red Flags: Verification equals 'deployment completed'; no predefined criteria; observation too short; exceptions excluded; comparison baseline absent; adverse signals not linked to change; review closed before real GxP use.

content:
GxP IT Audit Checklist [DA-12-024]: Aggregate all changes since the last comprehensive validation or periodic evaluation and demonstrate that the system's current intended use, risk controls, architecture, data flows, and assurance evidence remain coherent as a whole.
Phase: 12 Change Config Mgmt | Domain: Periodic Review | Topic: Cumulative validated-state review | Priority: Critical
Follow-Up Probe: Group individually low-risk releases by the critical control they touched and show whether repeated modifications, technical debt, deferred defects, or supplier releases crossed a threshold requiring broader revalidation or redesign.
Expected Evidence / Criteria: Complete release and change history, component and control mapping, current system description, risk and traceability updates, defect and incident trends, technical-debt register, supplier releases, cumulative-impact conclusion, and Quality decision. Acceptance requires threshold-based escalation and coherent current-state documentation.
Regulatory Alignment: EU GMP Annex 11 Sections 4.1, 4.3, 10, and 11; ICH Q9(R1) Sections 4.5 and 4.6.
Red Flags: No aggregation across releases; system description obsolete; same control repeatedly changed; technical debt unassessed; open defects accumulating; revalidation threshold undefined; current state cannot be reconstructed.

content:
GxP IT Audit Checklist [DA-12-025]: Demonstrate that change closure represents a complete validated-state decision supported by final implementation, test, deviation, configuration, documentation, training, backup, monitoring, and post-implementation evidence rather than administrative task completion.
Phase: 12 Change Config Mgmt | Domain: Change Closure & Governance | Topic: Evidence-based closure | Priority: Critical
Follow-Up Probe: Select a closed change associated with a subsequent incident or corrective data action and explain whether closure criteria should have detected the latent issue; show how the closure process and related population were reassessed.
Expected Evidence / Criteria: Closure checklist with source links, implemented scope, final test and deviations, production baseline, updated documents and training, backup or recovery impact, monitoring, post-implementation review, residual risks, and authorized approvals. Acceptance requires all mandatory evidence complete, exceptions explicit, and continued validated state justified.

Red Flags: Closure before production verification; open deviation omitted; baseline or SOP not updated; approvals predate evidence; later incident reveals missed effect; attachments inaccessible; residual risk not accepted; checklist copied.

content:
GxP IT Audit Checklist [DA-13-001]: Construct the complete population of potential system and data events from monitoring, service desk, quality, audit-trail exceptions, security, supplier, user complaints, and manual correction sources and reconcile it to formally logged incidents and deviations.
Phase: 13 Incident Problem Dev | Domain: Incident Governance | Topic: Complete event population | Priority: Critical
Follow-Up Probe: Explain every alert, data correction, failed job, user workaround, or supplier case that was not logged as an incident or assessed for GxP impact, including who made that exclusion decision and on what evidence.
Expected Evidence / Criteria: Incident and deviation procedures, source-system populations, inclusion and exclusion rules, reconciliation, reclassification records, and Quality oversight. Acceptance requires complete source coverage, traceable classification, investigation of unmatched events, and linkage of all potential GxP events to an impact decision.
Regulatory Alignment: EU GMP Annex 11 Sections 11 and 13; ICH Q9(R1) Sections 3 and 4; PIC/S PI 041-1 Sections 6 and 9.
Red Flags: Incident population comes only from ITSM; data corrections excluded; unmatched alerts ignored; supplier tickets invisible; user complaints not assessed; repeated low-severity events fragmented; no Quality challenge of classifications.

document_title: Top 25 Checklists GxP IT Audit Questions 2026
content:
GxP IT Audit Checklist [DA-13-002]: Reperform the initial classification of the most consequential recent event using the system's intended use, critical data, process stage, affected records, control failures, and potential product or patient consequences.
Phase: 13 Incident Problem Dev | Domain: Incident Classification | Topic: GxP impact and escalation | Priority: Critical
Follow-Up Probe: Remove the assumption that the final value or batch result was acceptable and explain what evidence independently bounds the event's impact population and justifies the chosen severity and Quality escalation.
Expected Evidence / Criteria: Classification matrix, intended-use and risk records, event facts, affected functions and data, initial and revised classifications, escalation timestamps, Quality assessment, and rationale. Acceptance requires conservative classification under uncertainty, timely escalation, and revision as evidence develops.
Regulatory Alignment: EU GMP Annex 11 Section 13; ICH Q9(R1) Sections 4.2 and 4.3; 21 CFR 211.192 for unexplained discrepancies affecting drug batches where applicable.
Red Flags: Classification based on outage duration alone; final acceptable result used to dismiss potential impact; Quality notified late; uncertainty not considered; affected population guessed; severity downgraded before evidence.

metadata.reference: EU GMP Annex 11 Section 13; ICH Q9(R1) Sections 4.2 and 4.3; 21 CFR 211.192 for unexplained discrepancies affecting drug batches where applicable.

content:
GxP IT Audit Checklist [DA-13-003]: Reconstruct the interval from first abnormal condition to detection, acknowledgement, technical response, business notification, and Quality escalation using native timestamps and explain every period in which the event remained active or unassessed.
Phase: 13 Incident Problem Dev | Domain: Incident Detection & Response | Topic: Detection and notification timeliness | Priority: Critical
Follow-Up Probe: Identify the earliest evidence that existed before the official start time and show why monitoring, a user, or a supplier did not recognize it; quantify records and decisions created during the undetected interval.
Expected Evidence / Criteria: Native system and monitoring logs, alert routing, acknowledgement, ITSM timeline, communication, escalation criteria, Quality notification, and affected-transaction analysis. Acceptance requires an evidence-based start time, justified response intervals, and impact assessment covering the full exposure window.
Regulatory Alignment: EU GMP Annex 11 Section 13; ICH Q9(R1) Sections 4.3 and 4.4; NIST SP 800-61 Rev. 3 as nonbinding incident-response guidance.
Red Flags: Official start equals ticket time despite earlier evidence; alert unacknowledged; after-hours gap; Quality escalation delayed; exposure window not used for sampling; SLA met only by redefining start time.

content:
GxP IT Audit Checklist [DA-13-004]: Demonstrate how the incident was contained without destroying or altering the records, logs, volatile evidence, configurations, and transaction context needed to establish GxP impact and root cause.
Phase: 13 Incident Problem Dev | Domain: Incident Response | Topic: Containment and evidence preservation | Priority: Critical
Follow-Up Probe: Show each restart, rollback, log rotation, cache clear, file deletion, account disablement, or configuration change performed during response and prove that evidence was captured first or the loss was explicitly assessed.
Expected Evidence / Criteria: Containment decision record, forensic or evidence-preservation procedure, native logs and snapshots, chain of custody where appropriate, responder actions, emergency changes, backup copies, and Quality oversight. Acceptance requires preserved originals, attributable actions, controlled access, and documented limitations where evidence was lost.
Regulatory Alignment: EU GMP Annex 11 Sections 7, 9, 10, 12, and 13; 21 CFR 11.10(c) and 11.10(e); NIST SP 800-61 Rev. 3 as nonbinding guidance.
Red Flags: System wiped or restarted before capture; logs overwritten; response actions use shared account; no original evidence; chain of custody unclear; emergency changes undocumented; evidence gap dismissed without impact assessment.

metadata.reference: EU GMP Annex 11 Sections 7, 9, 10, 12, and 13; 21 CFR 11.10(c) and 11.10(e); NIST SP 800-61 Rev. 3 as nonbinding guidance.

document_title: Top 25 Checklists GxP IT Audit Questions 2026
content:
GxP IT Audit Checklist [DA-13-005]: Starting from the full exposure window and affected functions, identify every GxP record and downstream decision potentially affected and demonstrate how completeness, accuracy, attribution, chronology, and use were verified.
Phase: 13 Incident Problem Dev | Domain: Data Integrity | Topic: Record and product impact assessment | Priority: Critical
Follow-Up Probe: Show the query or reconstruction logic that defines the affected population, then challenge it with records created immediately before and after the window, queued or cached transactions, replicas, reports, exports, and manual workarounds.
Expected Evidence / Criteria: Exposure-window rationale, function and data-flow analysis, reproducible population query, record list, downstream-use mapping, field and metadata checks, batch or quality impact, Quality disposition, and independent review. Acceptance requires complete bounded population, documented exclusions, and action for all affected released or in-process records.
Regulatory Alignment: EU GMP Annex 11 Sections 5, 7, 9, and 13; FDA Data Integrity and Compliance With Drug CGMP Q&A; PIC/S PI 041-1; 21 CFR 211.192 where applicable.
Red Flags: Population derived from ticket estimate; queued or downstream data omitted; boundary not tested; released records not assessed; final values checked without metadata or history; query not reproducible; Quality disposition absent.

document_title: Top 25 Checklists GxP IT Audit Questions 2026
content:
GxP IT Audit Checklist [DA-13-006]: For an audit-trail gap or anomalous event, reconstruct the underlying user, record, configuration, system, and database activity and demonstrate whether any GxP action occurred outside the visible audit history.
Phase: 13 Incident Problem Dev | Domain: Audit Trail | Topic: Audit-trail anomaly investigation | Priority: Critical
Follow-Up Probe: Use independent logs to challenge the period in which the application audit trail is blank, filtered, delayed, or inconsistent and explain all user and administrator activity, including failed or rolled-back transactions.
Expected Evidence / Criteria: Audit-trail configuration, gap or anomaly alert, raw audit events, database and platform logs, user activity, record versions, clock status, investigation, affected population, and CAPA. Acceptance requires independent reconstruction, documented completeness limitations, and Quality assessment of potential data alteration or concealment.
Regulatory Alignment: EU GMP Annex 11 Sections 9, 12.4, and 13; 21 CFR 11.10(e); FDA Data Integrity Q&A; PIC/S PI 041-1.
Red Flags: Gap accepted as no activity; independent logs unavailable; administrator actions excluded; filtered report substituted for raw events; unexplained clock gap; no retrospective record review; recurrence not controlled.

document_title: Top 25 Checklists GxP IT Audit Questions 2026
content:
GxP IT Audit Checklist [DA-13-007]: For a security incident or credible compromise, demonstrate how confidentiality, integrity, availability, authenticity, validated configuration, and regulated-record impact were assessed beyond the cybersecurity containment decision.
Phase: 13 Incident Problem Dev | Domain: Cybersecurity Incident Management | Topic: GxP impact of security compromise | Priority: Critical
Follow-Up Probe: Assume the attacker obtained the highest observed privilege and show what records or controls could have been changed without an application audit event, how such activity was searched, and what evidence bounds dwell time.
Expected Evidence / Criteria: Security timeline, identities and assets affected, privilege and attack-path analysis, native and centralized logs, configuration and file-integrity checks, record and audit-trail review, data exfiltration assessment, GxP impact, recovery, and Quality approval. Acceptance requires evidence-based scope and controlled residual uncertainty.
Regulatory Alignment: EU GMP Annex 11 Sections 7, 9, 12, and 13; NIST SP 800-61 Rev. 3 and NIST Cybersecurity Framework 2.0 as nonbinding guidance; 21 CFR 11.10(c) to 11.10(g) where applicable.
Red Flags: Security closure lacks Quality review; integrity impact assumed absent; dwell time unknown; privileged activity not reconstructed; only malware scan used; configuration or record comparison absent; uncertainty not risk-controlled.

metadata.expected_evidence: Security timeline, identities and assets affected, privilege and attack-path analysis, native and centralized logs, configuration and file-integrity checks, record and audit-trail review, data exfiltration assessment, GxP impact, recovery, and Quality approval. content:
GxP IT Audit Checklist [DA-13-008]: Trace the incident's affected transactions from source through transport, middleware, target, downstream processing, reconciliation, and any replay to prove that no record was silently lost, duplicated, reordered, truncated, or transformed.
Phase: 13 Incident Problem Dev | Domain: Interfaces & Integrations | Topic: Failed or duplicate transfer investigation | Priority: Critical
Follow-Up Probe: Select one transaction that was retried or manually reprocessed and show how uniqueness, original attribution, chronology, audit history, and downstream decision integrity were preserved.
Expected Evidence / Criteria: Correlation identifiers, source and target populations, message and queue logs, error and retry configuration, reconciliation, replay authorization, record and audit-trail checks, downstream impact, and deviation. Acceptance requires complete end-to-end accounting and controlled resolution of every exception.
Regulatory Alignment: EU GMP Annex 11 Sections 5, 7, 9, and 13; 21 CFR 11.10(a), 11.10(e), 11.10(f), and 11.10(h).
Red Flags: Service restored without transaction reconciliation; retry logic undocumented; duplicate or replay possible; manual reprocessing outside audit trail; rejected queue omitted; downstream reports not reassessed.

content:
GxP IT Audit Checklist [DA-13-009]: For the most significant backup or restore failure, demonstrate the exact data and configuration exposure, earliest unrecoverable point, detection method, compensating protection, recovery path, and verified integrity of the restored state.
Phase: 13 Incident Problem Dev | Domain: Backup & Recovery Incident | Topic: Failed backup or restore investigation | Priority: Critical
Follow-Up Probe: Challenge the assumption that a second copy was usable by tracing its completeness, encryption keys, retention, corruption checks, restore execution, audit trails, interfaces, and business acceptance.
Expected Evidence / Criteria: Backup population and topology, failure and alert logs, RPO calculation, copy independence, restore records, data and configuration reconciliation, key availability, business and Quality acceptance, root cause, CAPA, and retest. Acceptance requires bounded data exposure and objectively verified recovery.
Regulatory Alignment: EU GMP Annex 11 Sections 7.2, 13, and 16; 21 CFR 211.68(b); NIST SP 800-53 Rev. 5 CP-9 and CP-10 as nonbinding guidance.
Red Flags: Exposure window unknown; redundant copies share failure; successful status accepted without restore; keys unavailable; restored data not reconciled; RPO missed without Quality assessment; CAPA retest excludes failure mode.

document_title: Top 25 Checklists GxP IT Audit Questions 2026
content:
GxP IT Audit Checklist [DA-13-010]: Reconstruct how continuity arrangements were activated, operated, and exited during the outage and show that manual or alternate records, decisions, backlog, and later system reconciliation remained controlled.
Phase: 13 Incident Problem Dev | Domain: Business Continuity | Topic: Continuity activation and resumption | Priority: Critical
Follow-Up Probe: Select the longest or most chaotic shift and trace one record from manual creation through approval, custody, system entry, duplicate check, audit trail, reconciliation, and archival; explain any missing or overwritten step.
Expected Evidence / Criteria: Activation criteria and timeline, controlled forms or alternate system, role and communication records, manual record population, backlog controls, reconciliation, deviations, business and Quality acceptance, and lessons learned. Acceptance requires complete ALCOA+ records and verified transition back to normal operation.
Regulatory Alignment: EU GMP Annex 11 Sections 13 and 16; PIC/S PI 041-1 data-lifecycle and hybrid-record principles; ICH Q9(R1) Section 4.
Red Flags: Continuity activated late; uncontrolled forms or spreadsheets; records missing by shift; backlog unbounded; duplicate or transcription checks absent; normal operation resumed before reconciliation; Quality not involved.

Acceptance requires complete ALCOA+ records and verified transition ba
metadata.reference: EU GMP Annex 11 Sections 13 and 16; PIC/S PI 041-1 data-lifecycle and hybrid-record principles; ICH Q9(R1) Section 4.

document_title: Top 25 Checklists GxP IT Audit Questions 2026
content:
GxP IT Audit Checklist [DA-13-011]: For the latest material supplier or cloud incident, demonstrate how contractual notification, joint triage, evidence access, GxP impact, root cause, subprocessor involvement, corrective action, and service restoration were independently overseen by the regulated company.
Phase: 13 Incident Problem Dev | Domain: Supplier & Cloud Incident | Topic: Third-party incident accountability | Priority: Critical
Follow-Up Probe: Compare the supplier's final report with your own telemetry and affected-record analysis, identify inconsistencies or missing evidence, and show how your organization challenged conclusions rather than accepting provider closure.
Expected Evidence / Criteria: Quality or service agreement, notification timestamps, joint timeline, provider and customer logs, shared-responsibility matrix, impact assessment, supplier root cause and CAPA, internal challenge, SLA remedies, subprocessor evidence, and Quality closure. Acceptance requires timely access, reconciled facts, and effective actions under retained user accountability.
Regulatory Alignment: EU GMP Annex 11 Sections 3, 7, 12, 13, and 16; NIST SP 800-61 Rev. 3 as nonbinding incident-response guidance.
Red Flags: Supplier notified late; evidence withheld; internal assessment relies only on provider summary; subprocessor unknown; tenant data not reconciled; CAPA acceptance unchallenged; contract lacks incident or inspection evidence obligations.

Acceptance requires timely access, reconcile

document_title: Top 25 Checklists GxP IT Audit Questions 2026
content:
GxP IT Audit Checklist [DA-13-012]: Demonstrate how the investigation distinguished root cause, contributing causes, detection-control failure, and organizational or process conditions using evidence that can reproduce and explain the observed event.
Phase: 13 Incident Problem Dev | Domain: Problem Management | Topic: Evidence-based root cause | Priority: Critical
Follow-Up Probe: Present the strongest competing causal hypothesis, show the discriminating evidence used to reject it, and explain which facts remain uncertain and how that uncertainty changes corrective action or monitoring.
Expected Evidence / Criteria: Problem statement, complete timeline, evidence catalogue, technical and process analysis, hypotheses, experiments or reproduction, causal chain, contributing factors, detection failure, uncertainty, cross-functional review, and approved conclusion. Acceptance requires evidence sufficient to explain occurrence and recurrence and actions addressing the causal mechanism.
Regulatory Alignment: EU GMP Annex 11 Section 13; ICH Q9(R1) Sections 4.2, 4.3, and 5; PIC/S PI 041-1 Sections 6 and 9.
Red Flags: Root cause is 'human error,' 'software glitch,' or 'network issue' without causal evidence; competing hypotheses absent; event not reproducible or bounded; detection failure ignored; uncertainty concealed; supplier statement accepted verbatim.

metadata.expected_evidence: Problem statement, complete timeline, evidence catalogue, technical and process analysis, hypotheses, experiments or reproduction, causal chain, contributing factors, detection failure, uncertainty, cross-functional review, and approved conclusion. Acceptance requires evidence sufficient to explain

document_title: Top 25 Checklists GxP IT Audit Questions 2026
content:
GxP IT Audit Checklist [DA-13-013]: Show how the investigation searched for recurrence and analogous failure across alternate error codes, ticket categories, sites, versions, interfaces, manual corrections, supplier services, and near misses.
Phase: 13 Incident Problem Dev | Domain: Problem Management | Topic: Recurrence and similar-event search | Priority: High
Follow-Up Probe: Rerun the search using broader technical and business synonyms and compare the newly found population with the one used to conclude that the event was isolated.
Expected Evidence / Criteria: Documented search strategy, systems and time window, query terms and logic, results, clustering method, applicability decisions, historical impact review, and CAPA scope. Acceptance requires reproducible, sufficiently broad search and escalation when similar events are identified.
Regulatory Alignment: EU GMP Annex 11 Sections 11 and 13; ICH Q9(R1) Sections 4.3 and 4.6; PIC/S PI 041-1 Sections 6 and 9.
Red Flags: Search limited to exact error code or same system; query not retained; low-severity and supplier cases excluded; similar events relabelled; historical product or data impact not revisited; systemic pattern declared isolated.

metadata.expected_evidence: Documented search strategy, systems and time window, query terms and logic, results, clustering method, applicability decisions, historical impact review, and CAPA scope. Acceptance requires reproducible, sufficiently broad search and escalation when similar events are identified.
metadata.reference: EU GMP Annex 11 Sections 11 and 13; ICH Q9(R1) Sections 4.3 and 4.6; PIC/S PI 041-1 Sections 6 and 9.

document_title: Top 25 Checklists GxP IT Audit Questions 2026
content:
GxP IT Audit Checklist [DA-13-014]: For an event attributed to human error, demonstrate how system design, workload, procedure clarity, training effectiveness, access, interface usability, supervision, incentives, and error-detection controls were evaluated as causal or contributing conditions.
Phase: 13 Incident Problem Dev | Domain: Human Factors & Quality Culture | Topic: Human-error causal challenge | Priority: High
Follow-Up Probe: Place a competent person unfamiliar with the event in the same controlled scenario and show whether the process and system reliably lead to the correct action without relying on memory or informal knowledge.
Expected Evidence / Criteria: Task analysis, procedure and training content, competence, workload and environment, access and UI controls, system checks, supervision, interviews, recurrence data, and redesigned controls. Acceptance requires systemic assessment and CAPA beyond retraining where the process permits predictable error.
Regulatory Alignment: EU GMP Annex 11 Sections 1, 2, 6, 12, and 13; 21 CFR 11.10(f), 11.10(g), and 11.10(i); PIC/S PI 041-1 Section 6.
Red Flags: Root cause ends at operator mistake; CAPA is retraining only; procedure ambiguous; system permits invalid sequence; workload or incentives ignored; same error recurs; punitive response discourages reporting. Finding trigger: evidence is missing, unapproved, incomplete, inconsistent, or cannot be reproduced for the auditor-selected sample.

metadata.expected_evidence: Task analysis, procedure and training content, competence, workload and environment, access and UI controls, system checks, supervision, interviews, recurrence data, and redesigned controls. Acceptance requires systemic assessment and CAPA beyond retraining where the process permits predictable erro

document_title: Top 25 Checklists GxP IT Audit Questions 2026
content:
GxP IT Audit Checklist [DA-13-015]: Trace the incident backward through all changes and releases within the credible causal window and demonstrate how the implemented state differed from the tested and approved state.
Phase: 13 Incident Problem Dev | Domain: Change Management | Topic: Change-induced incident trace | Priority: Critical
Follow-Up Probe: Include individually low-risk, emergency, infrastructure, feature-flag, supplier, and direct configuration changes, then explain why any temporal or technical correlation was excluded as a cause.
Expected Evidence / Criteria: Causal-window rationale, complete deployment and configuration population, pre/post baselines, repository and supplier history, test evidence, incident timeline, correlation analysis, and change-process CAPA. Acceptance requires reconciliation to production sources and reassessment of affected change controls.
Regulatory Alignment: EU GMP Annex 11 Sections 4.2, 10, 11, and 13; 21 CFR 11.10(k); 21 CFR 211.68(b).
Red Flags: Change search limited to application tickets; feature flags or supplier releases omitted; approved and live baselines differ; correlation dismissed without analysis; testing gap not fed back to change process.

metadata.expected_evidence: Causal-window rationale, complete deployment and configuration population, pre/post baselines, repository and supplier history, test evidence, incident timeline, correlation analysis, and change-process CAPA. Acceptance requires reconciliation to production sources and reassessment of affected chang

document_title: Top 25 Checklists GxP IT Audit Questions 2026
content:
GxP IT Audit Checklist [DA-13-016]: Establish a defensible common timeline across application, database, operating system, identity, interface, cloud, monitoring, supplier, and quality records, accounting for time zones, daylight-saving changes, clock drift, latency, and log buffering.
Phase: 13 Incident Problem Dev | Domain: Forensic Traceability | Topic: Timestamp and log correlation | Priority: High
Follow-Up Probe: Select two events whose apparent order changes after normalization and show which chronology is authoritative, how uncertainty was bounded, and whether the revised sequence changes root cause or affected population.
Expected Evidence / Criteria: Time-source architecture, synchronization and drift monitoring, time-zone and daylight-saving rules, raw logs with source metadata, normalization method, latency estimates, common timeline, and uncertainty. Acceptance requires reproducible conversion and causal conclusions robust to known timing error.
Regulatory Alignment: EU GMP Annex 11 Sections 9, 12.4, and 13; 21 CFR 11.10(e); MHRA GxP Data Integrity Guidance Section 5.1 as nonbinding guidance.
Red Flags: Timeline mixes local and UTC without conversion; clock drift unknown; screenshots replace raw logs; buffered events treated as occurrence time; event order uncertain but stated as fact; no impact on causal conclusion assessed.

metadata.expected_evidence: Time-source architecture, synchronization and drift monitoring, time-zone and daylight-saving rules, raw logs with source metadata, normalization method, latency estimates, common timeline, and uncertainty. Acceptance requires reproducible conversion and causal conclusions robust to known timing err

document_title: Top 25 Checklists GxP IT Audit Questions 2026
content:
GxP IT Audit Checklist [DA-13-017]: Demonstrate that each interim workaround or compensating control is specific to the identified failure mode, effective for the full affected population, sustainable across shifts and sites, monitored, and time-bound until permanent correction.
Phase: 13 Incident Problem Dev | Domain: Interim Risk Control | Topic: Workaround and compensating-control effectiveness | Priority: Critical
Follow-Up Probe: Observe or simulate the workaround under peak workload and staff absence, then show how missed execution, transcription error, duplicate processing, or workaround drift is independently detected.
Expected Evidence / Criteria: Interim-control design, risk assessment, instructions, training, staffing and capacity, control execution records, independent verification, monitoring, deviations, expiry and escalation, and permanent-fix plan. Acceptance requires verified effectiveness and no uncontrolled extension.
Regulatory Alignment: EU GMP Annex 11 Sections 1, 13, and 16; ICH Q9(R1) Sections 4.4 to 4.6; PIC/S PI 041-1 Sections 6 and 9.
Red Flags: Workaround relies on memory; no capacity analysis; execution records incomplete; extension automatic; missed steps not detected; control owner conflicted; permanent fix repeatedly deferred; workaround changes GxP data outside audit trail.

metadata.expected_evidence: Interim-control design, risk assessment, instructions, training, staffing and capacity, control execution records, independent verification, monitoring, deviations, expiry and escalation, and permanent-fix plan. Acceptance requires verified effectiveness and no uncontrolled extension.

content:
GxP IT Audit Checklist [DA-13-018]: Trace one corrected or recovered record from original state through authorization, preserved source evidence, correction or replay method, independent verification, audit trail, downstream reconciliation, and final quality disposition.
Phase: 13 Incident Problem Dev | Domain: Data Correction & Recovery | Topic: Controlled repair of affected records | Priority: Critical
Follow-Up Probe: Demonstrate how the process prevents selective correction, overwriting of the original, duplicate downstream use, and correction by a person who performed or benefits from the original action.
Expected Evidence / Criteria: Affected-record population, approved correction protocol, preserved originals, authorized tools and identities, before and after values, reasons, audit trails, validation or verification of scripts, independent checks, downstream reconciliation, and Quality approval. Acceptance requires complete traceability and no loss of original evidence.
Regulatory Alignment: EU GMP Annex 11 Sections 5, 6, 7, 9, and 13; 21 CFR 11.10(a) and 11.10(e); FDA Data Integrity Q&A; PIC/S PI 041-1.
Red Flags: Original overwritten; correction script untested; bulk population not reconciled; selective records repaired; conflicted person approves; audit trail reason missing; downstream reports or decisions not refreshed; backup copy treated as original without verification.

metadata.reference: EU GMP Annex 11 Sections 5, 6, 7, 9, and 13; 21 CFR 11.10(a) and 11.10(e); FDA Data Integrity Q&A; PIC/S PI 041-1.

content:
GxP IT Audit Checklist [DA-13-019]: Demonstrate bidirectional linkage among the technical incident, quality deviation, affected records or batches, investigation, changes, CAPA, and disposition so that no part of the evidence or decision can be closed independently.
Phase: 13 Incident Problem Dev | Domain: Quality Event Integration | Topic: Incident-deviation-batch linkage | Priority: Critical
Follow-Up Probe: Select one linked item closed earlier than another and explain how new facts propagated to all dependent decisions, including any released batch, approved record, or previously accepted residual risk.
Expected Evidence / Criteria: Cross-system linkage procedure and identifiers, synchronized scope and timelines, affected batch or record list, shared evidence, change and CAPA references, decision updates, closure dependencies, and Quality oversight. Acceptance requires consistent facts and controlled propagation of material updates.
Regulatory Alignment: EU GMP Annex 11 Sections 4.2 and 13; 21 CFR 211.192 where applicable; ICH Q9(R1) Section 4.6.
Red Flags: IT and Quality scopes differ; no common identifier; one record closes while material actions remain open; batch or record list inconsistent; new root-cause evidence not propagated; supplier ticket absent from deviation.

content:
GxP IT Audit Checklist [DA-13-020]: Map each confirmed root and contributing cause, detection failure, and scope weakness to a corrective or preventive action and demonstrate that the action changes the causal mechanism rather than only documenting or retraining around it.
Phase: 13 Incident Problem Dev | Domain: CAPA Management | Topic: Cause-to-action traceability | Priority: Critical
Follow-Up Probe: Remove the proposed training and procedure actions from the plan and show which technical, process, governance, or supplier control prevents recurrence; explain any causal factor left without an action.
Expected Evidence / Criteria: Approved causal analysis, cause-to-CAPA map, action design and owner, risk priority, interim controls, technical and process implementation, cross-system applicability, validation or change records, due dates, and Quality approval. Acceptance requires full causal coverage and proportionate preventive action.
Regulatory Alignment: EU GMP Annex 11 Section 13; ICH Q9(R1) Sections 4.4 to 4.6; PIC/S PI 041-1 Sections 6 and 9.
Red Flags: CAPA consists only of retraining or SOP revision; root cause has no corresponding action; detection failure ignored; supplier cause not governed; applicability limited without rationale; due dates repeatedly extended.

content:
GxP IT Audit Checklist [DA-13-021]: Demonstrate that CAPA effectiveness was measured over a population and period capable of revealing recurrence, and that both the corrected control and the detection control operated successfully under representative and adverse conditions.
Phase: 13 Incident Problem Dev | Domain: CAPA Effectiveness | Topic: Sustained effectiveness verification | Priority: High
Follow-Up Probe: Rerun the documented effectiveness query against current incident, deviation, monitoring, audit-trail exception, change, and supplier data and explain any near miss, workaround, or differently classified recurrence.
Expected Evidence / Criteria: Predefined effectiveness criteria, baseline, population, observation period, source query, adverse-condition or control test, results, independent review, recurrence assessment, and response to failure. Acceptance requires cause-specific measures, sufficient opportunity for recurrence, and reopening or escalation when criteria are unmet.
Regulatory Alignment: EU GMP Annex 11 Sections 11 and 13; ICH Q9(R1) Section 4.6; PIC/S PI 041-1 Sections 6 and 9.
Red Flags: Effectiveness equals completion; observation period too short; query exact-match only; near misses excluded; source data incomplete; check performed by action owner without independent review; failed result not reopened.

Phase: 13 Incident Problem Dev | Domain: Regulatory & Privacy Notification | Topic: External notification decision | Priority: Critical
Follow-Up Probe: Show the earliest point at which the organization had sufficient awareness to start any notification period and explain delays caused by classification uncertainty, supplier dependence, or incomplete affected-person or product scope.

GxP IT Audit Checklist [DA-13-024]: Demonstrate that closure reflects resolved containment, bounded impact, supported root cause, implemented or governed CAPA, reconciled records, restored validated state, and explicitly accepted residual risk.

metadata.reference: EU GMP Annex 11 Sections 11 and 13; ICH Q9(R1) Sections 4.4 to 4.6; 21 CFR 211.192 where applicable.

GxP IT Audit Checklist [DA-13-025]: Show how management review combines incidents, deviations, near misses, audit-trail exceptions, security events, recovery failures, user workarounds, supplier issues, changes, and CAPA effectiveness to identify systemic control weaknesses and preventive priorities.

Follow-Up Probe: Present a trend that management initially considered acceptable and explain the threshold, dissenting evidence, business pressure, and subsequent outcome; show what would now trigger escalation earlier.

GxP IT Audit Checklist [DA-14-001]: Reconstruct the approved retirement decision and demonstrate how business, Quality, records, security, privacy, legal, supplier, continuity, and technical owners agreed the system boundary, timing, successor capability, retained obligations, and exit criteria.
Phase: 14 Decommission Retention | Domain: Decommissioning Governance | Topic: Retirement decision and scope | Priority: Critical

Expected Evidence / Criteria: Approved retirement business case, GxP and regulatory assessment, scope and dependency analysis, accountable owners, successor and archive decisions, risk assessment, legal and retention review, exit criteria, timeline, and Quality approval. Red Flags: Retirement approved by project or IT alone; scope differs from live inventory; open deviations, legal holds, or regulated uses omitted; exit criteria vague; irreversible shutdown scheduled before evidence completion; Quality approval absent.

content:
GxP IT Audit Checklist [DA-14-005]: Trace archive requirements for accessibility, readability, integrity, authenticity, security, metadata, audit trails, signatures, search, copies, retention, and destruction into the approved archive design and operating controls.
Phase: 14 Decommission Retention | Domain: Archiving | Topic: Archive requirements and design | Priority: Critical
Follow-Up Probe: Demonstrate how the archive remains usable if the original application, database, vendor, license server, identity provider, encryption algorithm, or viewer no longer exists.
Expected Evidence / Criteria: Archive URS or requirements, risk assessment, data and metadata model, format and viewer strategy, security and access design, integrity checks, search and copy capability, retention and legal-hold controls, backup and recovery, technology-refresh plan, and approvals. Acceptance requires long-term usability independent of unsupported production components.
Regulatory Alignment: EU GMP Annex 11 Sections 7, 8, 9, 14, and 17; 21 CFR 11.10(b) and 11.10(c) where Part 11 applies.
Red Flags: Archive is only file storage; proprietary viewer dependency unaddressed; audit trails or signatures excluded; no integrity monitoring; original identity context lost; retention and deletion manual; archive recovery absent.

document_title: Top 25 Checklists GxP IT Audit Questions 2026
content:
GxP IT Audit Checklist [DA-14-006]: Demonstrate how migration scope, sequencing, freeze periods, coexistence, transformation, reconciliation, exception handling, rollback, source preservation, and final cutover were derived from data and process risk.
Phase: 14 Decommission Retention | Domain: Data Migration | Topic: Migration strategy and risk | Priority: Critical
Follow-Up Probe: Assume the source must be shut down after a partially successful migration and explain how rejected records, late transactions, interfaces, manual workarounds, and rollback or forward recovery remain controlled without creating two conflicting systems of record.
Expected Evidence / Criteria: Approved migration plan and risk assessment, source and target scopes, freeze and cutover design, data ownership, transformation rules, validation strategy, reconciliation, reject handling, rollback or forward-fix plan, source preservation, responsibilities, and Quality approval. Acceptance requires one authoritative record at each point and controlled exception paths.
Regulatory Alignment: EU GMP Annex 11 Sections 4.8, 5, 7, 9, 10, and 17; 21 CFR 11.10(a) to 11.10(c) and 11.10(e) where Part 11 applies; ICH Q9(R1) Section 4.
Red Flags: No authoritative-system rule during coexistence; late transactions omitted; rejects handled informally; rollback ignores new records; source altered or destroyed before acceptance; migration risk generic; Quality not involved.

document_title: Top 25 Checklists GxP IT Audit Questions 2026
content:
GxP IT Audit Checklist [DA-14-007]: Trace every transformation of critical data and metadata from source representation to target and demonstrate that value, precision, units, code meaning, relationships, null semantics, status, chronology, and attribution remain unchanged or are explicitly approved.
Phase: 14 Decommission Retention | Domain: Data Migration | Topic: Mapping and preservation of meaning | Priority: Critical
Follow-Up Probe: Select one defaulted, concatenated, split, rounded, truncated, recoded, unmapped, or deprecated value and show how its original meaning and downstream use can still be reconstructed.
Expected Evidence / Criteria: Source and target dictionaries, approved mapping, transformation specifications, code and unit crosswalks, precision rules, relationship handling, scripts under control, test evidence, exceptions, and business or Quality sign-off. Acceptance requires no unapproved change of value or meaning and retained provenance for approved transformations.
Regulatory Alignment: EU GMP Annex 11 Section 4.8; 21 CFR 11.10(a) and 11.10(b); PIC/S PI 041-1 data-lifecycle principles.
Red Flags: Mapping inferred from code; unit or precision changes undocumented; nulls converted to zero; obsolete codes dropped; relationship broken; transformation script differs from approved version; downstream report not reconciled.

metadata.reference: EU GMP Annex 11 Section 4.8; 21 CFR 11.10(a) and 11.10(b); PIC/S PI 041-1 data-lifecycle principles.

document_title: Top 25 Checklists GxP IT Audit Questions 2026
content:
GxP IT Audit Checklist [DA-14-008]: Reconcile the full source population to extracted, transformed, loaded, rejected, quarantined, duplicated, and excluded populations using immutable cut-off criteria and independent control totals.
Phase: 14 Decommission Retention | Domain: Data Migration | Topic: Population and control-total reconciliation | Priority: Critical
Follow-Up Probe: Explain how matching total row counts could still hide missing child records, duplicated parents, changed amounts, null fields, attachment loss, or status shifts and show the additional checks that reveal each risk.
Expected Evidence / Criteria: Frozen source population, extraction logs, staged and target counts, field totals, relational counts, hash or checksum evidence where appropriate, reject and exclusion logs, duplicate checks, attachments and audit-trail totals, independent review, and approved reconciliation. Acceptance requires every source item accounted for exactly once or formally dispositioned.
Regulatory Alignment: EU GMP Annex 11 Sections 4.8 and 7; 21 CFR 11.10(a) to 11.10(c); FDA Data Integrity Q&A.
Red Flags: Only row count used; source not frozen; excludes and rejects netted out; child or attachment counts absent; duplicate detection weak; reconciliation prepared by migration developer only; unexplained variance accepted.

metadata.reference: EU GMP Annex 11 Sections 4.8 and 7; 21 CFR 11.10(a) to 11.10(c); FDA Data Integrity Q&A.

document_title: Top 25 Checklists GxP IT Audit Questions 2026
content:
GxP IT Audit Checklist [DA-14-009]: For an auditor-selected critical record, trace the complete source-to-target chain and prove preservation of content, context, metadata, audit trail, signatures, attachments, calculations, relationships, and inspection copies.
Phase: 14 Decommission Retention | Domain: Data Integrity | Topic: Critical record source-to-target trace | Priority: Critical
Follow-Up Probe: Select a corrected, signed, rejected, or reopened record with multiple versions and explain how the target distinguishes original, prior, current, and superseded states without flattening history.
Expected Evidence / Criteria: Source record and native history, extract and transformation trace, target record and versions, metadata, audit trail, signature links, attachments, related records, calculation or report output, and copy. Acceptance requires field-level equivalence or approved transformation with complete provenance.
Regulatory Alignment: EU GMP Annex 11 Sections 4.8, 7, 8, 9, 14, and 17; 21 CFR 11.10(a) to 11.10(c), 11.10(e), 11.50, and 11.70.
Red Flags: History flattened; only current value migrated; attachments or links missing; signatures displayed without version; calculations differ; target copy omits context; sample chosen by migration team only.

metadata.expected_evidence: Source record and native history, extract and transformation trace, target record and versions, metadata, audit trail, signature links, attachments, related records, calculation or report output, and copy. document_title: Top 25 Checklists GxP IT Audit Questions 2026
content:
GxP IT Audit Checklist [DA-14-010]: Demonstrate how every migration exception is uniquely identified, preserved, investigated, risk-assessed, corrected under control, independently verified, reprocessed once, and included in final reconciliation.
Phase: 14 Decommission Retention | Domain: Migration Exceptions | Topic: Rejected and quarantined records | Priority: Critical
Follow-Up Probe: Select the oldest or repeatedly failed exception and show why it did not reveal a broader mapping or source-quality problem; search the accepted population for the same causal pattern.
Expected Evidence / Criteria: Immutable exception log, original rejected payload, error and cause, affected-record and broader-scope assessment, controlled correction, approval, reprocessing logs, duplicate prevention, independent check, and final disposition. Acceptance requires zero unexplained exceptions at release and systemic action for recurring causes.
Regulatory Alignment: EU GMP Annex 11 Sections 4.2, 4.8, 7, 9, and 13; 21 CFR 11.10(a) and 11.10(e); ICH Q9(R1) Section 4.
Red Flags: Exception log mutable; original payload lost; manual fix unapproved; repeated errors treated individually; rejected records excluded from totals; reprocessing creates duplicates; open critical exceptions at shutdown.

Acceptance requires zero unexplained exceptions at release and system
metadata.reference: EU GMP Annex 11 Sections 4.2, 4.8, 7, 9, and 13; 21 CFR 11.10(a) and 11.10(e); ICH Q9(R1) Section 4.

document_title: Top 25 Checklists GxP IT Audit Questions 2026
content:
GxP IT Audit Checklist [DA-14-011]: Demonstrate that the migration or archive preserves every required audit event, prior value, new value, actor, timestamp, action, reason, record linkage, and review status in an intelligible and reviewable form.
Phase: 14 Decommission Retention | Domain: Audit Trail | Topic: Audit-trail preservation | Priority: Critical
Follow-Up Probe: Compare a raw source audit-trail export with the target or archive for events created by administrators, failed actions, deletions, configuration changes, and periods where user-facing reports normally filter events.
Expected Evidence / Criteria: Source audit schema and configuration, full event population, mapping, transformation rules, target or archive events, intelligible display and electronic copy, event and record linkage, review capability, reconciliation, and access control. Acceptance requires complete history and no loss of meaning or reviewability.
Regulatory Alignment: EU GMP Annex 11 Sections 9 and 17; 21 CFR 11.10(e); FDA Data Integrity Q&A; PIC/S PI 041-1.
Red Flags: Only audit-trail PDF retained; prior values or reasons omitted; admin or failed events filtered; record linkage broken; timestamps transformed without trace; audit events not searchable or reviewable; source destroyed before reconciliation.

metadata.expected_evidence: Source audit schema and configuration, full event population, mapping, transformation rules, target or archive events, intelligible display and electronic copy, event and record linkage, review capability, reconciliation, and access control. Acceptance requires complete history and no loss of meanin
metadata.reference: EU GMP Annex 11 Sections 9 and 17; 21 CFR 11.10(e); FDA Data Integrity Q&A; PIC/S PI 041-1.

document_title: Top 25 Checklists GxP IT Audit Questions 2026
content:
GxP IT Audit Checklist [DA-14-012]: Select a migrated or archived signed record and prove that signer identity, date and time, signature meaning, signed record version, and permanent linkage remain intact and cannot be reassigned or detached.
Phase: 14 Decommission Retention | Domain: Electronic Signatures | Topic: Signature linkage after migration | Priority: Critical
Follow-Up Probe: Show how signer identity is resolved after the user account, directory, or original application has been removed and how later corrections or format conversions avoid making the original signature appear to approve changed content.
Expected Evidence / Criteria: Source signed record and signature logs, identity reference, mapping, target or archive record version, manifestation, permanent linkage, correction behavior, copy output, and verification. Acceptance requires durable, unambiguous, non-transferable linkage independent of active user accounts.
Regulatory Alignment: EU GMP Annex 11 Sections 14 and 17; 21 CFR 11.50, 11.70, 11.100, and 11.200.
Red Flags: Signature preserved only as image or text; signer unresolved after account removal; version linkage lost; correction changes signed content without new signature; multiple signatures collapsed; export detaches signature. Finding trigger: evidence is missing, unapproved, incomplete, inconsistent, or cannot be reproduced for the auditor-selected sample.

metadata.expected_evidence: Source signed record and signature logs, identity reference, mapping, target or archive record version, manifestation, permanent linkage, correction behavior, copy output, and verification. Acceptance requires durable, unambiguous, non-transferable linkage independent of active user accounts.
metadata.reference: EU GMP Annex 11 Sections 14 and 17; 21 CFR 11.50, 11.70, 11.100, and 11.200.

document_title: Top 25 Checklists GxP IT Audit Questions 2026
content:
GxP IT Audit Checklist [DA-14-013]: Demonstrate preservation of time-zone and clock context, attachments, images, file properties, external references, annotations, units, display rules, and paper-electronic relationships required to interpret each retained record.
Phase: 14 Decommission Retention | Domain: Metadata & Hybrid Records | Topic: Time, attachments, and contextual integrity | Priority: High
Follow-Up Probe: Select a record crossing a daylight-saving change or site time zone and one whose attachment has the same filename as another record; show unambiguous chronology, association, integrity, and retrieval.
Expected Evidence / Criteria: Metadata inventory and mapping, time conversion rules, attachment identifiers and hashes where used, MIME and format handling, link and annotation mapping, hybrid-record index, test evidence, and reconciliation. Acceptance requires preserved association, meaning, chronology, and integrity.
Regulatory Alignment: EU GMP Annex 11 Sections 4.8, 7, 8, 9, and 17; 21 CFR 11.10(b), 11.10(c), and 11.10(e); MHRA GxP Data Integrity Guidance Section 5.1 as nonbinding guidance.
Red Flags: Timestamps normalized without original zone; attachments matched by filename only; links broken; unsupported files skipped; annotations omitted; paper-electronic index lost; duplicate files overwrite; hash or size not reconciled.

metadata.expected_evidence: Metadata inventory and mapping, time conversion rules, attachment identifiers and hashes where used, MIME and format handling, link and annotation mapping, hybrid-record index, test evidence, and reconciliation. Acceptance requires preserved association, meaning, chronology, and integrity.
metadata.reference: EU GMP Annex 11 Sections 4.8, 7, 8, 9, and 17; 21 CFR 11.10(b), 11.10(c), and 11.10(e); MHRA GxP Data Integrity Guidance Section 5.1 as nonbinding guidance.

document_title: Top 25 Checklists GxP IT Audit Questions 2026
content:
GxP IT Audit Checklist [DA-14-014]: Reconstruct the cutover and prove which system was authoritative for each process, site, record class, and time interval, including how late transactions, backlogs, manual records, and interface queues were controlled.
Phase: 14 Decommission Retention | Domain: Cutover & Coexistence | Topic: Authoritative-system transition | Priority: Critical
Follow-Up Probe: Select a record created near the cutover boundary and show how duplicate creation, update in the wrong system, clock difference, and delayed interface delivery were detected and reconciled.
Expected Evidence / Criteria: Cutover plan, freeze and authority matrix, synchronized timeline, user and interface controls, queue and backlog inventory, communication, boundary reconciliation, duplicate checks, deviations, and acceptance. Acceptance requires one unambiguous authoritative record for every interval and resolved transition exceptions.
Regulatory Alignment: EU GMP Annex 11 Sections 4.8, 5, 7, 9, 10, and 16; 21 CFR 11.10(a), 11.10(e), and 11.10(f).
Red Flags: Authority rule unclear; both systems writable; boundary times differ; late queue omitted; user access not aligned to freeze; duplicate records; manual backlog unreconciled; source changed after final extract.

metadata.expected_evidence: Cutover plan, freeze and authority matrix, synchronized timeline, user and interface controls, queue and backlog inventory, communication, boundary reconciliation, duplicate checks, deviations, and acceptance. Acceptance requires one unambiguous authoritative record for every interval and resolved t
metadata.reference: EU GMP Annex 11 Sections 4.8, 5, 7, 9, 10, and 16; 21 CFR 11.10(a), 11.10(e), and 11.10(f).

document_title: Top 25 Checklists GxP IT Audit Questions 2026
content:
GxP IT Audit Checklist [DA-14-015]: Trace archive or migration risks and requirements to test scenarios, raw evidence, deviations, reconciliation, acceptance, and release, including boundary, negative, failure, recovery, and long-term retrieval cases.
Phase: 14 Decommission Retention | Domain: Validation / Assurance | Topic: Archive and migration verification | Priority: Critical
Follow-Up Probe: Show the highest-risk requirement with reduced or no scripted testing and demonstrate why other objective evidence provides sufficient assurance; then present the last failed test and its full resolution chain.
Expected Evidence / Criteria: Validation or assurance plan, risk and requirement trace, test strategy, controlled tools and environments, positive and negative tests, raw execution evidence, deviations and defects, reconciliation, retrieval and recovery tests, summary, and Quality approval. Acceptance requires assurance commensurate with risk and no unexplained failed requirement.
Regulatory Alignment: EU GMP Annex 11 Sections 4.1, 4.2, 4.7, 4.8, and 17; 21 CFR 11.10(a) where Part 11 applies; ICH Q9(R1) Section 3.
Red Flags: Testing focused on counts only; long-term retrieval omitted; failed test overwritten; automated tool unassessed; deviations open at release; traceability mechanical; excluded requirements unsupported; source destroyed before approval. Finding trigger: evidence is missing, unapproved, incomplete, inconsistent, or cannot be reproduced for the auditor-selected sample.

metadata.reference: EU GMP Annex 11 Sections 4.1, 4.2, 4.7, 4.8, and 17; 21 CFR 11.10(a) where Part 11 applies; ICH Q9(R1) Section 3.

document_title: Top 25 Checklists GxP IT Audit Questions 2026
content:
GxP IT Audit Checklist [DA-14-016]: Retrieve an auditor-selected archived record without production-system access and demonstrate timely search, access, readability, integrity, intelligibility, audit history, signature linkage, and accurate human-readable and electronic copies.
Phase: 14 Decommission Retention | Domain: Archiving Operations | Topic: Retrieval, readability, and inspection copies | Priority: Critical
Follow-Up Probe: Repeat the retrieval for the oldest cohort and for a record created before a major format, viewer, operating-system, or archive-platform change; explain every manual or specialist step required.
Expected Evidence / Criteria: Archive search and retrieval procedure, access authorization, native or preserved representation, metadata and audit history, signature linkage, copies, integrity verification, retrieval SLA, platform-change tests, and exception handling. Acceptance requires reproducible timely retrieval with complete meaning and no dependence on the retired production environment.
Regulatory Alignment: EU GMP Annex 11 Sections 7.1, 8, 9, 14, and 17; 21 CFR 11.10(b) and 11.10(c).
Red Flags: Retrieval requires retired application; oldest records unreadable; metadata or audit trail absent; signatures unresolved; electronic copy proprietary or incomplete; manual reconstruction undocumented; SLA missed without action.
